ITQAN:v2p305#2/r18.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p305#2/r18.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p305#2/r18.anchor:
﴿ وابن السبيل ﴾ الضيف الذي ينزل بالمسلمين
1524 ﴿ إن ترك خيرا ﴾ مالا

SAMIN-DURR:2:180/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:180/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:180/r1.claim: كتب is passive; its omitted agent is God, understood from context and left out for brevity.
SAMIN-DURR:2:180/r1.anchor: مبني للمفعول وحذف الفاعل للعلم به - وهو الله تعالى - وللاختصار

SAMIN-DURR:2:180/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:180/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:180/r2.claim: One نائب الفاعل parse makes الوصية the subject; its feminine is metaphorical, and separation permits the masculine verb.
SAMIN-DURR:2:180/r2.anchor: كون القائم مقام الفاعل مؤنثا مجازيا، والثاني: الفصل بينه وبين مرفوعه

SAMIN-DURR:2:180/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:180/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:180/r3.claim: Another نائب الفاعل parse takes الوصية to imply الإيصاء, the verbal noun understood as what was prescribed.
SAMIN-DURR:2:180/r3.anchor: أنه الإيصاء المدلول عليه بقوله: { الوصية للوالدين } أي: كتب هو أي: الإيصاء

SAMIN-DURR:2:180/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:180/r4.speaker: الأخفش والكوفيون
SAMIN-DURR:2:180/r4.claim: Al-Akhfash and the Kufans allow the prepositional phrase as نائب الفاعل: عليكم is nominative on this parse and accusative on the other two.
SAMIN-DURR:2:180/r4.anchor: أنه الجار والمجرور، وهذا يتجه على رأي الأخفش والكوفيين

SAMIN-DURR:2:180/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:180/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:180/r5.claim: The author makes كتب govern إذا as a purely temporal adverb, not a condition: the prescription applies at death's arrival.
SAMIN-DURR:2:180/r5.anchor: العامل في " إذا " " كتب " على أنها ظرف محض، وليس متضمنا للشرط

SAMIN-DURR:2:180/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:180/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:180/r6.claim: الوصية cannot govern إذا as a مصدر whose complement precedes it; Abu al-Hasan permits that only under his expansive treatment of adverbs and their equivalents.
SAMIN-DURR:2:180/r6.anchor: ولا يجوز أن يكون العامل فيه لفظ " الوصية " لأنها مصدر، ومعمول المصدر لا يتقدم عليه

SAMIN-DURR:2:180/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:180/r7.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:2:180/r7.claim: Ibn Atiyya reads كتب as expressing God's binding decree, written from eternity; الوصية is نائب الفاعل, and both conditional answers are omitted but indicated by كتب.
SAMIN-DURR:2:180/r7.anchor: قال ابن عطية: " ويتجه في إعراب هذه الآية أن يكون " كتب " هو العامل في " إذا "

SAMIN-DURR:2:180/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:180/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:180/r8.claim: The author finds Ibn Atiyya inconsistent: إذا governed by كتب is temporal, whereas a conditional إذا cannot be governed by كتب if its answer is omitted.
SAMIN-DURR:2:180/r8.anchor: قال الشيخ: " وفي هذا تناقض لأنه جعل العامل في " إذا " كتب، وذلك يستلزم

SAMIN-DURR:2:180#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:180#2/r1.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:2:180#2/r1.claim: Ibn Atiyya lets an implied الإيصاء govern إذا and makes الوصية a مبتدأ; the implicit answer is like فعليه الوصية with a deleted فاء.
SAMIN-DURR:2:180#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطية في هذا الوجه: " ويكون هذا الإيصاء المقدر الذي يدل عليه ذكر الوصية بعد هو العامل في

SAMIN-DURR:2:180#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:180#2/r2.speaker: سيبويه
SAMIN-DURR:2:180#2/r2.claim: Ibn Atiyya invokes Sibawayh's conditional verse example, من يفعل الصالحات الله يحفظه, with the answer's فاء omitted.
SAMIN-DURR:2:180#2/r2.anchor: على [نحو] ما أنشده سيبويه: 829 من يفعل الصالحات الله يحفظه

SAMIN-DURR:2:180#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:180#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:180#2/r3.claim: The author objects that if implied الإيصاء governs إذا, it is purely temporal and cannot have a conditional answer; an omitted or implicit مصدر cannot govern under Basran rules or be deleted as نائب الفاعل.
SAMIN-DURR:2:180#2/r3.anchor: أحدها: أنه متناقض من حيث إنه إذا جعل " إذا " معمولة للإيصاء المقدر تمحضت للظرفية

SAMIN-DURR:2:180#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:180#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:180#2/r4.claim: A single clause cannot answer both إن and إذا; each condition requires its own answer.
SAMIN-DURR:2:180#2/r4.anchor: الثالث: قوله " جواب الشرطين " والشيء الواحد لا يكون جوابا لاثنين، بل جواب كل واحد مستقل بقدره

SAMIN-DURR:2:180#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:180#2/r5.speaker: سيبويه
SAMIN-DURR:2:180#2/r5.claim: Sibawayh permits deleting فاء جواب only by poetic necessity, citing a line where الله يشكرها follows the conditional.
SAMIN-DURR:2:180#2/r5.anchor: وهذا نص سيبويه على أنه لا يجوز إلا ضرورة وأنشد: من يفعل الحسنات الله يشكرها

SAMIN-DURR:2:180#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:180#2/r6.speaker: المبرد
SAMIN-DURR:2:180#2/r6.claim: Al-Mubarrad reportedly forbids deleting فاء even in poetry and transmits فالرحمن يشكره; others say this does not refute Sibawayh's transmitted wording.
SAMIN-DURR:2:180#2/r6.anchor: والمبرد روي عنه أنه لا يجيز حذف الفاء مطلقا، لا في ضرورة ولا غيرها

SAMIN-DURR:2:180#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:180#2/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:180#2/r7.claim: The preferred parse estimates إن ترك خيرا فليوص; that omitted answer also indicates the answer to إذا, better than making one condition answer another or reinterpreting كتب.
SAMIN-DURR:2:180#2/r7.anchor: وتحقيقه: أن جواب " إن " مقدر، تقديره: " كتب الوصية على أحدكم إذا حضره الموت إن ترك خيرا فليوص

SAMIN-DURR:2:180#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:180#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:180#3/r1.claim: الوصية may be a مبتدأ with للوالدين as its predicate.

SAMIN-DURR:2:180#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:180#3/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:180#3/r2.claim: Alternatively الوصية is the object and نائب الفاعل of كتب.
SAMIN-DURR:2:180#3/r2.anchor: والثاني: أنه مفعول " كتب " وقد تقدم

SAMIN-DURR:2:180#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:180#3/r3.speaker: الأخفش
SAMIN-DURR:2:180#3/r3.claim: A third parse makes الوصية a مبتدأ with omitted predicate فعليه; the author says al-Akhfash's permission to drop فاء جواب is refuted by Sibawayh's transmission.
SAMIN-DURR:2:180#3/r3.anchor: وهذا عند من يجيز حذف فاء الجواب وهو الأخفش وهو محجوج بنقل سيبويه

SAMIN-DURR:2:180#3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:180#3/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:180#3/r4.claim: بالمعروف may attach to الوصية or be a circumstantial qualifier through an omitted phrase: the bequest is fair, not unjust.
SAMIN-DURR:2:180#3/r4.anchor: أن يتعلق بمحذوف على أنه حال من الوصية، أي: حال كونها ملتبسة بالمعروف لا بالجور

SAMIN-DURR:2:180#4/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:180#4/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:180#4/r1.claim: حقا may modify an omitted مصدر of كتب or أوصى, meaning a true writing or bequest.
SAMIN-DURR:2:180#4/r1.anchor: أحدها: أن يكون نعتا لمصدر محذوف، وذلك المصدر المحذوف: إما مصدر " كتب "

SAMIN-DURR:2:180#4/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:180#4/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:180#4/r2.claim: Alternatively حقا is a circumstantial accusative from the definite omitted مصدر of كتب or أوصى.
SAMIN-DURR:2:180#4/r2.anchor: الثاني: أنه حال من المصدر المعرف المحذوف: [إما] مصدر " كتب " أو " أوصى "

SAMIN-DURR:2:180#4/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:180#4/r3.speaker: الزمخشري وابن عطية وأبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:2:180#4/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari, Ibn Atiyya, and Abu al-Baqa take حقا as emphasis of the sentence's content, with omitted عامل حق ذلك حقا.
SAMIN-DURR:2:180#4/r3.anchor: وقال الشيخ: " وهذا تأباه القواعد النحوية، لأن ظاهر قوله: " على المتقين " أن يتعلق

SAMIN-DURR:2:180#4/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:180#4/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:180#4/r4.claim: The author objects that attaching على المتقين to an emphatic مصدر violates its inability to govern, while making it an adjective undermines emphasis.
SAMIN-DURR:2:180#4/r4.anchor: لأن المصدر المؤكد لا يعمل، وأما الثاني فلأن [الوصف يخرجه عن التأكيد]

SAMIN-DURR:2:180#4/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:180#4/r5.speaker: بعض المعربين
SAMIN-DURR:2:180#4/r5.claim: Some grammarians attach حقا to the meaning of المتقين, like الأنفال 74; the author objects that it precedes its relative عامل and is unnatural.
SAMIN-DURR:2:180#4/r5.anchor: وقال بعض المعربين: " إنه مؤكد لما تضمنه معنى " المتقين " كأنه قيل: على المتقين حقا

SAMIN-DURR:2:180#4/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:180#4/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:180#4/r6.claim: The author prefers حقا as a verbal noun from the meaning of كتب: كتب الوصية means it became due, like قعدت جلوسا.
SAMIN-DURR:2:180#4/r6.anchor: قال الشيخ: " والأولى عندي أن يكون مصدرا من معنى " كتب " لأن معنى " كتب الوصية "

ZAJJAJ:v1p249/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p249/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p249/r3.claim: The second ‘prescribed for you’ omits the conjunction waw, which long discourse can leave understood; the sense is that both retaliation and bequest were prescribed.
ZAJJAJ:v1p249/r3.anchor: إذا طال استغنى عن العطف بالواو

ZAJJAJ:v1p249/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p249/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p249/r4.claim: The bequest requirement was abrogated by the inheritance verses in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ; Zajjāj explains its original wisdom because God prescribes with profound wisdom.
ZAJJAJ:v1p249/r4.anchor: هذا الفرض بإجماع نسخته آيات المواريث في سورة النساء وهذا مجمع عليه

ZAJJAJ:v1p249/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p249/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p249/r5.claim: The original prescription meant that one who left wealth was to bequeath fairly to parents and relatives.
ZAJJAJ:v1p249/r5.anchor: فمعنى (كتب عليكم): فرض عليكم - إن ترك أحدكم مالا - الوصية (للوالدين والأقربين بالمعروف)

ZAJJAJ:v1p249/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p249/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p249/r6.claim: Al-waṣiyya may be the passive subject in ‘the bequest was prescribed,’ or a nominative topic with li-l-wālidayn as predicate in the sense of a reported instruction.
ZAJJAJ:v1p249/r6.anchor: فرفع الوصية على ضربين، أحدهما على ما لم يسم فاعله، كأنه قال كتب عليكم الوصية للوالدين

ZAJJAJ:v1p249/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p249/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p249/r7.claim: The command addressed favoritism toward distant outsiders for display and reputation by directing a fair bequest to parents and close relatives.
ZAJJAJ:v1p249/r7.anchor: وإنما أمروا بالوصية في ذلك الوقت لأنهم كانوا ربما جاوزوا بدفع المال إلى البعداء طلبا للرياء والسمعة.

ZAJJAJ:v1p249/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p249/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p249/r8.claim: The verse does not require making a will while death is actually present, when a person is occupied; it requires arranging it while still able, in anticipation of death.
ZAJJAJ:v1p249/r8.anchor: ليس هو إنه كتب عليه أن يوصي إذا حضره الموت

ZAJJAJ:v1p249/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p249/r9.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p249/r9.claim: Bi-l-maʿrūf means what a discerning person recognizes as free of bias and injustice.
ZAJJAJ:v1p249/r9.anchor: بالشيء الذي يعلم ذو التمييز أنه لا جنف فيه ولا جور

ZAJJAJ:v1p250/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p250/r1.speaker: قوم
ZAJJAJ:v1p250/r1.claim: Some say the bequest command remains for one third; al-Zajjāj rejects this as an obligatory command, since Muslims agree one may bequeath a third or leave it, and the verse’s prescription was abrogated.
ZAJJAJ:v1p250/r1.anchor: وأمر الوصية في الثلث باق، وهذا القول ليس بشي لأن إجماع المسلمين أن ثلث الرجل له

ZAJJAJ:v1p250/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p250/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p250/r2.claim: Ḥaqqan is accusative as ‘that is truly required of you’; outside Qur’anic wording, nominative would also be grammatical.
ZAJJAJ:v1p250/r2.anchor: نصب على حق ذلك عليكم حقا

ASAD-NOTES:2:180#n152/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:180#n152/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:2:180#n152/r1.claim: Khayr here means “much wealth,” not merely property; sayings of A’ishah and Ali ibn Abi Talib support this reading, as do Zamakhshari and Baydawi.
ASAD-NOTES:2:180#n152/r1.anchor: The word khayr occurring in this sentence denotes "much wealth" and not simply "property"

ASAD-NOTES:2:180#n152/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:180#n152/r2.speaker: A'ishah and Ali ibn Abi Talib
ASAD-NOTES:2:180#n152/r2.claim: Sayings of A’ishah and Ali ibn Abi Talib, both referring to this verse, support reading khayr as much wealth.
ASAD-NOTES:2:180#n152/r2.anchor: supported by sayings of 'A'ishah and 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, both of them referring to this particular verse

ASAD-NOTES:2:180#n152/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:180#n152/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:2:180#n152/r3.claim: Those leaving much wealth should bequeath to particularly deserving family members in addition to, and before distributing, the fixed inheritance shares in 4:11–12.
ASAD-NOTES:2:180#n152/r3.anchor: make bequests to particularly deserving members of his family in addition to - and preceding the distribution of - the legally - fixed shares mentioned in 4:11-12

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p120/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p120/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p120/r1.claim: Al-Baqillani left later inimitability writers a rich rhetorical vocabulary; the Sakaki school inherited his method of placing Qur'anic examples beside human speech without distinction.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p120/r1.anchor: وترك لمدرسة السكاكي، طريقته في التناول البلاغي: تقدم مع الشواهد من قول البشر شاهداً من القرآن، دون تفرقة أو تمييز

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p120/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p120/r2.speaker: الجرجاني
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p120/r2.claim: Al-Jurjani's fifth-century treatise addresses theological disputes over inimitability and counters those who divert the explanation from rhetoric, especially proponents of ṣarfa.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p120/r2.anchor: والجرجاني - من القرن الخامس الهجري - يعرض في رسالته (الشافية) لقضية الإعجاز في جدل المتكلمين خصومه المذهبيين

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p120/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p120/r3.speaker: الجرجاني
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p120/r3.claim: For al-Jurjani, the challenge was to compose on any chosen subject at a level equal or close to the Qur'an's excellence; isolated words, lexical meanings, and mere matching of meter and rhyme were not the challenge.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p120/r3.anchor: ويذهب الجرجاني إلى استحالة أن يكون التحدي بالكلم المفردة أو بمعانيها التي هي لها بوضع اللغة

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p120/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p120/r4.speaker: الجرجاني
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p120/r4.claim: Al-Jurjani defines composition as pursuing grammatical meanings and rules in the relations among words; the author identifies this nazm and arrangement as the remaining site of inimitability.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p120/r4.anchor: ليس شيئاً غير توخي معاني النحو وأحكامه فيما بين الكلم

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p68#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p68#2/r1.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p68#2/r1.claim: Ali tells a dying dependent with little property that he need not make a bequest, invoking the verse’s condition of leaving substantial wealth.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p68#2/r1.anchor: دخل علي بن أبي طالب على مولى لهم وهو في الموت فقال ألا أوصي فقال له قال الله تبارك وتعالى

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p68#2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p68#2/r2.speaker: الزهري
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p68#2/r2.claim: Al-Zuhri says God made the bequest an obligation whether the estate is small or large.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p68#2/r2.anchor: عن الزهري قال جعل الله الوصية حقا مما قل منه أو كثر

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p68#2/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p68#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p68#2/r3.claim: Qatada says the bequest to parents was abrogated, while it remained for relatives who do not inherit.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p68#2/r3.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ إن ترك خيرا الوصية للوالدين والأقربين ﴾ قال نسخ الوالدين منها وترك الأقربين ممن لا يرث

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p68#2/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p68#2/r4.speaker: إبراهيم
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p68#2/r4.claim: Ibrahim says a bequest is good but optional: the Prophet died without making one, while Abu Bakr did make one.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p68#2/r4.anchor: عن إبراهيم قال ذكر عنده طلحة والزبير فقيل كانا يشددان في الوصية فقال وما عليهما ألا يفعلا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p155/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p155/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p155/r3.claim: The will verse follows naturally after the discussion of killing, retaliation, and blood money: it alerts each person to make a will before sudden death.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p155/r3.anchor: وذلك أنه لما ذكر تعالى القتل في القصاص، والدية، أتبع ذلك بالتنبيه على الوصية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p155/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p155/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p155/r4.claim: There is no need to coordinate this clause with the earlier command about retaliation or posit a deleted conjunction; it is a new sentence clearly connected in meaning to what precedes.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p155/r4.anchor: ولا ضرورة تدعو إلى أن: كتب، أصله: العطف على. كتب عليكم القصاص في القتلى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p155/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p155/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p155/r5.claim: The author's preferred sense of death's arrival is the arrival of its precursors and causes, such as illness and alarming symptoms; Arabic usage metaphorically calls causes of death death.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p155/r5.anchor: ومعنى حضور الموت أي: حضور مقدماته وأسبابه من العلل والأمراض والأعراض المخوفة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p155/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p155/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p155/r6.claim: The Qurʾānic phrase about death coming from every place while the person is not dead and the cited poems use death for its causes or personify death; Antarah, Jarir, and an unnamed poet provide examples.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p155/r6.anchor: والعرب تطلق على أسباب الموت موتا على سبيل التجوز. وقال تعالى: ويأتيه الموت من كل مكان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p155/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p155/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p155/r7.claim: The plural address means each believer individually, then the clause switches to one of you; the expected plural was avoided by following the universal sense of upon you, a rare construction illustrated by poetry.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p155/r7.anchor: ولو جرى نظم الكلام على خطاب المؤمنين لكان: إذا حضركم الموت، لكنه روعيت دلالة العموم في: عليكم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p157/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p157/r1.speaker: قول غير مسمى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p157/r1.claim: An alternative takes death literally and addresses executors and heirs: when someone dies they must carry out the will; on this reading the verse itself does not prove that making a will is obligatory.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p157/r1.anchor: وقيل: المراد بالموت هنا حقيقته لا مقدماته، فيكون الخطاب متوجها إلى الأوصياء والورثة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p157/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p157/r2.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p157/r2.claim: Mujahid says khayr means wealth throughout the Qurʾān, citing its uses for wealth in several other passages.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p157/r2.anchor: وقال مجاهد: الخير في القرآن كله المال وإنه لحب الخير لشديد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p157/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p157/r3.speaker: الزهري وأبو مجلز
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p157/r3.claim: They take the apparent wording to mean any amount of wealth, so a will is due whether the estate is small or large.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p157/r3.anchor: وبه قال: الزهري، وأبو مجلز، وغيرهما، قالوا: تجب فيما قل وفيما كثر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p157/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p157/r4.speaker: أبان
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p157/r4.claim: Aban sets the minimum estate for the obligation at two hundred silver dirhams.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p157/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p157/r5.speaker: النخعي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p157/r5.claim: Al-Nakhaʿi places the threshold between one thousand and five hundred dirhams.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p157/r5.anchor: وقال النخعي: من ألف درهم إلى خمسمائة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p157/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p157/r6.speaker: علي وقتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p157/r6.claim: ʿAli and Qatada set the threshold at one thousand dirhams or more.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p157/r6.anchor: وقال علي: وقتادة: ألف درهم فصاعدا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p157/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p157/r7.speaker: الجصاص
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p157/r7.claim: Al-Jaṣṣāṣ sets the threshold at four thousand dirhams.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p157/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p157/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p157/r8.claim: Those who define sufficient wealth by its relative abundance say the amount depends on a person's circumstances and the number of dependents.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p157/r8.anchor: وأما من قدره بمطلق الكثرة، فإن ذلك يختلف بحسب اختلاف حال الرجل، وكثرة عياله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p157/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p157/r9.speaker: عائشة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p157/r9.claim: ʿĀʾisha considered four hundred dinars no surplus for a man with dependents; for a family of four and three thousand, she likewise called it little and advised leaving it to the children.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p157/r9.anchor: وروي عن عائشة أنها قالت: ما أرى فضلا في مال هو أربعمائة دينار لرجل أراد أن يوصي وله عيال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p157/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p157/r10.speaker: علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p157/r10.claim: ʿAli stopped a client with seven hundred from making a will, saying that this did not count as wealth under the verse.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p157/r10.anchor: وعن علي: أن مولى له أراد أن يوصي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p157/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p157/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p157/r11.claim: The lack of a fixed amount does not negate obligation: the apparent rule applies once any wealth exists; if khayr has a narrower sense, juristic judgment determines what qualifies as good and sufficient wealth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p157/r11.anchor: ولا يدل عدم تقدير المال على أن الوصية لم تجب، إذ الظاهر التعليق بوجود مطلق الخير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p157/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p157/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p157/r12.claim: Calling the estate khayr subtly implies that it is lawful wealth: illicit property must be returned to its owners, and making a will from it is sinful.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p157/r12.anchor: وفي تسميته هنا وجعله خيرا إشارة لطيفة إلى أنه مال طيب لا خبيث

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p157/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p157/r13.speaker: قول غير مسمى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p157/r13.claim: One view holds the verse operative and makes a bequest to parents and relatives obligatory alongside their inheritance under the two verses.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p157/r13.anchor: فقال قوم: الآية محكمة، والوصية للوالدين والأقربين واجبة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p157/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p157/r14.speaker: قول غير مسمى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p157/r14.claim: Another view considers the verse operative but understands it to recommend voluntary bequests.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p157/r14.anchor: وقال قوم: إنها محكمة في التطوع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p157/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p157/r15.speaker: قول غير مسمى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p157/r15.claim: A further view says the will command does not conflict with inheritance; it concerns God's assignment of parents' and relatives' shares.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p157/r15.anchor: وقال قوم: إنها محكمة وليس معنى الوصية مخالفا للميراث، بل المعنى: كتب عليكم ما أوصى به الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p158/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p158/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p158/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the person near death must preserve for parents and relatives the shares God assigned them and not reduce those allotments.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p158/r1.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: أو كتب على المحتضر أن يوصي للوالدين والأقربين بتوفير ما أوصى به الله لهم عليهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p158/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p158/r2.speaker: الحسن وطاووس والضحاك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p158/r2.claim: They limit the operative command to parents and relatives who do not inherit, such as enslaved or non-Muslim kin, and to a bequest of one third or less.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p158/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p158/r3.speaker: ابن المنذر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p158/r3.claim: Ibn al-Mundhir reports a consensus among the scholars known to him that bequests to non-inheriting parents and relatives are permissible.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p158/r3.anchor: وقال: ابن المنذر: أجمع كل من يحفظ عنه من أهل العلم على أن الوصية للوالدين والأقرباء الذين لا يرثون جائزة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p158/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p158/r4.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن وقتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p158/r4.claim: They say the verse initially governed all relatives, then was abrogated as to anyone who inherits by the inheritance verse.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p158/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عباس، والحسن، وقتادة: الآية عامة، وتقرر الحكم بها برهة، ونسخ منها كل من يرث بآية الفرائض

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p158/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p158/r5.speaker: ابن عمر وابن عباس وابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p158/r5.claim: They regard the entire verse as abrogated; the bequest remains recommended, a position also attributed to al-Shaʿbi, al-Nakhaʿi, and Malik.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p158/r5.anchor: وقال ابن عمر، وابن عباس أيضا، وابن زيد: الآية كلها منسوخة. وبقيت الوصية ندبا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p158/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p158/r6.speaker: الربيع بن خثيم وغيره
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p158/r6.claim: Al-Rabiʿ ibn Khuthaym and others are reported as holding that there is no bequest.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p158/r6.anchor: لا وصية، وقيل: كانت في بدء الإسلام فنسخت بآية المواريث

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p158/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p158/r7.speaker: النبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p158/r7.claim: A prophetic report says God has assigned each rightful holder his right and that there is no bequest for an heir; the community's acceptance gives this solitary report near mass-transmitted status because they accept only established sound reports.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p158/r7.anchor: وبقوله عليه السلام: «إن الله أعطى كل ذي حق حقه، ألا لا وصية لوارث»

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p158/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p158/r8.speaker: قول غير مسمى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p158/r8.claim: One position gives relatives first claim on bequests and bars a bequest to outsiders when relatives are left without one.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p158/r8.anchor: وقال قوم: الوصية للقرابة أولا، فإن كانت لأجنبي فمعهم، ولا يجوز لغيرهم مع تركهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p158/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p158/r9.speaker: الشعبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p158/r9.claim: When Abu al-ʿAliya left his estate to Banu Hashim despite having been freed by a woman of Riyah, al-Shaʿbi objected that he had no right to do so.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p158/r9.anchor: وقال الشعبي: لم يكن ذلك له ولا كرامة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p158/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p158/r10.speaker: طاووس وجابر وابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p158/r10.claim: They say a bequest to non-relatives is redirected to the testator's relatives and the disposition annulled; this is also related from al-Hasan and held by Ishaq ibn Rahawayh.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p158/r10.anchor: وقال طاووس: إذا أوصى لغير قرابته ردت الوصية إلى قرابته ونقض فعله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p158/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p158/r11.speaker: الحسن وجابر بن زيد وعبد الملك بن يعلى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p158/r11.claim: They permit the third of the estate to remain with the recipient the testator selected.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p158/r11.anchor: وقال الحسن، وجابر بن زيد، أيضا، وعبد الملك بن يعلى: يبقى ثلث الوصية حيث جعلها الميت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p158/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p158/r12.speaker: مالك وأبو حنيفة والشافعي وأحمد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p158/r12.claim: They allow a bequest to an outsider even when relatives are left, whether the recipient is rich or poor and Muslim or non-Muslim; this is also reported from ʿUmar, Ibn ʿAbbas, and ʿAʾisha.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p158/r12.anchor: وقال مالك، وأبو حنيفة، والشافعي، وأحمد: إذا أوصى لغير قرابته وترك قرابته جاز ذلك وأمضي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p158/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p158/r13.speaker: الثوري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p158/r13.claim: Al-Thawri takes the apparent command to make a will as obligatory for anyone who leaves property.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p158/r13.anchor: وظاهر: كتب، وجوب الوصية على من خلف مالا، وهو قول الثوري

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p159/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p159/r1.speaker: أبو ثور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p159/r1.claim: Abu Thawr says a will is obligatory only for someone with a debt or property entrusted by others; it is not obligatory for someone with neither.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p159/r1.anchor: لا تجب إلا على من عليه دين أو عنده مال لقوم، فأما من لا دين عليه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p159/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p159/r2.speaker: قول غير مسمى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p159/r2.claim: Another view denies that making a will is obligatory, citing al-Nakhaʿi's report that the Prophet died without making one and a hadith that conditions it on wanting to make a will.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p159/r2.anchor: وقيل: لا تجب الوصية، واستدل بقول النخعي: مات رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ولم يوص

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p159/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p159/r3.speaker: أبو حنيفة ومالك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p159/r3.claim: They permit a bequest to an heir if the other heirs approve it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p159/r3.anchor: والموصى له، إن كان وارثا وأجاز ذلك الورثة جاز، وبه قال أبو حنيفة، ومالك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p159/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p159/r4.speaker: أبو حنيفة ومحمد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p159/r4.claim: They allow a bequest to an intentional killer if the heirs approve it; Abu Yusuf says such a bequest is invalid.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p159/r4.anchor: أو قاتلا عمدا وأجاز ذلك الورثة، جاز في قول أبي حنيفة ومحمد. وقال أبو يوسف: لا تجوز

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p159/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p159/r5.speaker: مالك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p159/r5.claim: If the testator directs that a bequest to an heir go to God's cause unless the heirs approve it, Malik says it becomes part of the estate when they refuse.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p159/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p159/r6.speaker: أبو حنيفة ومعمر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p159/r6.claim: They say the refused bequest in that arrangement is spent in God's cause.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p159/r6.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة، ومعمر: يمضى في سبيل الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p159/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p159/r7.speaker: ابن أبي ليلى وعثمان البتي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p159/r7.claim: They hold that if heirs approve an outsider's bequest above one third during the testator's life, they cannot revoke that approval after death.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p159/r7.anchor: قاله ابن أبي ليلى، وعثمان البتي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p159/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p159/r8.speaker: أبو حنيفة ومحمد وأبو يوسف وزفر والحسن بن صالح وعبيد الله بن الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p159/r8.claim: They require heirs to renew their approval after death; consent given during the testator's life alone is ineffective, a view also reported from ʿAbd Allah, Shurayh, and Ibrahim.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p159/r8.anchor: إن أجازوا ذلك في حياته لم يجز ذلك حتى يجيزوه بعد الموت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p159/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p159/r9.speaker: ابن القاسم عن مالك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p159/r9.claim: Under Malik's view, separately situated heirs who consent cannot revoke, while dependent household members or close kin may revoke if the testator recovers and can cut off their support.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p159/r9.anchor: وقال ابن القاسم عن مالك: إن استأذنهم فأذنوا فكل وارث بائن فليس له أن يرجع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p159/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p159/r10.speaker: ابن وهب عن مالك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p159/r10.claim: Ibn Wahb reports that heirs may withdraw consent given in good health but not consent given during illness; al-Layth agrees with Malik, and jurists agree that approval after death cannot be revoked.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p159/r10.anchor: وقال ابن وهب عن مالك: إن أذنوا له في الصحة فلهم أن يرجعوا، أو في المرض فلا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p159/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p159/r11.speaker: طاووس وعطاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p159/r11.claim: Tawus and ʿAtaʾ hold that heirs' approval during the testator's life is binding.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p159/r11.anchor: وروي عن طاووس وعطاء: إن أجازوه في الحياة جاز عليهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p159/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p159/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p159/r12.claim: Jurists agree that a sane adult who is not legally interdicted may make a valid will; they disagree about minors: Abu Hanifa bars it, while Malik and others allow it, as do two reported Shafiʿi positions.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p159/r12.anchor: ولا خلاف في صحة وصية العاقل البالغ غير المحجور عليه واختلف في الصبي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p159/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p159/r13.speaker: أبو حنيفة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p159/r13.claim: Abu Hanifa rejects a minor's will; al-Muzani says this follows by analogy from al-Shafiʿi, while Malik and others permit it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p159/r13.anchor: فقال أبو حنيفة: لا تجوز وصيته. قال المزني: وهو قياس قول الشافعي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p159/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p159/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p159/r14.claim: The command's apparent wording supports barring a minor from making a will because a minor is not legally accountable, but everyone agrees that a person may change or revoke their own will.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p159/r14.anchor: وظاهر قوله تعالى: كتب المنع. لأنه ليس من أهل التكليف، وأجمعوا على أنه للإنسان أن يغير وصيته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p160/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p160/r1.speaker: مالك وأبو حنيفة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p160/r1.claim: Malik and Abu Hanifa say an owner cannot revoke a mudabbar arrangement; al-Shafiʿi, Ahmad, Ishaq, al-Shaʿbi, al-Nakhaʿi, Ibn Shubruma, and al-Thawri treat it as a will.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p160/r1.anchor: فذهب مالك وأبو حنيفة إلى أنه ليس له أن يغير ما دبر، قال الشافعي، وأحمد، وإسحاق: هو وصيته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p160/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p160/r2.speaker: النبي وعائشة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p160/r2.claim: The Prophet is reported to have sold a mudabbar, and ʿAʾisha sold a female mudabbar; these sales are cited in the dispute over whether the arrangement can be revoked.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p160/r2.anchor: وأن عائشة باعت مدبرة، وإذا قال لعبده

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p160/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p160/r3.speaker: مالك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p160/r3.claim: Malik allows revocation after the words You are free after my death; saying someone is a mudabbar cannot be revoked, nor can the first wording be retracted if it was intended as manumission after death.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p160/r3.anchor: وإذا قال لعبده: أنت حر بعد موتي، فله الرجوع عند مالك في ذلك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p160/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p160/r4.speaker: الشافعي وأحمد وإسحاق وأبو ثور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p160/r4.claim: They classify all these formulations as wills.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p160/r4.anchor: وأما الشافعي، وأحمد، وإسحاق، وأبو ثور، فكل هذا عندهم وصية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p160/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p160/r5.speaker: أبو ثور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p160/r5.claim: Abu Thawr says the declaration I have revoked my mudabbar cancels the arrangement; al-Shafiʿi requires an actual sale or gift, since merely saying I revoke is ineffective.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p160/r5.anchor: فقال أبو ثور: إذا قال: رجعت في مدبري بطل التدبير، وقال الشافعي: لا يكون إلا ببيع أو هبة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p160/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p160/r6.speaker: ابن القاسم وأشهب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p160/r6.claim: For the ambiguous statement that a slave will be free after the owner's death without expressly intending a will or manumission arrangement, Ibn al-Qasim calls it a will and Ashhab calls it a mudabbar.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p160/r6.anchor: فقال ابن القاسم: هو وصية؟ وقال أشهب: هو مدبر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p160/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p160/r7.speaker: الدارقطني عن أنس بن مالك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p160/r7.claim: A testament formula used by the righteous predecessors confesses God's oneness, Muhammad's messengership, the Hour and resurrection, then exhorts one's family to fear God, reconcile, and obey God and His Messenger; it invokes Abraham's and Jacob's counsel to their children to die as Muslims.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p160/r7.anchor: هذا ما أوصى فلان بن فلان، أنه يشهد أن لا إله إلا الله، وحده لا شريك له، وأن محمدا عبده ورسوله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p160/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p160/r8.speaker: أنس بن مالك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p160/r8.claim: Al-Daraqutni transmits the cited testament formula from Anas ibn Malik.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p160/r8.anchor: رواه الدارقطني، عن أنس بن مالك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p160/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p160/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p160/r9.claim: Kataba is passive, with its agent omitted because God is known to be meant and for brevity; al-waṣiyya is apparently the passive subject, and the feminine verb lacks agreement because of separation, length, nonhuman feminine gender, and the sense of bequeathing.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p160/r9.anchor: وبني كتب للمفعول وحذف الفاعل للعلم به، وللاختصار، إذ معلوم أنه الله تعالى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p160/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p160/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p160/r10.claim: The answers to the two conditions are omitted. The sense is that the will was prescribed for a person when death's signs arrive and, if he has wealth, he should make a will; kataba cannot itself answer because it is past while the conditions are prospective.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p160/r10.anchor: وجواب الشرطين محذوف لدلالة المعنى عليه، ولا يجوز أن يكون من معنى: كتب، لمضي كتب واستقبال الشرطين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p161/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p161/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p161/r1.claim: The second condition has an omitted answer indicated by the first omitted answer, so the omitted answer in turn indicates another omission; the author calls the combined conditional structure one of the hardest syntax problems and refers readers to al-Takmil.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p161/r1.anchor: ويكون جواب الشرط الثاني محذوفا يدل عليه جواب الشرط الأول المحذوف، فيكون المحذوف دل على محذوف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p161/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p161/r2.speaker: قول غير مسمى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p161/r2.claim: Another parse treats both answers as omitted, understands kataba as future-directed obligation, and makes idha a temporal adverb governed by kataba; the answer to if he leaves wealth is then also omitted and signaled by kataba.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p161/r2.anchor: وقيل: جواب الشرطين محذوف ويقدر من معنى كتب عليكم الوصية ويتجوز بلفظ: كتب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p161/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p161/r3.speaker: أبو الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p161/r3.claim: Most grammarians do not let idha be governed by al-waṣiyya because a source or relative cannot have its complement preposed; Abu al-Hasan permits a temporal complement before a non-pure relative/source, as in the cited line attaching bi-l-raḥā to al-mutakāʿis.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p161/r3.anchor: وأجاز ذلك أبو الحسن لأنه يجوز عنده أن يتقدم المعمول إذا كان ظرفا على العامل فيه إذا لم يكن موصولا محضا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p161/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p161/r4.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p161/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya makes kataba govern idha, takes al-waṣiyya as the passive subject, and supplies a response to both conditions from the preceding kataba; Abū Ḥayyān finds this contradictory because idha cannot be both temporal and conditional.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p161/r4.anchor: وقال أبو محمد بن عطية: ويتجه في إعراب هذه الآية أن يكون: كتب، هو العامل في: إذا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p162/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p162/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p162/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya's parse cannot take the earlier spoken kataba as an omitted answer indicated by what precedes; that would make the estimated answer identical to the already uttered word. The apparent parse makes al-waṣiyya the passive subject of kataba.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p162/r1.anchor: وما كان مقدرا يدل عليه ما تقدم يستحيل أن يكون هو الملفوظ به المتقدم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p162/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p162/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p162/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari calls al-waṣiyya the faʿil of kataba, his term for the passive subject, and explains the masculine verb by separation and by the sense of the verbal phrase to make a will.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p162/r2.anchor: قال في تفسيره: والوصية فاعل كتب، وذكر فعلها للفاصل، ولأنها بمعنى: أن يوصي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p162/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p162/r3.speaker: قول غير مسمى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p162/r3.claim: Some grammarians make al-waṣiyya a subject in a conditional answer, with an omitted fa or an implied predicate such as it is due; the passive subject would be an implicit yuktabu explained by the wording that follows.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p162/r3.anchor: وأجاز بعض المعربين أن ترتفع الوصية على الابتداء، على تقدير الفاء، والخبر إما محذوف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p162/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p162/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p162/r4.claim: Abū Ḥayyān again finds Ibn ʿAṭiyya's analysis inconsistent: if idha is governed as a temporal adverb it is not a condition, and an omitted passive subject or unspoken verbal noun cannot serve as the proposed governor under the stated Basran rules.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p162/r4.anchor: لأن الشيء الواحد لا يكون شرطا وغير شرط في حالة واحدة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya misquotes Sibawayh's supporting verse; Sibawayh actually cites the line beginning whoever does good deeds, God rewards them, and says this construction is only poetic necessity.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163/r1.anchor: وأما قوله على نحو ما أيد سيبويه. من يفعل الحسنات الله يحفظه وهو تحريف على سيبويه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163/r2.speaker: سيبويه عن الخليل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163/r2.claim: Sibawayh transmits al-Khalil's ruling that a conditional clause without fa, such as if you come to me, I am generous, occurs only when a poet is forced; al-Akhfash's implied-fa analysis is refuted by this evidence.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163/r2.anchor: قال: لا يكون هذا إلا أن يضطر شاعر من قبل: أن أنا كريم، يكون كلاما مبتدأ

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163/r3.claim: The less strained parse makes the prepositional phrase ʿalaykum the passive subject: al-waṣiyya then answers the listener's implicit question about what was prescribed, as subject or predicate.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163/r3.anchor: وأجاز بعضهم أن تقام مقام المفعول الذي لم يسم فاعله الجار والمجرور الذي هو: عليكم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163#2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163#2/r1.claim: The prepositional phrase serving as passive subject is the best analysis and requires fewer assumptions than positing an implicit verbal noun and its pronoun.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163#2/r1.anchor: وهذا الوجه أحسن، وأقل تكلفا من الوجه الذي قبله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163#2/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163#2/r2.claim: The author says the phrase about parents was discussed earlier in the command to show kindness to parents.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163#2/r2.anchor: وتقدم الكلام على ذلك في قوله تعالى: وبالوالدين إحسانا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163#2/r3.claim: Al-aqrabīn is the plural of al-aqrab, an elative meaning nearest; its apparent scope includes every relative closer to the deceased, with parents named first and then included again for emphasis and special care.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163#2/r3.anchor: والأقربين جمع الأقرب، وظاهره أنه أفعل تفضيل، فكل من كان أقرب إلى الميت دخل في هذا اللفظ

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163#2/r4.speaker: المفسرون
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163#2/r4.claim: Exegetes identify the relatives variously as children, relatives other than children, all kin, or non-inheriting relatives.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163#2/r4.anchor: وعند المفسرين: الأقربون الأولاد، أو من عدا الأولاد، أو جميع القرابات، أو من لا يرث من الأقارب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163#2/r5.speaker: قول غير مسمى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163#2/r5.claim: One explanation of fairness limits a bequest to one third and says not to favor the rich over the poor.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163#2/r5.anchor: بالمعروف أي: لا يوصي بأزيد من الثلث، ولا للغني دون الفقير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163#2/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163#2/r6.claim: Ibn Masʿud explains fairness as giving first to the neediest relative.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163#2/r6.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود: الأخل فالأخل، أي: الأحوج فالأحوج

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163#2/r7.speaker: قول غير مسمى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163#2/r7.claim: Another explanation is that the will must contain no injustice.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163#2/r8.speaker: قول غير مسمى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163#2/r8.claim: Another view initially leaves the amount to the testator's judgment, then sets the upper limit at one third, citing the report that one third is much.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163#2/r8.anchor: وقيل: كان هذا موكولا إلى اجتهاد الموصي، ثم بين ذلك وقدر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163#2/r9.speaker: قول غير مسمى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163#2/r9.claim: Fairness may mean a moderate amount recognized by people's conscience without harming heirs, since people had sometimes bequeathed all their property.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163#2/r9.anchor: وقيل: بالقصد الذي تعرفه النفوس دون إضرار بالورثة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163#2/r10.speaker: قول غير مسمى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163#2/r10.claim: Another interpretation requires that the bequest concern a known portion of the testator's property rather than an unspecified amount.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163#2/r10.anchor: وقيل: بالمعروف من ماله غير المجهول

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163#2/r11.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163#2/r11.claim: Al-Zamakhshari summarizes fairness as justice: do not leave the poor for the rich and do not exceed one third.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163#2/r11.anchor: وقد لخص ذلك الزمخشري وفسره بالعدل، وهو أن لا يوصي للغني ويدع الفقير، ولا يتجاوز الثلث

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163#2/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163#2/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163#2/r12.claim: The phrase bi-l-maʿrūf attaches either to al-waṣiyya or to an omitted adjective meaning characterized by fairness, making it a circumstantial phrase.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163#2/r12.anchor: وتعلق بالمعروف بقوله: الوصية، أو بمحذوف، أي: كائنة بالمعروف، فيكون بالمعروف حالا من الوصية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163#2/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163#2/r13.speaker: ابن عطية والزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163#2/r13.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya and al-Zamakhshari parse ḥaqqan as an emphatic verbal noun affirming the sentence's content, roughly this is truly binding.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163#2/r13.anchor: انتصب: حقا، على أنه مصدر مؤكد لمضمون الجملة، أي: حق ذلك حقا، قاله ابن عطية، والزمخشري

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163#2/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163#2/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163#2/r14.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects that parse because the following phrase ʿalā al-muttaqīn must attach to ḥaqqan or describe it, which prevents ḥaqqan from being an emphatic verbal noun under the grammatical rules he cites.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163#2/r14.anchor: وهذا تأباه القواعد النحوية لأن ظاهر قوله: على المتقين إذن يتعلق على ب: حقا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p170/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p170/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p170/r3.claim: The passage prescribes a deathbed will, threatens those who knowingly alter it, and exempts reconciliation among recipients when the testator's will was biased or wrongful.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p170/r3.anchor: ثم ذكر تعالى مشروعية الوصية لمن حضره الموت، وذكر أن الوصية للوالدين والأقربين، وتوعد من بدل الوصية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p170/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p170/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p170/r4.claim: These verses frame the accountable person's life from faith in God at its beginning to the will at death, with major duties and sins selected as examples rather than an exhaustive list.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p170/r4.anchor: حاوية لما يطلب من المكلف من بدء حاله وهو: الإيمان بالله، وختم حاله وهو: الوصية عند مفارقه هذا الوجود

ALUSI-FULL:v2p52/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p52/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p52/r1.claim: This is an independent legal ruling, set apart from earlier rulings to mark its independence.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p52/r1.anchor: بيان حكم آخر من الأحكام المذكورة وفصله عما سبق

ALUSI-FULL:v2p52/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p52/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p52/r2.claim: The omitted “O believers” is explained by the recent admonition, the link to the preceding discussion of the dead, or the ruling’s lack of hardship.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p52/r2.anchor: ولم يصدره ب ( ياأيها الذين آمنوا ) لقرب العهد بالتنبيه

ALUSI-FULL:v2p52/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p52/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p52/r3.claim: Death’s arrival means either its causes and signs, such as dangerous illnesses, or death itself drawing near.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p52/r3.anchor: حضور أسبابه وظهور أماراته من العلل والأمراض المخوفة

ALUSI-FULL:v2p52/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p52/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p52/r4.claim: The fronting emphasizes how firmly the impending event takes hold of the person’s awareness.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p52/r4.anchor: وتقديم المفعول لإفادة كمال تمكن الفاعل عند النفس

ALUSI-FULL:v2p52/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p52/r5.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v2p52/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas and Mujahid explain “good” as property or wealth.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p52/r5.anchor: أي مالا كما قاله إبن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنه ومجاهد

ALUSI-FULL:v2p52/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p52/r6.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v2p52/r6.claim: Some restrict “good” to substantial wealth, since ordinary usage reserves “wealthy” for someone with a great deal.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p52/r6.anchor: إذ لا يقال في العرف للمال : ( خيرا ) إلا إذا كان كثيرا

ALUSI-FULL:v2p52/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p52/r7.speaker: علي
ALUSI-FULL:v2p52/r7.claim: Ali advised a dying client with six or seven hundred dirhams not to bequeath, citing the substantial-wealth condition; al-Bayhaqi and others transmit it from Urwa.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p52/r7.anchor: أن عليا كرم الله تعالى وجهه دخل على مولى له في الموت وله سبعمائة درهم أو ستمائة درهم

ALUSI-FULL:v2p52/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p52/r8.speaker: عائشة
ALUSI-FULL:v2p52/r8.claim: A man with three thousand dirhams and four dependents asked Aisha about bequeathing; she called it little and advised leaving it to his family.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p52/r8.anchor: عن عائشة رضي الله تعالى عنها أن رجلا

ALUSI-FULL:v2p52/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p52/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p52/r9.claim: Whether property counts as substantial depends on a person’s circumstances and dependents, not a fixed amount.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p52/r9.anchor: أن الكثرة غير مقدرة بمقدار بل تختلف باختلاف حال الرجل

ALUSI-FULL:v2p52/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p52/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v2p52/r10.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas sets the threshold at sixty dinars: whoever leaves less has not left “good.”
ALUSI-FULL:v2p52/r10.anchor: من لم يترك ستين دينارا لم يترك خيرا

ALUSI-FULL:v2p52/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p52/r11.speaker: الزهري
ALUSI-FULL:v2p52/r11.claim: Al-Zuhri holds that bequest is prescribed whether the estate is small or large, taking “good” to mean property without a size limit.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p52/r11.anchor: ومذهب الزهري أن ( الوصية ) مشروعة مما قل أو كثر

ALUSI-FULL:v2p52/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p52/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p52/r12.claim: Al-Alusi suggests the wording implies that bequests should use lawful, wholesome assets, since illicit property must be returned to its owners.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p52/r12.anchor: ينبغي أن يكون الموصى به حلالا طيبا لا خبيثا

ALUSI-FULL:v2p52/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p52/r13.speaker: الرضي
ALUSI-FULL:v2p52/r13.claim: Al-Radi explains the masculine verb form: omitting the feminine marker is preferable when a separated subject is grammatically but not truly feminine.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p52/r13.anchor: إذا كان الظاهر غير حقيقي التأنيث منفصلا فترك العلامة أحسن

ALUSI-FULL:v2p52/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p52/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p52/r14.claim: “Wasiyya” is the verbal noun and the thing enjoined; al-Qamus gives awṣā and waṣṣā as “to entrust or enjoin.”

ALUSI-FULL:v2p52/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p52/r15.speaker: الجمهور والرضي
ALUSI-FULL:v2p52/r15.claim: Most construe the preposition with “wasiyya” through an “an” clause plus verb; al-Radi permits a verbal noun without that reinterpretation and is preferred.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p52/r15.anchor: والجار متعلق بها فلا بد من تأويلها بأن مع الفعل عند الجمهور أو بالمصدر بناءا على تحقيق

ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r1.claim: One parse makes “the bequest” the subject of “was written”; the condition’s omitted answer is supplied by “was written for you.”
ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r1.anchor: ما المكتوب فقيل هو الوصية وجواب الشرط محذوف

ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r2.claim: Another parse makes “the bequest for parents” a nominal conditional answer with an implicit fā; Khalil rejects its omission except in poetic necessity.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r2.anchor: مبتدأ خبره ( للوالدين ) والجملة جواب الشرط بإضمار الفاء

ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r3.speaker: الخليل
ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r3.claim: Khalil rejects dropping the fā from a nominal conditional answer outside poetic necessity.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r3.anchor: إضمار الفاء غير صحيح لا يجتريء عليه إلا في ضرورة الشعر

ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r4.claim: “Was written” can govern “when”; the time phrase limits when the obligation arises while evoking its eternal inscription.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r4.anchor: والظرف قيد للإيجاب من حيث الحدوث والوقوع

ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r5.claim: A further parse makes “you” the deputy subject and “the bequest” the predicate, answering “What was written?”

ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r6.claim: The time phrase may instead be governed by “the bequest,” construed as a verbal noun or “an” clause; adverbs readily accommodate verbal force.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r6.anchor: وجوز أن يكون العامل الوصية وهي وإن كانت اسما

ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r7.claim: “One of you” is distributive, making the obligation individual rather than communal.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r7.anchor: يفيد العموم على سبيل البدل فمعنى

ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r8.claim: The wording is contrasted with the same “written upon you” formula for retaliation at 2:178.

ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r9.claim: Al-Alusi rejects the claim that the dying person must bequeath while others must preserve the will; preservation arises only after a will exists.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r9.anchor: بل عليه بأن يوصى وعلى الغير بأن يحفظ ولا يبدل

ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r10.claim: It is strained to make “you” mean intending and preserving the bequest instead of the bequest itself.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r10.anchor: إرادة الإيصاء وحفظه من الوصية تعسف لا يخفى

ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r11.speaker: بعض المحققين
ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r11.claim: Some investigators treat both clauses as conditions with omitted answers: if death comes, let him bequeath if he leaves property; the second condition qualifies the first.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r11.anchor: وأختار بعض المحققين أن ( إذا ) شرطية وجواب كل من الشرطين محذوف

ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r12.speaker: بعض المحققين
ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r12.claim: These investigators praise the parse for stating the rule generally, then detailing the required bequest parenthetically.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r12.anchor: ومجموع الشرطين معترض بين ( كتب ) وفاعله لبيان كيفية الإيصاء قبل

ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r13.claim: Al-Alusi cautions that the parse requires so many deletions that they weaken its advantages.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r13.anchor: وأنت تعلم ما في ذلك من كثرة الحذف المهونة لما تقدم

ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r14.speaker: ابن عباس وابن عمر وقتادة وشريح ومجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r14.claim: Ibn Abbas, Ibn Umar, Qatada, Shurayh, Mujahid, and others hold that the original bequest ruling was abrogated by inheritance verses.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r14.anchor: كما قاله إبن عباس وابن عمر وقتادة وشريح ومجاهد وغيرهم

ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r15.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r15.claim: The Prophet said God allotted each person an inheritance share, so no bequest may go to an heir; al-Tirmidhi graded the report sound.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r15.anchor: عن عمرو بن خارجة رضي الله تعالى عنهم أن النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم خطبهم

ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r16.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r16.claim: Abu Umama says he heard the Prophet at the Farewell Pilgrimage say that God gave every rights-holder their due and there is no bequest to an heir.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r16.anchor: عن أبي أمامة الباهلي سمعت رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم في حجة الوداع

ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r17.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r17.claim: Abd ibn Humayd transmits a similar statement from Hasan.

ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r18.claim: Al-Alusi says communal acceptance makes these reports recurrent enough for abrogation by his imams; some also infer recurrence from broad transmission or unopposed shared practice.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r18.anchor: لتلقي الأمة لها بالقبول انتظمت في سلك المتواتر في صحة النسخ بها عند أئمتنا

ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r19.claim: The inheritance verse itself effected abrogation, while the hadith explain how; al-Fakhr al-Islam then gives two arguments.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p53/r19.anchor: على أن النسخ في الحقيقة بآية المواريث والأحاديث مبينة لجهة نسخها

ALUSI-FULL:v2p54/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p54/r1.speaker: فخر الإسلام
ALUSI-FULL:v2p54/r1.claim: Al-Fakhr argues that the later inheritance verse says “after a bequest” indefinitely; if the earlier specified bequest still governed, inheritance would follow it, so the unrestricted wording abrogates it.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p54/r1.anchor: من بعد وصية يوصى بها أو دين

ALUSI-FULL:v2p54/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p54/r2.speaker: فخر الإسلام
ALUSI-FULL:v2p54/r2.claim: His second argument treats abrogation as transfer: God first required fair bequests among kin, then fixed shares Himself because testators may misjudge or intend harm.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p54/r2.anchor: فرض الإيصاء في الأقربين إلى العباد بشرط أن يراعوا الحدود

ALUSI-FULL:v2p54/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p54/r3.speaker: فخر الإسلام
ALUSI-FULL:v2p54/r3.claim: The fixed inheritance shares replace delegated bequests with God’s wiser allotment, like a principal freeing a slave after instructing an agent to do so.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p54/r3.anchor: على وجه تيقن به أنه الصواب وأن فيه الحكمة البالغة

ALUSI-FULL:v2p54/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p54/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p54/r4.claim: The fā in the inheritance passage signals that the earlier bequest scheme caused the transfer to inheritance.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p54/r4.anchor: الفاء تدل على سببية ما قبلها لما بعدها

ALUSI-FULL:v2p54/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p54/r5.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v2p54/r5.claim: Some argue the inheritance verse confirms bequests by giving them priority, and object that solitary reports are not made recurrent by communal acceptance.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p54/r5.anchor: آية المواريث لا تعارض هذا الحكم بل تحققه من حيث تدل على تقديم الوصية مطلقا

ALUSI-FULL:v2p54/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p54/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p54/r6.claim: Al-Alusi rejects anti-abrogation readings that identify the bequest with God’s inheritance allotment or the decedent’s duty to execute it.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p54/r6.anchor: على ما فيه بمعزل عن التحقيق وكذا ما قيل

ALUSI-FULL:v2p54/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p54/r7.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v2p54/r7.claim: Another account says bequests to heirs were obligatory without fixed shares, then God’s own bequest of inheritance shares replaced the former delegation.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p54/r7.anchor: من أن الوصية للوارث كانت واجبة بهذه الآية من غير تعيين لأنصبائهم

ALUSI-FULL:v2p54/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p54/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v2p54/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas holds that the duty was abrogated only for inheriting relatives and remained binding for non-inheriting relatives, such as non-Muslim kin.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p54/r8.anchor: وإليه ذهب إبن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنه

ALUSI-FULL:v2p54/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p54/r9.speaker: علي
ALUSI-FULL:v2p54/r9.claim: A report from Ali warns that dying without a bequest for non-inheriting relatives ends one’s work in disobedience.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p54/r9.anchor: وروي عن علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه من لم يوص عند موته لذوي قرابته ممن لا يرث

ALUSI-FULL:v2p54/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p54/r10.speaker: الأكثرون
ALUSI-FULL:v2p54/r10.claim: Most hold that obligation was abrogated for everyone, while bequests to non-inheriting relatives remain recommended.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p54/r10.anchor: وهي مستحبة في حق الذين لا يرثون وإليه ذهب الأكثرون

ALUSI-FULL:v2p54/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p54/r11.speaker: محمد بن الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v2p54/r11.claim: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan infers that “relatives” alone does not include parents because the verse coordinates parents and relatives.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p54/r11.anchor: وأستدل محمد بن الحسن بالآية على أن مطلق الأقربين لا يتناول الوالدين

ALUSI-FULL:v2p54/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p54/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p54/r12.claim: “As a duty” is a cognate accusative emphasizing “was written,” governed either by that verb or an implicit “it is truly due.”
ALUSI-FULL:v2p54/r12.anchor: مصدر مؤكد للحدث الذي دل عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v2p54/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p54/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p54/r13.claim: “Upon the God-fearing” can modify the accusative or the implicit verb; a verbal noun may also govern it directly.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p54/r13.anchor: صفة له أو متعلق بالفعل المحذوف على المختار

ALUSI-FULL:v2p54/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p54/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p54/r14.claim: “The God-fearing” means believers; the explicit description marks carrying out a bequest as a trait of those who fear God.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p54/r14.anchor: ووضع المظهر موضع المضمر للدلالة على أن المحافظة على الوصية

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p192/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p192/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p192/r1.claim: The command means that a bequest was made obligatory.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p192/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: {كتب عليكم} أي فرض عليكم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p192/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p192/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p192/r2.claim: Death arriving means the onset or signs of death, including illness and disease.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p192/r2.anchor: أي جاءه أسباب الموت وآثاره من العلل والأمراض

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p192/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p192/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p192/r3.claim: Khayr means property or wealth, as in the Quranic phrase about spending from good things.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p192/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p192/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p192/r4.claim: At the beginning of Islam, a person leaving property was required to bequeath to parents and close relatives; inheritance rules later abrogated this command.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p192/r4.anchor: كانت الوصية فريضة في ابتداء الإسلام للوالدين والأقربين على من مات وله مال ثم نسخت بآية الميراث

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p192/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p192/r5.speaker: عمرو بن خارجة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p192/r5.claim: Amr ibn Kharija reports the Prophet said God assigned each entitled person their due and there is no bequest for an heir.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p192/r5.anchor: عن عمرو بن خارجة قال: كنت آخذا بزمام ناقة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال:

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p192/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p192/r6.speaker: ابن عباس وطاووس وقتادة والحسن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p192/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas, Tawus, Qatada, and al-Hasan say the obligation was abrogated only for relatives who inherit and remained for noninheriting parents and relatives.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p192/r6.anchor: وهو قول ابن عباس وطاووس وقتادة والحسن

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p192/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p192/r7.speaker: طاووس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p192/r7.claim: Tawus says a bequest to named people should be taken back and given to needy relatives if the testator left those relatives out.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p192/r7.anchor: قال طاووس: من أوصى لقوم سماهم وترك ذوي قرابته محتاجين انتزعت منهم وردت إلى ذوي قرابته

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p192/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p192/r8.speaker: الأكثرون
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p192/r8.claim: Most scholars say the obligation was abrogated for everyone, though a bequest for noninheriting relatives remains strongly required.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p192/r8.anchor: وذهب الأكثرون إلى أن الوجوب صار منسوخا في حق الكافة وهي حتمية في حق الذين لا يرثون

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p192/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p192/r9.speaker: ابن عمر
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p192/r9.claim: Ibn Umar reports the Prophet said a Muslim who has something to bequeath should not spend two nights without a written will at hand.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p192/r9.anchor: عن ابن عمر أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p193/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p193/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p193/r1.claim: A bequest should follow proper practice, stay within one third, and not favor a wealthy person while leaving the poor; Ibn Masud says to prioritize the neediest relatives.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p193/r1.anchor: يريد يوصي بالمعروف ولا يزيد على الثلث ولا يوصي للغني ويدع الفقير، قال ابن مسعود: الوصية للأخل فالأخل أي الأحوج فالأحوج

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p193/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p193/r2.speaker: سعد بن مالك
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p193/r2.claim: Sa'd ibn Malik reports that the Prophet denied requests to bequeath all or half one's estate, then allowed a third but called it much and said leaving heirs wealthy is better than leaving them poor and begging.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p193/r2.anchor: عن سعد بن مالك قال جاءني النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يعودني

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p193/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p193/r3.speaker: عائشة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p193/r3.claim: Aisha told a man with 3,000 and four dependents that his estate was small and he should leave it for them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p193/r3.anchor: أن رجلا قال لعائشة رضي الله عنها: إني أريد أن أوصي

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p193/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p193/r4.speaker: علي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p193/r4.claim: Ali prefers bequeathing one fifth to one fourth and one fourth to one third; he says a person who bequeaths a third has left nothing behind.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p193/r4.anchor: وقال علي رضي الله عنه: لأن أوصي بالخمس أحب إلي من أن أوصي بالربع ولأن أوصي بالربع أحب إلي من أن أوصي بالثلث

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p193/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p193/r5.speaker: الحسن البصري
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p193/r5.claim: Al-Hasan al-Basri recommends bequeathing one sixth, one fifth, or one fourth.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p193/r5.anchor: وقال الحسن البصري رضي الله عنه يوصي بالسدس أو الخمس أو الربع

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p193/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p193/r6.speaker: الشعبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p193/r6.claim: Al-Shabi says people used to bequeath one fifth or one fourth.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p193/r6.anchor: وقال الشعبي إنما كانوا يوصون بالخمس أو الربع

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p193#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p193#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p193#2/r1.claim: Haqqan is accusative as a verbal noun, or as an object meaning that the bequest was made binding.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p193#2/r1.anchor: نصب على المصدر وقيل على المفعول أي جعل الوصية حقا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p193#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p193#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p193#2/r2.anchor: قوله تعالى: {حقا} نصب على المصدر وقيل على المفعول أي جعل الوصية حقا {على المتقين} المؤمنين

BURSEVI:v1p233/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p233/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p233/r1.claim: The Persian lines value freedom and death as a passage to greater life; the wise should subdue the self through spiritual discipline and enliven the heart with abiding life.
BURSEVI:v1p233/r1.anchor: شير مولى جويد آزادىء ومرك ونكه اندر مرك بيند صد وجود همو روانه بسوزاند وجود

BURSEVI:v1p233/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p233/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p233/r2.claim: The arrival of death means its causes and signs have appeared, such as illnesses and symptoms, rather than the instant of death itself.
BURSEVI:v1p233/r2.anchor: حضر أسبابه وظهر أمارته وآثاره من العلل والأمراض

BURSEVI:v1p233/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p233/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p233/r3.claim: A person cannot make a bequest at the actual moment of death, which is why the verse refers to the onset and signs of death.
BURSEVI:v1p233/r3.anchor: إذ لا اقتدار على الوصية عند حضور نفس الموت والعامل في إذا مدلول كتب

BURSEVI:v1p233/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p233/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p233/r4.claim: The semantic content of “was prescribed” governs the conditional; the prescription does not first occur at death, but its application to the person begins then.
BURSEVI:v1p233/r4.anchor: والعامل في إذا مدلول كتب لأن الكتب بمعنى الإيجاب لا يحدث وقت حضور الموت بل الحادث تعلقه بالمكلف

BURSEVI:v1p233/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p233/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p233/r5.claim: The wording “was prescribed” signals that this obligation was inscribed in pre-eternity, though it applies to the person at the onset of death.
BURSEVI:v1p233/r5.anchor: فكأنه قيل توجه عليكم إيجاب الله تعالى ومقتضى كتابه إذا حضر فعبر عن توجه الإيجاب وتعلقه بكتب للدلالة على أن هذا المعنى مكتوب في الأزل

BURSEVI:v1p233#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p233#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p233#2/r1.claim: Khayr here means property, whether little or much, though ordinary Arabic does not call someone a possessor of wealth when their property is small.
BURSEVI:v1p233#2/r1.anchor: {إن ترك خيرا} أي : مالا قليلا أو كثيرا

BURSEVI:v1p233#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p233#2/r2.speaker: عائشة
BURSEVI:v1p233#2/r2.claim: Aisha advised a man with three thousand and four dependents to leave his modest wealth to his children rather than make a bequest.
BURSEVI:v1p233#2/r2.anchor: وعن عائشة رضي الله عنها "أن رجلا أراد أن يوصي قالت : كم مالك؟ قال : ثلاثة آلاف

BURSEVI:v1p233#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p233#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p233#2/r3.claim: The basic sense of good is anything desirable and beneficial, the opposite of evil.
BURSEVI:v1p233#2/r3.anchor: وأصل الخير أن يكون لكل ما يرغب فيه مما هو نافع لأنه ضد الشر

BURSEVI:v1p233#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p233#2/r4.speaker: إخوان الصفا
BURSEVI:v1p233#2/r4.claim: The Brethren of Purity define good as doing what ought to be done, at the right time, for the right reason.
BURSEVI:v1p233#2/r4.anchor: قال في "إخوان الصفا" الخير فعل ما ينبغي في الوقت

BURSEVI:v1p233#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p233#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p233#2/r5.claim: Al-wasiyya is the passive subject of “was prescribed,” meaning that making a bequest was enjoined.
BURSEVI:v1p233#2/r5.anchor: نائب فاعل كتب أي : فرض الإيصاء

BURSEVI:v1p233#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p233#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p233#2/r6.claim: The recipients are parents and close relatives, whether or not they inherit.

BURSEVI:v1p233#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p233#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p233#2/r7.claim: A fair bequest should not exceed a third, favor the rich while leaving the poor, or violate justice.
BURSEVI:v1p233#2/r7.anchor: بالعدل لا يزيد على الثلث ولا يوصي لغني ويدع الفقير

BURSEVI:v1p233#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p233#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p233#2/r8.claim: In pre-Islamic custom, people bequeathed to distant outsiders for show and prestige while leaving close relatives poor; early Islam redirected those bequests to parents and relatives.
BURSEVI:v1p233#2/r8.anchor: وكان السبب في نزول هذه الآية أن أهل الجاهلية كانوا يوصون بمالهم للبعدى رياء وسمعة طلبا للفخر والشرف

BURSEVI:v1p233#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p233#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p233#2/r9.claim: The bequest ruling applied when it served justice and wisdom, then was abrogated by the inheritance verse in Surat al-Nisa; bequests are no longer obligatory and may go to non-heirs, but not heirs.
BURSEVI:v1p233#2/r9.anchor: فعمل بها ما كان العمل بها صلاحا وحكمة ثم نسختها آية المواريث في سورة النساء فالآن لا يجب على أحد أن يوصي لأحد قريب ولا بعيد

BURSEVI:v1p233#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p233#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p233#2/r10.claim: The obligation protects wealth from waste and relatives from deprivation; those who truly fear God should not abandon this practice as originally prescribed.

BURSEVI:v1p233#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p233#2/r11.speaker: ابن الشيخ
BURSEVI:v1p233#2/r11.claim: Ibn al-Shaykh answers that the phrase does not restrict the duty to already pious people; it means the duty binds everyone who chooses and pursues piety.
BURSEVI:v1p233#2/r11.anchor: قال ابن الشيخ في "حواشيه" : فإن قيل قوله : على المتقين يقتضي

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:180/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:180/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:180/r1.claim: “When death comes” means when its causes have arrived and its signs have appeared.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:180/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:180/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:180/r2.claim: One explanation takes “good” to mean wealth generally; another takes it to mean substantial wealth.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:180/r2.anchor: وقيل مالا كثيرا، لما روي عن علي رضي الله تعالى عنه

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:180/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:180/r3.speaker: علي
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:180/r3.claim: Ali stopped a client with 700 dirhams from making a bequest, arguing that “good” means substantial wealth.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:180/r3.anchor: عن علي رضي الله تعالى عنه: أن مولى له أراد أن يوصي وله سبعمائة درهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:180/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:180/r4.speaker: عائشة
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:180/r4.claim: Aisha told a man with 3,000 dirhams and four dependents that this was little and should be left to his family.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:180/r4.anchor: وعن عائشة رضي الله تعالى عنها: أن رجلا أراد أن يوصي فسألته كم مالك

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:180/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:180/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:180/r5.claim: Al-waṣiyya is nominative as the subject of kutiba; the feminine verb is separated from its subject, or construed with an omitted “to bequeath” or al-īṣāʾ, matching the pronoun in “whoever changes it.”
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:180/r5.anchor: مرفوع بكتب، وتذكير فعلها للفصل، أو على تأويل أن يوصي

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:180/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:180/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:180/r6.claim: The conditional time expression depends on the meaning of kutiba, not on al-waṣiyya, which follows it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:180/r6.anchor: والعامل في إذا مدلول كتب لا الوصية لتقدمه عليها.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:180/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:180/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:180/r7.claim: The alternative makes al-waṣiyya a subject with “for parents” as predicate and supplies a conditional answer without fa; al-Bayḍāwī rejects it as valid only by poetic necessity.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:180/r7.anchor: وقيل مبتدأ خبره { للولدين } ، والجملة جواب الشرط بإضمار الفاء

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:180/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:180/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:180/r8.claim: The alternative syntax is illustrated by two poetic lines about God rewarding good deeds and requiting evil.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:180/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:180/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:180/r9.claim: A view held that this early Islamic bequest rule was abrogated by inheritance verses and the Prophetic rule that heirs receive no bequest.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:180/r9.anchor: وكان هذا الحكم في بدء الإسلام فنسخ بآية المواريث

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:180/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:180/r10.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:180/r10.claim: The Prophet said God has given each rightful person their due and that no bequest is for an heir.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:180/r10.anchor: " إن الله أعطى كل ذي حق حقه، ألا لا وصية لوارث ".

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:180/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:180/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:180/r11.claim: Al-Bayḍāwī questions abrogation: inheritance rules do not contradict the verse and can confirm priority for bequests; the solitary hadith does not become mass-transmitted merely through communal acceptance.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:180/r11.anchor: وفيه نظر: لأن آية المواريث لا تعارضه بل تؤكده

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:180/r12.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:180/r12.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:180/r12.claim: To avoid conflict, al-waṣiyya may mean God’s command that parents and relatives inherit, or the dying person’s allocation of what God prescribed for them.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:180/r12.anchor: من فسر الوصية بما أوصى به الله من توريث الوالدين والأقربين

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:180/r13.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:180/r13.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:180/r13.claim: Bequests should be just: do not favor the wealthy and do not exceed one-third of the estate.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:180/r13.anchor: بالعدل فلا يفضل الغنى، ولا يتجاوز الثلث.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:180/r14.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:180/r14.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:180/r14.claim: Ḥaqqan is an emphatic verbal noun, meaning that this is truly obligatory.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:180/r14.anchor: { حقا على المتقين } مصدر مؤكد أي حق ذلك حقا.

BIQAI-FULL:v1p333/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p333/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p333/r7.claim: After urging the giving of wealth and then life through retaliation, the passage urges bequest of wealth near death, when worldly poverty is no longer feared and afterlife reward is hoped for.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p333/r7.anchor: أتبع ذلك بذله في حال الإشراف على النقلة والأمن من فقر الدنيا والرجاء لغنى الآخرة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p333/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p333/r8.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p333/r8.claim: Al-Ḥarālī connects the sequence to graded spiritual education: the preceding passages address those hoping to attain taqwā, then raise the address to what is due of the already pious; the mention of death in retaliation leads to bequest at death.
