BIQAI-FULL:v1p333/r8.anchor: ولما كان في الخطاب السابق ذكر القتل والقصاص الذي هو حال حضرة الموت انتظم به ذكر الوصية

BIQAI-FULL:v1p333/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p333/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p333/r9.claim: Bequest was initially obligatory, as the emphatic phrase indicates, then inheritance rules abrogated that duty for inheriting relatives while leaving bequest permissible in other cases.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p333/r9.anchor: ثم نسخ بآية المواريث وجوبه فبقي جوازه , وبينت السنة أن الإرث والوصية لا يجتمعان

BIQAI-FULL:v1p333/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p333/r10.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v1p333/r10.claim: The Prophet said that God assigned each right-holder their due and that there is no bequest for an heir; Aḥmad and the four collections transmit it from ʿAmr b. Khārija and Abū Umāma.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p333/r10.anchor: فقال صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( إن الله سبحانه وتعالى أعطى كل ذي حق حقه فلا وصية لوارث ) رواه أحمد

BIQAI-FULL:v1p333/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p333/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p333/r11.claim: Death’s arrival means the approach of its causes and signs.

BIQAI-FULL:v1p333/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p333/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p333/r12.claim: Khayr here is property that can be bequeathed, whether little or much; Biqāʿī cites 28:24 as an example of the word for a small amount.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p333/r12.anchor: أي ما لا ينبغي أن يوصى فيه قليلا كان أو كثيرا , أما إطلاقه على الكثير فكثير

BIQAI-FULL:v1p335/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p335/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p335/r1.claim: Parents are named first because of their honor and the magnitude of their right.

BIQAI-FULL:v1p335/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p335/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p335/r2.claim: Bequests to other close relatives must follow recognized fairness, with just distribution according to what people know as equitable.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p335/r2.anchor: أي العدل الذي يتعارفه الناس في التسوية والتفضيل

BIQAI-FULL:v1p335/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p335/r3.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p335/r3.claim: Al-Ḥarālī defines maʿrūf as what people’s souls accept without aversion.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p335/r3.anchor: والمعروف ما تقبله الأنفس ولا تجد منه تكرها

BIQAI-FULL:v1p335/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p335/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p335/r4.claim: The emphasis in ḥaqqan and ʿalā al-muttaqīn stirs hearers to obey and reminds them of their coming account before God.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p335/r4.anchor: وأكد الوجوب بقوله : { حقا } وكذا قوله : { على المتقين * } فهو إلهاب وتهييج وتذكير

DURR-FULL:v1p422/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p422/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p422/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses khayr as wealth.
DURR-FULL:v1p422/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {إن ترك خيرا} قال: مالا

DURR-FULL:v1p422/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p422/r6.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v1p422/r6.claim: Mujahid says khayr means wealth throughout the Quran, citing 100:8, 38:32, and 24:33.
DURR-FULL:v1p422/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد قال: الخير في القرآن كله المال {إن ترك خيرا} (لحب الخير) (العاديات الآية 8)

DURR-FULL:v1p422/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p422/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p422/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says someone leaving fewer than sixty dinars has not left enough wealth to count as khayr.
DURR-FULL:v1p422/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {إن ترك خيرا الوصية} قال: من لم يترك ستين دينار لم يترك خيرا

DURR-FULL:v1p422/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p422/r8.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
DURR-FULL:v1p422/r8.claim: Ali advised a dying client with only six or seven hundred dirhams not to make a bequest, since he lacked substantial wealth and should leave it to his heirs.
DURR-FULL:v1p422/r8.anchor: عن عروة أن علي بن أبي طالب دخل على مولى لهم في الموت وله سبعمائة درهم أو ستمائة درهم

DURR-FULL:v1p422/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p422/r9.speaker: عائشة
DURR-FULL:v1p422/r9.claim: Aisha first asked a man who wanted to bequeath how much property he owned.
DURR-FULL:v1p422/r9.anchor: عن عائشة أن رجلا قال لها: إني أريد أن أوصي قالت: كم مالك

DURR-FULL:v1p423/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p423/r1.speaker: عائشة
DURR-FULL:v1p423/r1.claim: Aisha considered three thousand a small estate for a man with four dependents and advised leaving it to them.
DURR-FULL:v1p423/r1.anchor: قال: ثلاثة آلاف قالت: كم عيالك قال: أربعة قالت: قال الله {إن ترك خيرا} وهذا شيء يسير فاتركه لعيالك فهو أفضل

DURR-FULL:v1p423/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p423/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p423/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says a person whose estate is seven hundred dirhams should not make a bequest.
DURR-FULL:v1p423/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: إن ترك الميت سبعمائة درهم فلا يوصي

DURR-FULL:v1p423/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p423/r3.speaker: أبو مجلز
DURR-FULL:v1p423/r3.claim: Abu Mujliz says the bequest applies to someone who leaves wealth.
DURR-FULL:v1p423/r3.anchor: عن أبي مجلز قال: الوصية على من ترك خيرا

DURR-FULL:v1p423/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p423/r4.speaker: الزهري
DURR-FULL:v1p423/r4.claim: Al-Zuhri says God made bequest a right whether the estate is small or large.
DURR-FULL:v1p423/r4.anchor: عن الزهري قال: جعل الله الوصية حقا مما قل منه أو كثر

DURR-FULL:v1p423/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p423/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
DURR-FULL:v1p423/r5.claim: The Prophet says a Muslim should not let three nights pass without keeping a will ready; Ibn Umar always kept his will ready.
DURR-FULL:v1p423/r5.anchor: عن ابن عمر قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول ما حق امرىء مسلم تمر عليه ثلاث ليال إلا وصيته عنده

DURR-FULL:v1p423/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p423/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v1p423/r6.claim: In a sermon relayed by Qatada, the Prophet warns against withholding God's due during life and then distributing wealth at death.
DURR-FULL:v1p423/r6.anchor: عن قتادة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أيها الناس ابتاعوا أنفسكم من ربكم

DURR-FULL:v1p423/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p423/r7.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v1p423/r7.claim: Qatada urges people to consider needy relatives who do not inherit and bequeath to them equitably.
DURR-FULL:v1p423/r7.anchor: ثم يقول قتادة: ويلك يا ابن آدم اتق الله ولا تجمع إساءتين مالك إساءة في الحياة

DURR-FULL:v1p423/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p423/r8.speaker: عبيد الله بن عبد الله بن معمر
DURR-FULL:v1p423/r8.claim: Ubayd Allah ibn Abd Allah ibn Ma'mar says named beneficiaries receive a bequest; if the will says to place it where God commanded, it goes to relatives.
DURR-FULL:v1p423/r8.anchor: عن عبيد الله بن عبد الله بن معمر قاضي البصرة قال: من أوصى فسمى أعطينا من سمى

DURR-FULL:v1p423/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p423/r9.speaker: طاوس
DURR-FULL:v1p423/r9.claim: Tawus says a bequest to named people is taken back for needy relatives if those relatives were left out.
DURR-FULL:v1p423/r9.anchor: عن طاوس قال: من أوصى لقوم وسماهم وترك ذوي قرابته محتاجين

DURR-FULL:v1p423/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p423/r10.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v1p423/r10.claim: Al-Hasan says if a bequest to non-relatives is one third, they get one third of it and the other two thirds return to relatives.
DURR-FULL:v1p423/r10.anchor: عن الحسن قال: إذا أوصى في غير أقاربه بالثلث جاز لهم ثلث الثلث

DURR-FULL:v1p423/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p423/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p423/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas said this verse had been abrogated while explaining the sura; al-Hakim authenticated the report.
DURR-FULL:v1p423/r11.anchor: عن محمد بن سيرين قال: خطب ابن عباس فقرأ سورة البقرة فبين ما فيها حتى مر على هذه الآية

DURR-FULL:v1p424/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p424/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p424/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says children inherited while parents received a bequest; the inheritance verse in 4:7 abrogated the bequest for parents.
DURR-FULL:v1p424/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في الوصية {للوالدين والأقربين} قال: كان ولد الرجل يرثونه وللوالدين الوصية

DURR-FULL:v1p424/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p424/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p424/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the inheritance verse detailed the parents' shares and retained a bequest of up to one third for relatives who did not inherit.
DURR-FULL:v1p424/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: كان لا يرث مع الوالدين غيرهما إلا وصية الأقربين فأنزل الله آية الميراث

DURR-FULL:v1p424/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p424/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p424/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says the bequest for parents and relatives applied until the inheritance verse superseded it.
DURR-FULL:v1p424/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {إن ترك خيرا الوصية للوالدين والأقربين} قال: فكانت الوصية لذلك حين نسختها آية الميراث

DURR-FULL:v1p424/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p424/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p424/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas distinguishes inheriting relatives, whose bequest was abrogated, from noninheriting relatives, whose bequest remained.
DURR-FULL:v1p424/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس في الآية قال: نسخ من يرث ولم ينسخ الأقربين الذين لا يرثون

DURR-FULL:v1p424/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p424/r5.speaker: ابن عمر
DURR-FULL:v1p424/r5.claim: Ibn Umar says the inheritance verse abrogated this bequest verse.
DURR-FULL:v1p424/r5.anchor: عن ابن عمر أنه سئل عن هذه الآية {الوصية للوالدين والأقربين} قال: نسختها آية الميراث

DURR-FULL:v1p424/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p424/r6.speaker: شريح
DURR-FULL:v1p424/r6.claim: Shurayh says a person used to be able to bequeath all his property until the inheritance verse was revealed.
DURR-FULL:v1p424/r6.anchor: عن قتادة عن شريح في الآية قال: كان الرجل يوصي بماله كله حتى نزلت آية الميراث

DURR-FULL:v1p424/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p424/r7.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v1p424/r7.claim: Mujahid says children received inheritance and parents and relatives received bequests, a rule later abrogated.
DURR-FULL:v1p424/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد في الآية قال: كان الميراث للولد والوصية للوالدين والأقربين فهي منسوخة

DURR-FULL:v1p424/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p424/r8.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v1p424/r8.claim: Qatada says khayr meant wealth, commonly a thousand or more; after parents were excluded and heirs received shares, bequests went to noninheriting relatives or others.
DURR-FULL:v1p424/r8.anchor: عن قتادة في الآية قال: الخير المال كان يقال ألف فما فوق ذلك فأمر أن يوصي

DURR-FULL:v1p424/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p424/r9.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v1p424/r9.claim: The Prophet says God allotted each person an inheritance share, so a bequest for an heir is invalid; al-Tirmidhi authenticated the report.
DURR-FULL:v1p424/r9.anchor: عن عمرو بن خارجة أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم خطبهم على راحلته فقال: إن الله قد قسم لكل إنسان نصيبه من الميراث

DURR-FULL:v1p424/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p424/r10.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v1p424/r10.claim: At the Farewell Pilgrimage, the Prophet said God gave each rightful person their due and there is no bequest for an heir.
DURR-FULL:v1p424/r10.anchor: عن أبي أمامة الباهلي سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في حجة الوداع في خطبته يقول: إن الله قد أعطى كل ذي حق حقه

IBNABIHATIM:v1p298/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p298/r1.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v1p298/r1.claim: Al-Hasan says every Muslim must make a proper, nonwrongful bequest when death approaches.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p298/r1.anchor: عن الحسن قوله : كتب عليكم اذا حضر احدكم الموت فقال : نعم الوصية حق على كل مسلم

IBNABIHATIM:v1p298/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p298/r2.speaker: علي
IBNABIHATIM:v1p298/r2.claim: Ali advised a man who asked about making a bequest that, since he had little, he should leave it to his children.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p298/r2.anchor: قال له علي : انما قال الله ان ترك خيرا الوصية وانك انما تركت شيئا يسيرا فاتركه لولدك .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p298/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p298/r3.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد، عبيدة، عطاء بن أبي رباح، أبو العالية، سعيد بن جبير، عطية، الضحاك، السدي، مقاتل بن حيان، الربيع بن أنس، قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v1p298/r3.claim: These authorities explain khayr as wealth, meaning an estate substantial enough to bequeath.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p298/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس : ان ترك خيرا يعني : مالا .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p298/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p298/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p298/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says someone leaving fewer than sixty dinars has not left khayr.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p298/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس ان ترك خيرا قال ابن عباس : من لم يترك ستين دينار لم يترك خيرا .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p298/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p298/r5.speaker: الحكم
IBNABIHATIM:v1p298/r5.claim: Al-Hakam sets the threshold at eighty dinars, saying a person who leaves less has not left khayr.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p298/r5.anchor: وقال الحكم : لم ترك خيرا من لم يترك ثمانين دينار .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p298/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p298/r6.speaker: علي
IBNABIHATIM:v1p298/r6.claim: Ali treated an estate of three or four hundred dinars without a bequest as not meeting the verse's condition of leaving khayr.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p298/r6.anchor: قيل لعلي : ان رجلا من قريش قد توفى وترك ثلاثمائة دينار أو اربعمائة دينار ولم يوص قال : ليس بشئ

IBNABIHATIM:v1p298/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p298/r7.speaker: قتادة؛ أبو محمد
IBNABIHATIM:v1p298/r7.claim: Qatada says khayr was conventionally a thousand or more; Abu Muhammad clarifies that the measure is dirhams.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p298/r7.anchor: سمعت قتادة : ان ترك خيرا قال : الخير : المال كان يقال : الفا فما فوقه قال : أبو محمد يعني : الف درهم .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p298/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p298/r8.speaker: ابن عباس، ابن عمر، أبو موسى الأشعري، سعيد بن المسيب، الحسن، مجاهد، عطاء، سعيد بن جبير، محمد بن سيرين، زيد بن أسلم، الربيع بن أنس، قتادة، السدي، مقاتل بن حيان، إبراهيم النخعي، الشيخ، الضحاك، الزهري
IBNABIHATIM:v1p298/r8.claim: They report that the bequest command was abrogated by the inheritance allocation in 4:7.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p298/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله الوصية للوالدين والاقربين فنسختها هذه الاية للرجال نصيب مما ترك الوالدان والاقربون

IBNABIHATIM:v1p300/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p300/r1.speaker: أبو العالية، سعيد بن جبير، الحسن، الربيع بن أنس، الضحاك، مقاتل بن حيان، الزهري، قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v1p300/r1.claim: The parents' bequest was abrogated because they became heirs; bequests remained for relatives who do not inherit.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p300/r1.anchor: عن أبي العالية قوله : الوصية للوالدين والاقربين قال : نسخ الوالدين فالحقهما بأهل الميراث وصارت الوصية لاهل القرابة الذين لا يرثون

IBNABIHATIM:v1p300/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p300/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v1p300/r2.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says this bequest is incumbent on the God-fearing.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p300/r2.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير في قول الله : بالمعروف حقا على المتقين يقول : تلك الوصية حق على المتقين .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p300/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p300/r3.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
IBNABIHATIM:v1p300/r3.claim: For Muqatil, the God-fearing means the believers.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p300/r3.anchor: عن مقاتل بن حيان قوله : حقا على المتقين يعني : المؤمنين .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p51#3/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p51#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p51#3/r1.claim: Early reciters in regions with Uthman’s codices read in local dialects; variation concerned performance forms, not added or omitted letters or readings against the codex’s grammar.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p51#3/r1.anchor: فقرأ كل فريق بعربية قومه في وجوه الأداء ، لا في زيادة الحروف ونقصها ، ولا في اختلاف الإعراب دون مخالفته مصحف عثمان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p51#3/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p51#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p51#3/r2.claim: A single reciter may transmit more than one Arabic form to preserve both language and Qur’an; many differences may reflect reader choice.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p51#3/r2.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون القارئ الواحد قد قرأ بوجهين ليرى صحتهما في العربية قصدا لحفظ اللغة مع حفظ القرآن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p51#3/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p51#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p51#3/r3.claim: Some criticisms of variant readings by al-Zamakhshari and Ibn al-ʿArabi merit consideration, though others are questionable.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p51#3/r3.anchor: وعليه يحمل ما يقع في كتابي الزمخشري وابن العربي من نقد بعض طرق القراء ، على أن في بعض نقدهم نظرا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p51#3/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p51#3/r4.speaker: مالك
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p51#3/r4.claim: Malik disliked imala despite its transmission from readers, including Nafiʿ through Warsh, whose report was distinctive to Egyptian transmitters.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p51#3/r4.anchor: وقد كره مالك رحمه الله القراءة بالإمالة مع ثبوتها عن القراء ، وهي مروية عن مقرئ المدينة نافع من رواية ورش عنه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p51#3/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p51#3/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p51#3/r5.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr infers from Malik’s dislike that Malik regarded imala as a reader’s discretionary choice.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p51#3/r5.anchor: فدلت كراهته على أنه يرى أن القارئ بها ما قرأ إلا بمجرد الاختيار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p51#3/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p51#3/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p51#3/r7.claim: He sees no harm in proposed pronunciations so long as Qur’anic words and sentences remain as written in the codex agreed by the Companions.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p51#3/r7.anchor: ولا ضير في ذلك ما دامت كلمات القرآن وجمله محفوظة على نحو ما كتب في المصحف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p51#3/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p51#3/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p51#3/r8.claim: Uthman required adherence to the codex recorded from the Prophet’s recitation, gathered and burned conflicting codices, and was supported by most Companions; Ibn Masʿud was among the few dissenters.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p51#3/r8.anchor: فإن عثمان لما أمر بكتب المصحف على نحو ما قرأ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ، وأثبته كتاب المصحف ، رأى أن يحمل الناس على اتباعه وترك قراءات ما خالفه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p51#3/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p51#3/r9.speaker: شمس الدين الأصفهاني
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p51#3/r9.claim: Al-Isfahani says Abu Bakr, ʿUmar, ʿUthman, Zayd, the Emigrants, and Helpers shared the public reading the Prophet recited to Gabriel in his final year; Zayd reportedly witnessed the final review.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p51#3/r9.anchor: قال الأصفهاني في تفسيره كانت قراءة أبي بكر وعمر وعثمان وزيد بن ثابت والمهاجرين والأنصار واحدة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p51#3/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p51#3/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p51#3/r10.claim: Uthman completed Abu Bakr’s collection by copying it into regional codices; consensus made this codex nearly universal and left conflicting readings abandoned by near-consensus.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p51#3/r10.anchor: إنما كان فعل عثمان إتماما لما فعله أبو بكر من جمعه القرآن الذي كان يقرأ في حياة الرسول ، وأن عثمان نسخه في مصاحف لتوزع على الأمصار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p51#3/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p51#3/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p51#3/r11.claim: Readers with variants outside Uthman’s codex continued to recite what they had received without prohibition, but were classed as anomalous and gradually stopped writing them in codices.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p51#3/r11.anchor: وبقى الذين قرأوا قراءات مخالفة لمصحف عثمان يقرأون بما رووه لا ينهاهم أحد عن قراءتهم ولكن يعدوهم شذاذا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p51#3/r14.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p51#3/r14.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p51#3/r14.claim: Variants contrary to Uthman’s codex were attributed to Ibn Masʿud, Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, and Salim, and were gradually relinquished.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p51#3/r14.anchor: وممن نسبت إليهم قراءات مخالفة لمصحف عثمان ، عبد الله بن مسعود وأبي بن كعب وسالم مولى أبي حذيفة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p51#3/r16.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p51#3/r16.speaker: الزمخشري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p51#3/r16.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says al-Harith ibn Suwayd, a companion of Ibn Masʿud, buried his codex during al-Hajjaj’s period because it differed from the authoritative codex.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p51#3/r16.anchor: ذكره الزمخشري في الكشاف في سورة الفتح أن الحارث بن سويد صاحب عبد الله بن مسعود كان له مصحف دفنه في مدة الحجاج

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p51#3/r17.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p51#3/r17.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p51#3/r17.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr says al-Zamakhshari went too far in weakening readings for violating grammarians’ conventions because he neglected their transmission chains.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p51#3/r17.anchor: وقد أفرط الزمخشري في توهين بعض القراءات لمخالفتها لما اصطلح عليه النجاة وذلك من إعراضه عن معرفة الأسانيد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p51#3/r18.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p51#3/r18.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p51#3/r18.claim: A sound reading must fit Arabic, agree with Uthman’s codex, and have a sound transmission; specialists agree it cannot be rejected.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p51#3/r18.anchor: من أجل ذلك اتفق علماء القراءات والفقهاء على أن كل قراءة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p51#3/r19.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p51#3/r19.speaker: أبو بكر ابن العربي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p51#3/r19.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabi says mass transmission of a reading follows that of the codex it matches; readings that fail this are anomalous.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p51#3/r19.anchor: قال أبو بكر ابن العربي : ومعنى ذلك عندي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p51#3/r20.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p51#3/r20.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p51#3/r20.claim: The codex itself is mass-transmitted through the wording it contains, explaining the transmission status of readings that conform to it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p51#3/r20.anchor: يعني وأن تواتر المصحف ناشئ عن تواتر الألفاظ التي كتبت فيه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247/r1.claim: The testament verse connects syntactically to the preceding “يا أيها الذين آمنوا,” explaining the missing conjunction.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247/r1.anchor: كأن الآية متصلة بقوله يا أيها الذين آمنوا فلذلك سقطت واو العطف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247/r2.claim: “كُتِبَ” means imposed and established, and the wording suggests the rule was written from eternity.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247/r3.speaker: بعض أهل العلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247/r3.claim: Some scholars held that making a will was obligatory.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247/r3.anchor: وقال بعض أهل العلم: الوصية فرض،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247/r4.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247/r4.claim: Some held that making a will had been obligatory but was abrogated.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247/r5.speaker: فريق
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247/r5.claim: Others treated making a will as recommended.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247/r6.claim: One parsing makes “الوصية” the passive subject governed by “كتب.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247/r6.anchor: وكتب عامل في رفع الوصية على المفعول الذي لم يسم فاعله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247/r7.claim: The feminine marker is omitted from “كتب” because the intervening phrase is long; Sibawayh allows “قام امرأة,” especially with long separation.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247/r8.speaker: جمهور النحاة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247/r8.claim: Most grammarians reject making “الوصية” govern the following “إذا”: it is in the source noun’s complement and cannot be governed from before it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247/r8.anchor: ولا يصح عند جمهور النحاة أن تعمل الوصية في إذا لأنها في حكم الصلة للمصدر الذي هو الوصية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247/r9.claim: One parsing makes “كتب” govern “إذا,” meaning God's prescription takes effect at death; “الوصية” is passive subject and both conditional responses are understood from “كتب عليكم.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247/r9.anchor: ويتجه في إعراب هذه الآية أن يكون كتب هو العامل في إذا والمعنى توجه إيجاب الله عليكم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247/r10.claim: Another parsing supplies “الإيصاء,” which governs “إذا”; “الوصية” is a subject, and the conditional responses are understood as above.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247/r10.anchor: أن يكون التقدير: كتب عليكم الإيصاء، ويكون هذا الإيصاء المقدر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247/r11.claim: The verbal-noun parsing raises “الوصية” as subject, with an implied “فعليه الوصية” or an understood ف.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247/r11.anchor: أنشد سيبويه: [البسيط] من يفعل الصالحات الله يحفظها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247#2/r1.claim: The continuation gives al-Akhfash's example: “بالرحا” attaches to “المتقاعس,” as though the wording were “أبعلي هذا المتقاعس بالرحا.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247#2/r1.anchor: تقول وصكت وجهها بيمينها ... أبعلي هذا بالرحا المتقاعس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247#2/r2.claim: The poem illustrates the parsing in which “بالرحا” modifies “المتقاعس.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247#2/r2.anchor: فإنه يرى أن «بالرحا» متعلق بقوله المتقاعس، كأنه قال: أبعلي هذا المتقاعس بالرحا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247#2/r3.claim: “When death comes” is figurative: it means when a person fears death and its signs appear.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247#2/r3.anchor: وفي قوله تعالى إذا حضر مجاز لأن المعنى إذا تخوف وحضرت علاماته

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247#2/r5.speaker: الزهري وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247#2/r5.claim: Some jurists set no minimum estate amount; a will was required for little or much.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247#2/r5.anchor: فقال الزهري وغيره: تجب فيما قل وفيما كثر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247#2/r6.speaker: النخعي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247#2/r6.claim: Al-Nakha'i required a will only for an estate of five hundred dirhams or more.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247#2/r6.anchor: وقال النخعي: تجب في خمسمائة درهم فصاعدا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247#2/r7.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب وقتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247#2/r7.claim: Ali and Qatada set the minimum estate at one thousand dirhams.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247#2/r7.anchor: وقال علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه وقتادة: في ألف فصاعدا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247#2/r8.speaker: فريق
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247#2/r8.claim: One view keeps the verse generally operative but limits it to non-inheriting parents and relatives.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247#2/r8.anchor: فقال فريق: محكمة ظاهرها العموم ومعناها الخصوص في الوالدين اللذين لا يرثان

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن وقتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247#2/r9.claim: They say the verse first applied generally, then inheritance shares abrogated it for heirs; non-inheriting relatives remain eligible, and some of the view excludes parents.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247#2/r9.anchor: وقال ابن عباس والحسن وقتادة: الآية عامة وتقرر الحكم بها برهة ونسخ منها كل من يرث

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247#2/r10.speaker: ابن عمر وابن عباس وابن زيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247#2/r10.claim: They hold the whole verse was abrogated, leaving wills recommended; Malik has a similar view, as do those who say there is no bequest to an heir.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247#2/r10.anchor: وقال ابن عمر وابن عباس أيضا وابن زيد: الآية كلها منسوخة وبقيت الوصية ندبا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247#2/r11.claim: When Urwa asked al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym to bequeath him a codex, al-Rabi' pointed to his son and cited 33:6; Ibn Umar acted similarly.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247#2/r11.anchor: وقال عروة بن ثابت للربيع بن خثيم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247#2/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247#2/r12.claim: The inheritance verse in Surat al-Nisa is said to abrogate this verse; a mass-transmitted report says God assigned each rights-holder a due and there is no bequest to an heir.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247#2/r12.anchor: وبين أن آية الفرائض في سورة النساء ناسخة، لهذا الحديث المتواتر: «إن الله قد أعطى كل ذي حق حقه فلا وصية لوارث»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247#2/r13.speaker: بعض أهل العلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247#2/r13.claim: Some say the abrogating proof is the mass-transmitted Sunna report; Ibn Atiyya discusses Sunna abrogating scripture at 2:106.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247#2/r13.anchor: وقال بعض أهل العلم: إن الناسخ لهذه الآية هي السنة المتواترة في الحديث المذكور قبل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247#2/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247#2/r14.speaker: قوم من العلماء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247#2/r14.claim: Some scholars prioritize bequests to relatives; if relatives are left out, a bequest to a stranger cannot stand.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p247#2/r14.anchor: وقال قوم من العلماء: الوصية للقرابة أولى فإن كانت لأجنبي فمعهم ولا تجوز لغيرهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p248/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p248/r1.speaker: الناس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p248/r1.claim: At Abu al-Aliya's death, people marveled that a woman from Riyah freed him but he left property to the Banu Hashim.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p248/r1.anchor: وقال الناس حين مات أبو العالية: عجبا له أعتقته امرأة من رياح وأوصى بماله لبني هاشم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p248/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p248/r2.speaker: الشعبي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p248/r2.claim: Al-Sha'bi objected that Abu al-Aliya had no right to make that bequest.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p248/r2.anchor: وقال الشعبي: «لم يكن ذلك له ولا كرامة»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p248/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p248/r3.speaker: طاوس وجابر بن زيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p248/r3.claim: Tawus and Jabir ibn Zayd would redirect a bequest to non-relatives to the testator's relatives and annul it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p248/r3.anchor: وقال طاوس: «إذا أوصى لغير قرابة ردت الوصية إلى قرابته ونقض فعله» وقاله جابر بن زيد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p248/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p248/r4.speaker: الحسن وجابر بن زيد وعبد الملك بن يعلى
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p248/r4.claim: They allow one third to stand as designated and return two thirds to relatives.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p248/r4.anchor: وقال الحسن وجابر بن زيد أيضا وعبد الملك بن يعلى: يبقى ثلث الوصية حيث جعلها ويرد ثلثاها إلى قرابته

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p248/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p248/r5.speaker: مالك وجماعة من العلماء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p248/r5.claim: Malik and other scholars hold that a will remains valid wherever the deceased directed it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p248/r5.anchor: وقال مالك رحمه الله وجماعة من العلماء: الوصية ماضية حيث جعلها الميت

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p248/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p248/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p248/r7.claim: “بالمعروف” means a customary, moderate amount, without harming heirs or dissipating the bequest wastefully.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p248/r7.anchor: وبالمعروف معناه بالقصد الذي تعرفه النفوس دون إضرار بالورثة ولا تبذير للوصية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p248/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p248/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p248/r8.anchor: وحقا مصدر مؤكد، وخص المتقون بالذكر تشريفا للرتبة ليتبادر الناس إليها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p248/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p248/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p248/r9.claim: The verse singles out the God-fearing to honor their rank and encourage people to follow it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p248/r9.anchor: وخص المتقون بالذكر تشريفا للرتبة ليتبادر الناس إليها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p181#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p181#3/r1.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p181#3/r1.claim: Al-Zajjāj supplies an implied ‘and’: the phrase means ‘and it is prescribed for you’; after a long passage, the conjunction can be omitted when understood.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p181#3/r1.anchor: قال الزجاج المعنى وكتب عليكم إلا أن الكلام إذا طال استغنى عن العطف بالواو

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p181#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p181#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p181#3/r2.claim: The obligation is not to make a will at the moment of death, but while capable and to state beforehand what should go to whom after death.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p181#3/r2.anchor: وليس المراد كتب عليكم أن يوصي احدكم عند الموت لأنه في شغل حينئذ وإنما المعنى كتب علكيم أن توصوا وأنتم قادرون على الوصية

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p181#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p181#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p181#3/r3.claim: The scholars collectively take khayr here to mean wealth.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p181#3/r3.anchor: فأما الخير هاهنا فهو المال في قول الجماعة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p181#3/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p181#3/r4.speaker: علي وقتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p181#3/r4.claim: One view sets the minimum wealth for a will at one thousand dirhams.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p181#3/r4.anchor: أحدها أنه ألف درهم فصاعدا روي عن علي وقتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p181#3/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p181#3/r5.speaker: طاووس عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p181#3/r5.claim: A view transmitted by Ṭāwūs from Ibn ʿAbbās sets the threshold at seven hundred dirhams or more.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p181#3/r5.anchor: والثاني أنه سبعمائة درهم فما فوقها رواه طاووس عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p181#3/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p181#3/r6.speaker: عكرمة عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p181#3/r6.claim: A view transmitted by ʿIkrima from Ibn ʿAbbās sets the threshold at sixty dinars or more.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p181#3/r6.anchor: والثالث ستون دينار فما فوقها رواه عكرمة عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p181#3/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p181#3/r7.speaker: عائشة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p181#3/r7.claim: ʿĀʾisha told a man with three thousand dirhams and four dependents that this was a small amount and should be left for his family.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p181#3/r7.anchor: قالت عائشة لرجل سألها إني أريد الوصية فقالت كم مالك قال ثلاثة آلاف قالت كم عيالك قال أربعة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p181#3/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p181#3/r8.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p181#3/r8.claim: Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī places the relevant amount between one thousand and five hundred dirhams.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p181#3/r8.anchor: والخامس أنه من ألف درهم إلى خمسمائة قاله إبراهيم النخعي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p181#3/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p181#3/r9.speaker: معمر عن الزهري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p181#3/r9.claim: A report from Maʿmar via al-Zuhrī says the will applies to wealth, little or much.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p181#3/r9.anchor: والسادس أنه القليل والكثير رواه معمر عن الزهري

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p181#3/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p181#3/r10.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p181#3/r10.claim: Bi-l-maʿrūf means in a manner involving no injustice.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p181#3/r10.anchor: فأما المعروف فهو الذي لا حيف فيه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p181#3/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p181#3/r11.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p181#3/r11.claim: One opinion held that making the will was recommended rather than obligatory.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p181#3/r11.anchor: وهل كانت الوصية ندبا أو واجبة فيه قولان أحدهما أنها كانت ندبا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p181#3/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p181#3/r12.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p181#3/r12.claim: The stronger opinion is that the will was obligatory, because kutiba means that it was prescribed as a duty.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p181#3/r12.anchor: والثاني أنها كانت فرضا وهو أصح لقوله تعالى ﴿ كتب ﴾ ومعناه فرض

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p181#3/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p181#3/r13.speaker: ابن عمر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p181#3/r13.claim: Ibn ʿUmar says the verse was abrogated by the inheritance verse.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p181#3/r13.anchor: قال ابن عمر نسخت هذه الآية بآية الميرات

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p181#3/r14.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p181#3/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p181#3/r14.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says it was abrogated by the inheritance rule, ‘Men have a share of what parents and near relatives leave’ (4:7).
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p181#3/r14.anchor: وقال ابن عباس نسختها ﴿ للرجال نصيب مما ترك الوالدان والأقربون ﴾ النساء 7

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p181#3/r15.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p181#3/r15.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p181#3/r15.claim: Scholars agree that the bequest for parents and near relatives who inherit has been abrogated.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p181#3/r15.anchor: والعلماء متفقون على نسخ الوصية للوالدين والأقربين الذين يرثون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p181#3/r16.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p181#3/r16.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p181#3/r16.claim: Scholars differ over whether a bequest is obligatory for relatives who do not inherit; one view says it is.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p181#3/r16.anchor: وهم مختلفون في الأقربين الذين لا يرثون هل تجب الوصية لهم على قولين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p181#3/r17.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p181#3/r17.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p181#3/r17.claim: The sounder view is that a will is not obligatory for any non-inheriting relative.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p181#3/r17.anchor: على قولين اصحهما أنها لا تجب لأحد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p492#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p492#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p492#2/r1.claim: On the stronger of two views, bequests to parents and relatives were obligatory before the inheritance verses; fixed inheritance shares abrogated the duty for heirs, who now take their divinely set shares without a bequest or the testator's favor.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p492#2/r1.anchor: وقد كان ذلك واجبا -على أصح القولين -قبل نزول آية المواريث، فلما نزلت آية الفرائض نسخت هذه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p492#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p492#2/r2.speaker: النبي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p492#2/r2.claim: The Prophet says God has given each rights-holder their due, so an heir may not receive a bequest.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p492#2/r2.anchor: ولهذا جاء الحديث في السنن وغيرها عن عمرو بن خارجة قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يخطب وهو يقول: "إن الله قد أعطى كل ذي حق حقه، فلا وصية لوارث"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p492#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p492#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p492#2/r3.claim: After reciting the verse, Ibn Abbas said it had been abrogated; al-Hakim graded this report authentic on the two authorities' criteria.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p492#2/r3.anchor: فقال: نسخت هذه الآية. وكذا رواه سعيد بن منصور

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p492#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p492#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p492#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says that initially only parents inherited alongside one another, while other relatives received by bequest; the inheritance verse set the parents' shares and preserved a bequest for relatives from one-third of the estate.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p492#2/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {الوصية للوالدين والأقربين} قال: كان لا يرث مع الوالدين غيرهما إلا وصية للأقربين، فأنزل الله آية الميراث

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p492#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p492#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p492#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas, via Ata, says this bequest verse was abrogated by the inheritance ruling in 4:7.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p492#2/r5.anchor: عن عطاء، عن ابن عباس، في قوله: {الوصية للوالدين والأقربين} نسختها هذه الآية: {للرجال نصيب مما ترك الوالدان والأقربون

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p492#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p492#2/r6.speaker: ابن عمر وأبو موسى وسعيد بن المسيب والحسن ومجاهد وعطاء وسعيد بن جبير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p492#2/r6.claim: Ibn Abi Hatim lists Ibn Umar, Abu Musa, Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib, Hasan, Mujahid, Ata, and Saʿid ibn Jubayr as holding that inheritance verses abrogated this verse.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p492#2/r6.anchor: وروي عن ابن عمر (4) وأبي موسى، وسعيد بن المسيب، والحسن، ومجاهد، وعطاء، وسعيد بن جبير، ومحمد بن سيرين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p492#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p492#2/r7.speaker: محمد بن سيرين وعكرمة وزيد بن أسلم والربيع بن أنس وقتادة والسدي ومقاتل بن حيان
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p492#2/r7.claim: Ibn Abi Hatim also lists Ibn Sirin, Ikrima, Zayd ibn Aslam, al-Rabi, Qatada, al-Suddi, and Muqatil ibn Hayyan as holding that inheritance verses abrogated this verse.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p492#2/r7.anchor: ومحمد بن سيرين، وعكرمة، وزيد بن أسلم، والربيع بن أنس، وقتادة، والسدي، ومقاتل بن حيان

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p492#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p492#2/r8.speaker: طاوس وإبراهيم النخعي وشريح والضحاك والزهري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p492#2/r8.claim: Ibn Abi Hatim also lists Tawus, Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿi, Shurayh, al-Dahhak, and al-Zuhri as holding that inheritance verses abrogated this verse.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p492#2/r8.anchor: وطاوس، وإبراهيم النخعي، وشريح، والضحاك، والزهري: أن هذه الآية منسوخة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p493/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p493/r1.speaker: أبو مسلم الأصفهاني
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p493/r1.claim: Abu Muslim says the verse was not abrogated but explains inheritance legislation, glossing it as God's prescription for inheriting parents and relatives under 4:11; al-Razi says this is the view of most commentators and recognized jurists, which Ibn Kathir finds surprising.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p493/r1.anchor: عن أبي مسلم الأصفهاني (6) أن هذه الآية غير منسوخة، وإنما هي مفسرة بآية المواريث

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p493/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p493/r2.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن ومسروق وطاوس والضحاك ومسلم بن يسار والعلاء بن زياد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p493/r2.claim: A reported middle view abrogates bequests for relatives who inherit but preserves them for those who do not; Ibn Abbas, Hasan, Masruq, Tawus, al-Dahhak, Muslim ibn Yasar, and al-Ala ibn Ziyad hold it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p493/r2.anchor: قال: ومنهم من قال: إنها منسوخة فيمن يرث، ثابتة فيمن لا يرث، وهو مذهب ابن عباس، والحسن، ومسروق، وطاوس

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p493/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p493/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير والربيع بن أنس وقتادة ومقاتل بن حيان
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p493/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir adds Saʿid ibn Jubayr, al-Rabi, Qatada, and Muqatil ibn Hayyan to those holding that bequests were abrogated for heirs but remained for non-heirs.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p493/r3.anchor: قلت: وبه قال أيضا سعيد بن جبير، والربيع بن أنس، وقتادة، ومقاتل بن حيان

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p493/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p493/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p493/r4.claim: In later technical usage, the partial view is specification, not abrogation: inheritance law removes heirs from the general term relatives while non-inheriting relatives remain covered; this fits those who regard the original bequest as recommended.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p493/r4.anchor: لأن "الأقربين" أعم ممن يرث ومن (9) لا يرث، فرفع حكم من يرث بما عين له

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p493/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p493/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p493/r5.claim: Because the verse's context indicates an obligatory bequest, the author sides with the majority: bequests to inheriting relatives are abrogated by inheritance law and forbidden by the no-bequest-for-an-heir hadith.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p493/r5.anchor: فأما من يقول: إنها كانت واجبة وهو الظاهر من سياق الآية -فيتعين أن تكون منسوخة بآية الميراث

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p493/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p493/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p493/r6.claim: Inheritance law is an independent divine obligation for fixed-share heirs and residuaries, replacing the earlier ruling; bequests for non-inheriting relatives remain recommended from one-third, supported by this verse and the Prophet's instruction to keep a written will.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p493/r6.anchor: بقي الأقارب الذين لا ميراث لهم، يستحب له أن يوصى لهم من الثلث، استئناسا بآية الوصية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p493/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p493/r7.speaker: النبي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p493/r7.claim: The Prophet says a Muslim with something to bequeath should not spend two nights without a written will; Ibn Umar says he always kept one after hearing this.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p493/r7.anchor: عن ابن عمر، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "ما حق امرئ مسلم له شيء يوصي فيه، يبيت ليلتين إلا ووصيته مكتوبة عنده".

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p494/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p494/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p494/r1.claim: Many verses and hadiths command kindness and benevolence toward relatives.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p494/r1.anchor: والآيات والأحاديث بالأمر ببر الأقارب والإحسان إليهم، كثيرة جدا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p494/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p494/r2.speaker: النبي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p494/r2.claim: A report from the Prophet has God tell Adam's child that He granted a share of wealth at death to purify him and His servants' prayer follows after death.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p494/r2.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "يقول الله تعالى: يا ابن آدم، ثنتان لم يكن لك واحدة منهما: جعلت لك نصيبا في مالك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p494/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p494/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p494/r3.claim: Here khayr means wealth; Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ata, Saʿid ibn Jubayr, Abu al-Aliya, Atiyya al-Awfi, al-Dahhak, al-Suddi, al-Rabi, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, Qatada, and others are cited for this gloss.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p494/r3.anchor: وقوله: {إن ترك خيرا} أي: مالا. قاله ابن عباس، ومجاهد، وعطاء، وسعيد بن جبير

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p494/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p494/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p494/r4.claim: Authorities differ on whether a bequest applies regardless of the estate's size or only when substantial wealth is left.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p494/r4.anchor: ثم منهم من قال: الوصية مشروعة سواء قل المال أو كثر كالوراثة (4) ومنهم من قال: إنما يوصي إذا ترك مالا جزيلا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p494/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p494/r5.speaker: علي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p494/r5.claim: Ali considers 300 or 400 dinars too little to count as substantial wealth for a bequest, and advises a man with little to leave it to his children.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p494/r5.anchor: قال: ليس بشيء، إنما قال الله: {إن ترك خيرا}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p494/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p494/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p494/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says one who leaves less than sixty dinars has not left substantial wealth.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p494/r6.anchor: عن عكرمة، عن ابن عباس: {إن ترك خيرا} قال ابن عباس: من لم يترك ستين دينارا لم يترك خيرا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p494/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p494/r7.speaker: طاوس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p494/r7.claim: Tawus sets the threshold at eighty dinars; Qatada transmits the saying that it was one thousand or more.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p494/r7.anchor: قال طاوس: لم يترك خيرا من لم يترك ثمانين دينارا. وقال قتادة: كان يقال: ألفا فما فوقها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p494#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p494#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p494#2/r1.claim: Maʿruf means gentle and benevolent treatment; Hasan says a bequest at death according to what is proper, not objectionable, is a Muslim's right.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p494#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p494#2/r2.speaker: الحسن
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p494#2/r2.claim: Hasan says every Muslim should make a proper, non-objectionable bequest when death approaches.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p494#2/r2.anchor: عن الحسن، قوله: {كتب عليكم إذا حضر أحدكم الموت} فقال: نعم، الوصية حق، على كل مسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p494#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p494#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p494#2/r3.claim: A proper bequest for relatives must not wrong heirs through extravagance or stinginess.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p494#2/r3.anchor: والمراد بالمعروف: أن يوصي لأقربيه وصية لا تجحف بورثته، من غير إسراف ولا تقتير

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p494#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p494#2/r4.speaker: النبي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p494#2/r4.claim: When Saʿd, whose only heir was a daughter, asked to bequeath two-thirds or half his wealth, the Prophet refused; he allowed one-third but called it much, saying it is better to leave heirs wealthy than begging.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p494#2/r4.anchor: قال: "الثلث، والثلث كثير؛ إنك أن تذر ورثتك أغنياء خير من أن تذرهم عالة يتكففون الناس".

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p494#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p494#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p494#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas recommends reducing a bequest to a quarter rather than a third, citing the Prophet's statement that one-third is much.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p494#2/r5.anchor: أن ابن عباس قال: لو أن الناس غضوا من الثلث إلى الربع فإن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p494#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p494#2/r6.speaker: النبي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p494#2/r6.claim: Hanifa bequeathed one hundred camels to an orphan in his care; when his sons complained, the Prophet limited a charitable bequest through stepped amounts from five to forty camels.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p494#2/r6.anchor: فقال حنيفة: إني أوصيت ليتيم لي بمائة من الإبل، كنا نسميها المطيبة. فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، "لا لا لا.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p496/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p496/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p496/r1.claim: The author doubts that the camel-bequest report is reliably attributable to the Prophet.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p496/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p496/r2.speaker: النبي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p496/r2.claim: The author calls the report from Abu Hurayra the best in this subject: a wrongdoer may end a lifetime of good with an unjust bequest and enter Hell, while a lifelong wrongdoer may end with a just will and enter Paradise; Abu Hurayra cites 2:229 against transgressing God's limits.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p496/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "إن الرجل ليعمل بعمل أهل الخير سبعين سنة، فإذا أوصى حاف في وصيته

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p58/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p58/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن أبي أوفى
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p58/r1.claim: Asked whether the Prophet made a will, Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa answered no; when asked how the commanded will was fulfilled, he said the Prophet willed the Book of God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p58/r1.anchor: حدثنا طلحة بن مصرف قال: " سألت عبد الله بن أبي أوفى: أوصى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم؟ قال: لا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p58/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p58/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p58/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir likens this to Ibn Abbas’s statement that the Prophet left only what lies between the two covers.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p58/r2.anchor: وهذا نظير ما تقدم عن ابن عباس: " ما ترك إلا ما بين الدفتين "

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p58/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p58/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p58/r3.claim: People were required to bequeath their property when death approached, as stated in this verse.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p58/r3.anchor: وذلك أن الناس كتب عليهم الوصية في أموالهم كما قال تعالى: {كتب عليكم إذا حضر أحدكم الموت

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p58/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p58/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p58/r4.claim: The Prophet left no inheritable estate; his property continued as charity after his death, so he needed no will concerning it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p58/r4.anchor: وأما هو صلى الله عليه وسلم فلم يترك شيئا يورث عنه، وإنما ترك ماله صدقة جارية من بعده

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p58/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p58/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p58/r5.claim: He did not explicitly appoint a successor because his indications toward Abu Bakr made the matter clear; although he considered naming Abu Bakr, he refrained, saying God and the believers would have only Abu Bakr, as proved true.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p58/r5.anchor: ولم يوص إلى خليفة يكون بعده على التنصيص؛ لأن الأمر كان ظاهرا من إشارته وإيمائه إلى الصديق

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p58/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p58/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p58/r6.claim: The Prophet’s instruction to the people was to follow God’s Book.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p58/r6.anchor: وإنما أوصى الناس باتباع كتاب الله تعالى

JISHUMI:v1p748/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p748/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p748/r1.claim: Wills are recommended by Qurʾān and Sunna; jurists differ over obligation, though most say they are not obligatory.
JISHUMI:v1p748/r1.anchor: لا خلاف أن الوصية مرغب فيها، وقد ورد القرآن والسنة بذلك، واختلفوا في وجوبها على ثلاثة أقوال على ما تقدم،

JISHUMI:v1p748/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p748/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p748/r2.claim: Will law covers testator, beneficiary, wording/timing, and executor.
JISHUMI:v1p748/r2.anchor: والكلام في الوصية على أربعة أوجه: صفة الموصي، وصفة الموصى له، وصفة الوصية ومحلها ووقتها، وصفة الوصي.

JISHUMI:v1p748/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p748/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p748/r3.claim: A testator must be sane and adult; most invalidate a minor's will, while al-Shāfiʿī validates it.
JISHUMI:v1p748/r3.anchor: فأما صفة الموصي فأن يكون عاقلا بالغا. واختلفوا في وصية الصبي فالأكثر على أنه لا يصح،

JISHUMI:v1p748/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p748/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p748/r4.claim: If beneficiaries are countable, divide the valid will equally among rich and poor, men and women.
JISHUMI:v1p748/r4.anchor: فأما الموصى له: فعلى وجهين إن كانوا عددا يحصون جاز، وهو بينهم بالسوية الغني والفقير والذكر والأنثى سواء،

JISHUMI:v1p748/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p748/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p748/r5.claim: An uncountable charitable class is valid; Abū Yūsuf permits one beneficiary while Muḥammad requires two or more.
JISHUMI:v1p748/r5.anchor: إن كان فيه قربة فلا يدخل فيه الغني كالوصية لأهل الحاجة والمسكنة جاز كقوله: لفقراء بني تميم،

JISHUMI:v1p748/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p748/r6.speaker: أبو يوسف
JISHUMI:v1p748/r6.claim: Abū Yūsuf says giving to one member of an uncountable charitable class suffices.
JISHUMI:v1p748/r6.anchor: فإن أعطى واحدا منهم جاز عند أبي يوسف.

JISHUMI:v1p748/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p748/r7.speaker: محمد
JISHUMI:v1p748/r7.claim: Muḥammad says the bequest is valid only if at least two members receive something.
JISHUMI:v1p748/r7.anchor: وقال محمد: لا يجوز إلا أن يعطى اثنين فصاعدا

JISHUMI:v1p748/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p748/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p748/r8.claim: A will to an uncountable class named without a charitable sense, such as Banū Tamīm elders, is invalid.
JISHUMI:v1p748/r8.anchor: وإن كان لفظ الوصية يقع للغني والفقير، ولا يحصون فهو باطل، نحو أن يقول: لشيوخ بني تميم.

JISHUMI:v1p748/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p748/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p748/r9.claim: If a class is used for the needy, distribute to countable members or otherwise the needy; two named beneficiaries each receive a share.
JISHUMI:v1p748/r9.anchor: وإن كانوا لا يحصون جعلت في أهل الحاجة، نحو أن يوصي لزمنى بني تميم، وإن أوصى لاثنين بأكثر من الثلث ضرب كل واحد بسهمه.

JISHUMI:v1p748/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p748/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p748/r10.claim: A will is from one-third after debts and before inheritance; excess needs heirs' approval after death, and beneficiary acceptance is generally required after death except in Zufar's view.
JISHUMI:v1p748/r10.anchor: فأما صفة الوصية ومحلها ووقتها: فمحلها ثلث المال بعد الدين، والمواريث بعدهما؛ ولذلك قالت الفقهاء: الموصى له شريك الوارث،

JISHUMI:v1p748/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p748/r11.speaker: زفر
JISHUMI:v1p748/r11.claim: Zufar says no beneficiary acceptance is needed; otherwise acceptance follows death, and heirs take if the beneficiary dies without accepting.
JISHUMI:v1p748/r11.anchor: وتفتقر الوصية إلى قبول الموصى له، إلا ما قاله زفر أنه لا يفتقر إلى القبول،

JISHUMI:v1p748/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p748/r12.speaker: مالك
JISHUMI:v1p748/r12.claim: A bequest to heir or killer is invalid; Mālik permits a killer's bequest, and schools differ on heirs' approval.
JISHUMI:v1p748/r12.anchor: ولا تجوز الوصية للوارث، وللقاتل عمدا، أو خطأ، قال مالك: تجوز للقاتل،

JISHUMI:v1p748/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p748/r13.speaker: أبو يوسف
JISHUMI:v1p748/r13.claim: If heirs approve a killer's bequest, Abū Yūsuf invalidates it; Abū Ḥanīfa and Muḥammad allow it.
JISHUMI:v1p748/r13.anchor: فإن أجازت الورثة وصية القاتل لم يجز عند أبي يوسف، ويجوز عند أبي حنيفة ومحمد،

JISHUMI:v1p748/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p748/r14.speaker: الشافعي
JISHUMI:v1p748/r14.claim: Pious acts or duties such as pilgrimage, zakāt, and expiations come from one-third by the author's view; al-Shāfiʿī charges them to the whole estate.
JISHUMI:v1p748/r14.anchor: وما أوصى به من القرب ابتداء، أو ما لزمه فأوصى به كالحج والزكاة والكفارات فجميع ذلك من الثلث،

JISHUMI:v1p748/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p748/r15.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p748/r15.claim: A testator may revoke a will by agreement, healthy or ill; it remains limited to one-third.
JISHUMI:v1p748/r15.anchor: ويجوز الرجوع من الوصايا بالاتفاق، وسواء أوصى في صحته أو في مرضه، فإنه يكون من الثلث.

JISHUMI:v1p467/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p467/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p467/r1.claim: The verse establishes parents’ rights even if they are unbelievers: the duty arises from parenthood, and unbelief does not remove it; parental maintenance is obligatory in either case.
JISHUMI:v1p467/r1.anchor: وتدل على وجوب حقهما، وإن كانا كافرين لأنه عام، ولأن وجوب الحق

JISHUMI:v1p467/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p467/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p467/r2.claim: When parents share the child’s religion, they are owed filial goodness and respect; maintenance and kind companionship are required whether or not their religion matches.
JISHUMI:v1p467/r2.anchor: قلنا: البر والتعظيم، فأما النفقة والمصاحبة بالمعروف فتجب في الحالين،

JISHUMI:v1p467/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p467/r3.speaker: أبو حنيفة
JISHUMI:v1p467/r3.claim: Abu Hanifa holds that maintenance is obligatory for close relatives; the Shafiʿi position is that it is not.
JISHUMI:v1p467/r3.anchor: فعند أبي حنيفة تجب، وقال الشافعي: لا تجب.

JISHUMI:v1p467/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p467/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p467/r4.claim: The verse establishes relatives’ rights, distinguishing them from strangers; the commentator states that maintenance for prohibited-degree kin is due only when they share a religion.
JISHUMI:v1p467/r4.anchor: والآية تدل عليه، فتدل على وجوب حق ذوي القربى لتميزهم من الأجانب،

JISHUMI:v1p467/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p467/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p467/r5.claim: The verse establishes the rights of orphans and the needy, namely meeting their needs.
JISHUMI:v1p467/r5.anchor: وتدل على وجوب حق اليتامى والمساكين، وهو ما يسد خلتهم.

JISHUMI:v1p745/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p745/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p745/r5.claim: Kutiba means prescribed or made obligatory; its root is writing.
JISHUMI:v1p745/r5.anchor: كتب: فرض، ومنه الصلاة المكتوبة، وأصله من الكتابة، وقد بينا.

JISHUMI:v1p745/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p745/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p745/r6.claim: Maʿruf is what cannot rightly be denied.
JISHUMI:v1p745/r6.anchor: المعروف هو الذي لا يجوز أن ينكر.

JISHUMI:v1p745/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p745/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p745/r7.claim: Al-wasiyya may be the passive subject governed by kutiba, or a subject whose predicate is li-l-walidayn; in the latter analysis the clause is quoted as “the bequest is for the parents.”
JISHUMI:v1p745/r7.anchor: في رفع (الوصية) وجهان: أحدهما: أنه اسم ما لم يسم فاعله، والعامل فيه (كتب).

JISHUMI:v1p745/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p745/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p745/r8.claim: Idha may be governed by kutiba, meaning the duty applies at illness; al-Zajjaj instead takes the will to be made while healthy, with the words “if death comes to us” introducing its terms.
JISHUMI:v1p745/r8.anchor: والعامل في (إذا) قيل فيه وجهان: أحدهما: (كتب) كأنه قيل: كتب عند المرض.

JISHUMI:v1p745/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p745/r9.speaker: الأصم
JISHUMI:v1p745/r9.claim: Al-Asamm says people used to bequeath to distant relatives for prestige while bypassing close kin, so the verse initially made bequests to those kin obligatory to end the custom.
JISHUMI:v1p745/r9.anchor: منعا لهم عما اعتادوه، عن الأصم.

JISHUMI:v1p745/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p745/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p745/r10.claim: Another account says testators had free disposition of their property but were told not to exceed the named recipients; after the inheritance verse came down, the Prophet said God had assigned each right-holder’s share and there is no bequest for an heir.
JISHUMI:v1p745/r10.anchor: قال، صلى الله عليه وسلم -: إن الله تعالى أعطى كل ذي حق حقه، فلا وصية لوارث.

JISHUMI:v1p745/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p745/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p745/r11.claim: Haqqan may be an accusative verbal noun meaning “truly,” an object meaning the bequest was made a right, or an accusative detached from al-wasiyya.
JISHUMI:v1p745/r11.anchor: حقا نصب على المصدر أي حق ذلك حقا، وقيل: على المفعول أي جعل الوصية حقا،

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p249#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p249#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p249#2/r1.claim: The phrase means that death is near and its signs have appeared.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p249#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p249#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p249#2/r2.claim: Here خير means a large amount of wealth.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p249#2/r2.anchor: عن عائشة رضي الله عنها ان رجلا أراد الوصية

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p249#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p249#2/r3.speaker: عائشة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p249#2/r3.claim: Aisha discouraged a man with children and 400 dinars from bequeathing, and told another with 3,000 and four children to leave his little wealth to them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p249#2/r3.anchor: عن عائشة رضي الله عنها ان رجلا أراد الوصية وله عيال وأربعمائة دينار فقالت ما أرى فيه فضلا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p249#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p249#2/r4.speaker: علي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p249#2/r4.claim: Ali stopped his client, who had 700, from bequeathing because he did not regard that amount as wealth under the verse.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p249#2/r4.anchor: وعن علي رضي الله عنه ان مولى له أراد ان يوصي وله سبعمائة فمنعه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p249#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p249#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p249#2/r5.claim: وصية is the subject of كتب; its feminine verb is explained by the intervening phrase and by its sense of making a bequest, which also accounts for the later masculine pronoun.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p249#2/r5.anchor: والوصية فاعل كتب وذكر فعلها للفاصل ولأنها بمعنى ان يوصى ولذلك ذكر الراجع

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p249#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p249#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p249#2/r6.claim: The initial bequest duty for heirs was abrogated by the inheritance verse and the Prophetic rule that an heir receives no bequest.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p249#2/r6.anchor: والوصية للوارث كانت في بدء الإسلام فنسخت بآية المواريث وبقوله عليه الصلاة والسلام

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p249#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p249#2/r7.speaker: النبي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p249#2/r7.claim: The Prophet said that God assigned each rights-holder their due and that an heir may not receive a bequest; the community's acceptance makes the report effectively mass-transmitted despite its solitary transmission.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p249#2/r7.anchor: بقوله عليه الصلاة والسلام 87 ( إن الله أعطى كل ذي حق حقه ألا لا وصية لوارث ) + + وبتلقي الأمة إياه بالقبول

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p249#2/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p249#2/r8.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p249#2/r8.claim: An alternative view says the bequest rule was not abrogated: an heir may receive both the bequest and inheritance under the two verses.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p249#2/r8.anchor: وقيل لم تنسخ والوارث يجمع له بين الوصية والميراث بحكم الآيتين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p249#2/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p249#2/r9.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p249#2/r9.claim: Another view says the bequest verse does not conflict with inheritance law and means that God prescribed inheritance for parents and relatives.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p249#2/r9.anchor: وقيل ما هي بمخالفة لآية المواريث ومعناها كتب عليكم ما اوصى به الله من توريث الوالدين والأقربين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p250/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p250/r1.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p250/r1.claim: The alternative reconciliation makes the dying person responsible for giving parents and relatives what God prescribed and not reducing their shares.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p250/r1.anchor: أو كتب على المحتضر ان يوصي للوالدين والأقربين بتوفير ما اوصى به الله لهم عليهم وان لا ينقص من انصبائهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p250/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p250/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p250/r2.claim: بالمعروف means fairly: do not favor the rich while leaving the poor, and do not exceed one third of the estate.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p250/r2.anchor: بالعدل وهو ان لا يوصي للغني ويدع الفقير ولا يتجاوز الثلث

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p250/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p250/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p250/r3.claim: حقا is an emphatic verbal noun: the matter is indeed a right.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p250/r3.anchor: مصدر مؤكد أي حق ذلك حقا

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r1.anchor: قوله عز وجل : { كتب عليكم إذا حضر أحدكم الموت } أي فرض عليكم

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r2.claim: The bequest takes effect at death through a will made beforehand; the dying person is too occupied to compose it then.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r2.anchor: ولكن تكون العطية بما تقدم من الوصية عند حضور الموت

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r3.claim: All interpreters agree that khayr here means property or wealth.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r3.anchor: والخير : المال في قول الجميع , قال مجاهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r4.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r4.claim: Mujāhid takes khayr throughout the Qur’an as wealth; the passage cites 100:8, 38:32, 24:33, and Shuʿayb’s words in 11:84 as examples.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r4.anchor: قال مجاهد : الخير في القرآن كله المال

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r5.speaker: الجمهور من التابعين والفقهاء
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r5.claim: Most Successors and jurists say obligatory bequests initially prevented ostentatious gifts to outsiders; inheritance legislation fixed recipients and shares and abolished the obligation, while the Sunna prohibited bequests to heirs.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r5.anchor: فذهب الجمهور من التابعين والفقهاء إلى أن العمل بها كان واجبا قبل فرض المواريث لئلا يضع الرجل ماله في البعداء

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r6.speaker: الحسن وقتادة وطاوس وجابر بن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Qatāda, Ṭāwūs, and Jābir ibn Zayd say inheritance abolished obligatory bequests to parents and other heirs; the obligation remains for relatives who do not inherit.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r6.anchor: وبقي فرض الوصية للأقربين الذين لا يرثون على حالة , وهذا قول الحسن , وقتادة , وطاوس , وجابر بن زيد

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r7.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r7.claim: Under the continuing obligation to relatives, Qatāda returns one-third of a third bequeathed to outsiders to relatives, leaving two-thirds of that third to the named legatee.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r7.anchor: أن يرد ثلث الثلث على قرابته ويكون ثلثا الثلث لمن أوصى له به , وهذا قول قتادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r8.speaker: جابر بن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r8.claim: Jābir ibn Zayd reportedly returns two-thirds of the bequeathed third to relatives; the text also assigns two-thirds to the named legatee.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r8.anchor: أن يرد ثلثا الثلث على قرابته ويكون ثلثا الثلث لمن أوصى له به , وهذا قول جابر بن زيد

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r9.speaker: طاوس
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r9.claim: Ṭāwūs assigns the entire third bequeathed to outsiders to relatives instead.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r9.anchor: أنه يريد الثلث كله على قرابته , وهذا قول طاوس

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r10.speaker: علي
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r10.claim: ʿAlī sets the wealth requiring a bequest at one thousand dirhams, interpreting khayr accordingly.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r10.anchor: أن الخير ألف درهم وهذا قول علي

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r11.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r11.claim: Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī gives a range of five hundred to one thousand dirhams for wealth requiring a bequest.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r11.anchor: والثاني : من ألف درهم إلى خمسمائة درهم , وهذا قول إبراهيم النخعي

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r12.speaker: الزهري
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r12.claim: Al-Zuhrī sets no threshold: a bequest is obligatory whether the estate is small or large.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r12.anchor: أنه غير مقدر وأن الوصية تجب في قليل المال وكثيره , وهذا قول الزهري

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r13.claim: One interpretation of maʿrūf is equitable moderation without shortchanging recipients or exceeding proper bounds.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r13.anchor: أحدهما : بالعدل الوسط الذي لا بخس فيه ولا شطط

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r14.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r14.claim: Alternatively, the bequest must concern known property rather than unknown property.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r14.anchor: والثاني : يعني بالمعروف من ماله دون المجهول

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r15.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r15.claim: Piety protects heirs from excessive bequests and relatives from stinginess.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r15.anchor: يعني بالتقوى من الورثة أن لا يسرف , والأقربين أن لا يبخل

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r16.speaker: ابن مسعود
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r16.claim: Ibn Masʿūd’s instruction al-ajall fa-l-ajall is explained as prioritizing those in greatest need.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r16.anchor: قال ابن مسعود : الأجل فالأجل , يعني الأحوج فالأحوج

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r17.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r17.claim: The maximum bequest without excess is a third, supported by the Prophet’s statement that a third is much.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r17.anchor: وغاية ما لا سرف فيه : الثلث , لقول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ( الثلث والثلث كثير )

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r18.speaker: أبو بكر وعمر
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r18.claim: Al-Ḥasan reports that Abū Bakr and ʿUmar bequeathed a fifth, saying to give what God accepted for Himself: a fifth.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r18.anchor: وروى الحسن أن أبا بكر وعمر رضي الله عنهما وصيا بالخمس وقالا يوصي بما رضي الله لنفسه , : بالخمس

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r19.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r19.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r19.claim: The report adds that a fifth is proper, a quarter strenuous, and a third the maximum judges permit.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p231/r19.anchor: وكان يقول : الخمس معروف , والربع جهد , والثلث غاية ما تجيزه القضاة

MUJAHID:v1p95#3/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p95#3/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p95#3/r1.claim: Mujahid says the 'good' left behind means wealth.
MUJAHID:v1p95#3/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ إن ترك خيرا ﴾ يعني مالا

MUQATIL:2:180-182/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:180-182/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:180-182/r1.claim: Kutiba means that something was made obligatory, as in 2:216 and 57:27, where the same verb is used for fighting and monasticism being prescribed.
MUQATIL:2:180-182/r1.anchor: { كتب عليكم } ، يعنى فرض عليكم، نظيرها:

MUQATIL:2:180-182/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:180-182/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:180-182/r2.claim: If a person leaves khayr at death, khayr means wealth; the will gives parents preference over other relatives and makes a suitable bequest to relatives.
MUQATIL:2:180-182/r2.anchor: بعد موته { خيرا } ، يعنى المال، { الوصية للوالدين والأقربين بالمعروف } ،

MUQATIL:2:180-182/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:180-182/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:180-182/r3.claim: The will was obligatory for non-inheriting relatives; neglecting a bequest to one's relatives ended one's deeds in disobedience. The later inheritance verse abrogated the rule for parents, but bequests for non-inheriting relatives remained up to one third of the estate.
MUQATIL:2:180-182/r3.anchor: والذين لا يرثون يقول الله عز وجل تلك الوصية { حقا على المتقين } [آية: 180]، فمن لم يوص لقرابته عند موته،

NASAFI-FULL:v1p88#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p88#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p88#3/r1.claim: كتب means prescribed as an obligation.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p88#3/r1.anchor: فرض ﴿ عليكم إذا حضر أحدكم الموت ﴾

NASAFI-FULL:v1p88#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p88#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p88#3/r2.claim: Death’s arrival means it has drawn near and its signs have appeared.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p88#3/r2.anchor: أى إذا دنا منه فظهرت أمارته

NASAFI-FULL:v1p88#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p88#3/r3.speaker: علي
NASAFI-FULL:v1p88#3/r3.claim: Ali glosses خير as abundant wealth; he stopped a client with only seven hundred from bequeathing, saying this was not enough.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p88#3/r3.anchor: روى عن على رضى الله عنه أن مولى له أراد أن يوصى وله سبعمائة فمنعه

NASAFI-FULL:v1p88#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p88#3/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p88#3/r4.claim: One view says bequests to heirs were required early in Islam, then abrogated by inheritance verses, as explained in Sharh al-Manar.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p88#3/r4.anchor: وكانت للوارث فى بدء الإسلام فنسخت بآية المواريث

NASAFI-FULL:v1p88#3/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p88#3/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p88#3/r5.claim: Another view keeps the verse for non-inheriting relatives, including non-Muslim parents of new Muslims; a recommended bequest maintains kinship, and كتب then does not mean obligatory.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p88#3/r5.anchor: وقيل هى غير منسوخة لانها نزلت فى حق من ليس بوارث

NASAFI-FULL:v1p88#3/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p88#3/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p88#3/r6.claim: A fair bequest neither favors the rich while leaving the poor nor exceeds one-third.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p88#3/r6.anchor: بالعدل وهو أن لا يوصى للغنى ويدع الفقير

NASAFI-FULL:v1p88#3/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p88#3/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p88#3/r7.claim: حقا is an emphatic verbal noun; the God-fearing here are those who avoid associating partners with God.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p88#3/r7.anchor: مصدر مؤكد أى حق ذلك حقا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r1.claim: This is the Qur'an's fullest treatment of bequest; it also mentions bequest in the inheritance passage and the instruction about witnesses at death.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r1.anchor: هذه آية الوصية، وليس في القرآن ذكر للوصية إلا في هذه الآية،

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r2.claim: This verse is fuller than the other Qur'anic mentions and preceded the fixed inheritance shares.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r2.anchor: والتي في البقرة أتمها وأكملها ونزلت قبل نزول الفرائض والمواريث على ما يأتي بيانه.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r3.claim: The wording estimates a coordinating wāw, “and it was prescribed for you,” omitted after the clause became long.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r3.anchor: وفي الكلام تقدير واو العطف أي وكتب عليكم، فلما طال الكلام أسقطت الواو.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r4.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r4.claim: One explanation links this to the preceding retaliation ruling: a person facing execution is as though death arrived, so this is time for a bequest.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r4.anchor: وقيل: لما ذكر أن لولي الدم أن يقتص فهذا الذي أشرف على أن يقتص منه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r5.claim: The omitted relative wāw has a parallel in the night passage, understood as “and the one who.”
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r5.anchor: ومثله في بعض الأقوال: لا يصلاها إلا الأشقى الذي كذب وتولى

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r6.claim: Kataba means the ruling was prescribed and established.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r6.anchor: و «كتب» معناه فرض وأثبت كما تقدم.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r7.claim: The arrival of death means arrival of its causes; Arabs name a cause by its outcome.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r7.anchor: وحضور الموت: أسبابه، ومتى حضر السبب كنت به العرب عن المسبب

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r8.speaker: شاعرهم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r8.claim: An unnamed poet says “I am death,” illustrating how an outcome is spoken of as already present.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r8.anchor:
قال شاعرهم:
يأيها الراكب المزجي مطيته

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r9.speaker: عنترة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r9.claim: Antarah calls death obedient to his hand, another poetic instance of personifying death as present.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r9.anchor:
وقال عنترة:
وإن الموت طوع يدي إذا ما

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r10.speaker: جرير
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r10.claim: Jarir calls himself the death people have heard about, likewise illustrating the expression.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r10.anchor:
وقال جرير في مهاجاة الفرزدق:
أنا الموت الذي حدثت عنه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r11.claim: The masculine verb kataba is used because the intended verbal noun is al-īṣāʾ.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r11.anchor: إنما ذلك لأنه أراد بالوصية الإيصاء.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r12.claim: A second explanation says the intervening material substitutes for the feminine ending, allowed after a long separation.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r12.anchor: وقيل: لأنه تخلل فاصل فكان الفاصل كالعوض من تاء التأنيث

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r13.speaker: أبو الحسن الأخفش
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r13.claim: Al-Akhfash analyzes the conditional answer as “then the bequest,” with the result marker fa omitted.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r13.anchor: قال الأخفش: التقدير فالوصية، ثم حذفت الفاء

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r14.speaker: شاعرهم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r14.claim: An unnamed poetic line exemplifies omission of the fa from a conditional result.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r14.anchor:
من يفعل الحسنات الله يشكرها
والشر بالشر عند الله مثلان

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r15.speaker: أبو الحسن الأخفش
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r15.claim: An alternative makes the past-tense conditional answer precede or follow it: bequest to parents and relatives if he leaves wealth.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r15.anchor: والجواب الآخر: أن الماضي يجوز أن يكون جوابه قبله وبعده

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r16.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r16.claim: Without an estimated fa, al-waṣiyya can be a subject or passive subject of “was prescribed for you.”
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r16.anchor: فإن قدرت الفاء فالوصية رفع بالابتداء، وإن لم تقدر الفاء جاز أن ترفعها بالابتداء

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r17.speaker: جمهور النحاة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r17.claim: Most grammarians reject al-waṣiyya as governor of idhā because the noun-derived relative construction precedes it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r17.anchor: ولا يصح عند جمهور النحاة أن تعمل «الوصية» في «إذا» لأنها في حكم الصلة للمصدر

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r18.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r18.claim: The temporal clause may be governed by kataba, meaning God's obligation takes effect when death approaches and is eternally written.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r18.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون العامل في «إذا»: «كتب» والمعنى: توجه إيجاب الله إليكم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r19.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r19.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r19.claim: Alternatively, an implied īṣāʾ indicated by “bequest” governs idhā.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r19.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون العامل في «إذا» الإيصاء يكون مقدرا دل على الوصية

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r20.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r20.speaker: علي وعائشة وابن عباس
