QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r20.claim: Ali, Aisha, and Ibn Abbas report that khayr means substantial wealth and considered seven hundred dinars small.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180/r20.anchor: فقيل: المال الكثير روي ذلك عن علي وعائشة وابن عباس وقالوا في سبعمائة دينار إنه قليل

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#2/r1.speaker: قتادة عن الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#2/r1.claim: Qatada transmits from al-Hasan that wealth means one thousand dinars or more.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#2/r1.anchor: قتادة عن الحسن: الخير ألف دينار فما فوقها.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#2/r2.speaker: الشعبي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#2/r2.claim: Al-Sha'bi sets the threshold between five hundred and one thousand dinars.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#2/r2.anchor: الشعبي: ما بين خمسمائة دينار إلى ألف.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#2/r3.claim: A bequest broadly means anything commanded or entrusted during life or after death; custom narrows it to instructions executed after death.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#2/r3.anchor: والوصية عبارة عن كل شيء يؤمر بفعله ويعهد به في الحياة وبعد الموت.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#2/r4.claim: Waṣiyya relates to waṣā; its plural is waṣāyā, like qaḍāyā, and waṣī can mean testator or appointed executor.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#2/r4.anchor: والجمع وصايا كالقضايا جمع قضية. والوصي يكون الموصي والموصى إليه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#2/r5.claim: Related forms describe connected growth, appointing an executor, mutual exhortation, and joining one thing to another; the noun has variant pronunciations.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#2/r5.anchor: وتواصى النبت تواصيا إذا اتصل. وأرض واصية: متصلة النبات.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#2/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#2/r6.claim: A Prophetic report urges treating women well, describing them as captives held by their husbands.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#2/r6.anchor:
وفي الحديث:
" استوصوا بالنساء خيرا فإنهن عوان عندكم "

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#2/r7.speaker: العلماء
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#2/r7.claim: Scholars agree that someone holding entrusted property or owing debts must make a bequest to disclose and discharge those obligations.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#2/r7.anchor: بعد إجماعهم على أنها واجبة على من قبله ودائع وعليه ديون.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#2/r8.speaker: مالك والشافعي والثوري
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#2/r8.claim: The majority say bequest is not obligatory for someone with no deposits or debts, whether wealthy or poor.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#2/r8.anchor: وأكثر العلماء على أن الوصية غير واجبة على من ليس قبله شيء من ذلك

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#2/r9.speaker: الزهري وأبو مجلز
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#2/r9.claim: Al-Zuhri and Abu Mujliz take the apparent verse to require a bequest whether the estate is small or large.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#2/r9.anchor: وقالت طائفة: الوصية واجبة على ظاهر القرآن: قاله الزهري وأبو مجلز

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#2/r10.speaker: أبو ثور
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#2/r10.claim: Abu Thawr requires a bequest only when the person owes a debt or holds someone else's property; otherwise it is optional.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#2/r10.anchor: قال أبو ثور: ليست الوصية واجبة إلا على رجل عليه دين أو عنده مال لقوم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#2/r11.speaker: ابن المنذر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#2/r11.claim: Ibn al-Mundhir approves Abu Thawr's distinction: entrusted property must be returned, but one owing no right need not make a will.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#2/r11.anchor: قال ابن المنذر: وهذا حسن لأن الله فرض أداء الأمانات إلى أهلها

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#2/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#2/r12.speaker: ابن عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#2/r12.claim: Ibn Umar reports the Prophet's instruction not to pass two nights without a written will; another version says three nights, and Ibn Umar kept one ready.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#2/r12.anchor: ما حق امرىء مسلم له شيء يريد أن يوصي فيه يبيت ليلتين إلا ووصيته مكتوبة عنده

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#2/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#2/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#2/r13.claim: Opponents argue a universal duty would not depend on the person's wish; duty remains when rights owed or due risk being lost.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#2/r13.anchor: لو كانت واجبة لم يجعلها إلى إرادة الموصي، ولكان ذلك لازما على كل حال

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#2/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#2/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#2/r14.claim: “Prescribed for you” is read as applying when a person chooses to make a bequest.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#2/r14.anchor: قد تقدم الجواب عنه في الآية قبل، والمعنى: إذا أردتم الوصية

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#2/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#2/r15.speaker: النخعي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#2/r15.claim: Al-Nakha'i says the Prophet died without a will while Abu Bakr made one; making a will is good, but omitting it is not blameworthy.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#2/r15.anchor: وقال النخعي: مات رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ولم يوص، وقد أوصى أبو بكر

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#3/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#3/r1.claim: Khayr means money, as in Qur'anic references to spending wealth and loving wealth.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#3/r1.anchor:
والخير المال كقوله:
وما تنفقوا من خير

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#3/r2.speaker: أبو بكر الصديق
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#3/r2.claim: Abu Bakr is reported to have bequeathed one fifth.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#3/r2.anchor: فروي عن أبي بكر الصديق رضي الله عنه أنه أوصى بالخمس.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#3/r3.speaker: علي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#3/r3.claim: Ali is reported as setting aside one fifth from Muslim war booty.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#3/r3.anchor: وقال علي رضي الله عنه من غنائم المسلمين بالخمس.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#3/r4.speaker: معمر عن قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#3/r4.claim: Ma'mar transmits from Qatada that Umar bequeathed one quarter; al-Bukhari also reports this from Ibn Abbas.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#3/r4.anchor: وقال معمر عن قتادة: أوصى عمر بالربع. وذكره البخاري عن ابن عباس.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#3/r5.speaker: علي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#3/r5.claim: Ali preferred bequeathing one fifth to one quarter, and one quarter to one third.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#3/r5.anchor: وروي عن علي رضي الله عنه أنه قال: لأن أوصي بالخمس أحب إلي من أن أوصي بالربع

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#3/r6.speaker: علي وابن عباس وعائشة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#3/r6.claim: Ali, Ibn Abbas, and Aisha advised those with small estates and dependents to leave the property to heirs rather than bequeath it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#3/r6.anchor: واختار جماعة لمن ماله قليل وله ورثة ترك الوصية روي ذلك عن علي وابن عباس وعائشة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#3/r7.speaker: عائشة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#3/r7.claim: Aisha told Ibn Abi Mulayka, with an estate of three thousand and four dependents, that this was little wealth and leaving it to them was better.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#3/r7.anchor: قال لها: إني أريد أن أوصي قالت: وكم مالك؟ قال: ثلاثة آلاف. قالت: فكم عيالك؟

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#3/r8.speaker: جمهور العلماء
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#3/r8.claim: The majority prohibit bequeathing more than one third.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#3/r8.anchor: ذهب الجمهور من العلماء إلى أنه لا يجوز لأحد أن يوصي بأكثر من الثلث

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#3/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#3/r9.speaker: أبو حنيفة وأصحابه
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#3/r9.claim: The Hanafis allow a person with no heirs to bequeath the entire estate.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#3/r9.anchor: إلا أبا حنيفة وأصحابه فإنهم قالوا: إن لم يترك الموصي ورثة جاز له أن يوصي بماله كله.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#3/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#3/r10.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#3/r10.claim: The Prophet explains the one-third limit as protecting heirs from destitution and begging.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#3/r10.anchor: إنك أن تذر ورثتك أغنياء خير من أن تذرهم عالة يتكففون الناس

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#3/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#3/r11.speaker: ابن عباس وأبو عبيدة ومسروق وإسحق ومالك
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#3/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas, Abu Ubayda, Masruq, Ishaq, and one report from Malik say the limit does not apply when there are no heirs.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#3/r11.anchor: ومن لا وارث له فليس ممن عني بالحديث روي هذا القول عن ابن عباس

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#3/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#3/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#3/r12.claim: The disagreement turns on whether the public treasury is an heir or only a custodian.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#3/r12.anchor: وسبب الخلاف مع ما ذكرنا، الخلاف في بيت المال هل هو وارث أو حافظ لما يجعل فيه؟

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#3/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#3/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#3/r13.claim: Scholars agree a person who dies leaving heirs cannot bequeath the whole estate.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#3/r13.anchor: من مات وله ورثة فليس له أن يوصي بجميع ماله

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#3/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#3/r14.speaker: عمرو بن العاص
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#3/r14.claim: Near death, Amr ibn al-As began dictating a will; his son Abdullah said it consumed property belonging to both and suggested asking siblings' approval.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#3/r14.anchor: وروي عن عمرو بن العاص رضي الله عنه أنه قال حين حضرته الوفاة لابنه عبد الله: إني قد أردت أن أوصي

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#3/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#3/r15.speaker: العلماء
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#3/r15.claim: Scholars agree a testator may alter or revoke a will, though they dispute whether a mudabbar slave is an exception.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#3/r15.anchor: وأجمعوا أن للإنسان أن يغير وصيته ويرجع فيما شاء منها إلا أنهم اختلفوا من ذلك في المدبر

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#3/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#3/r16.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#3/r16.claim: Malik allows changes to a will until death but says a slave made mudabbar cannot be withdrawn from that status.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#3/r16.anchor: إلا أن يدبر فإن دبر مملوكا فلا سبيل له إلى تغيير ما دبر

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#4/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#4/r1.claim: The Prophet's instruction says a Muslim with something to bequeath should keep a written will ready, cited in the mudabbar discussion.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#4/r1.anchor: ما حق امرىء مسلم له شيء يوصي فيه يبيت ليلتين إلا ووصيته مكتوبة عنده

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#4/r2.speaker: أبو الفرج المالكي وأبو حنيفة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#4/r2.claim: Abu al-Faraj al-Maliki and Abu Hanifa analogize the mudabbar to fixed-term emancipation: the term is certain and neither can be revoked.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#4/r2.anchor: قال أبو الفرج المالكي: المدبر في القياس كالمعتق إلى شهر لأنه أجل آت لا محالة.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#4/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#4/r3.speaker: الشافعي وأحمد وإسحق
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#4/r3.claim: Al-Shafi'i, Ahmad, and Ishaq treat the mudabbar as a bequest because it counts against the third.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#4/r3.anchor: وقال الشافعي وأحمد وإسحق: هو وصية لإجماعهم أنه في الثلث كسائر الوصايا.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#4/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#4/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#4/r4.claim: The fixed-term analogy is challenged by permission to have intercourse with a mudabbara; reports that the Prophet and Aisha sold a mudabbar support this practice.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#4/r4.anchor: وقد ثبت: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم باع مدبرا، وأن عائشة دبرت جارية لها ثم باعتها

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#4/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#4/r5.speaker: الشعبي وابن سيرين وابن شبرمة والنخعي والثوري
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#4/r5.claim: Al-Sha'bi, Ibn Sirin, Ibn Shubrumah, al-Nakha'i, and al-Thawri permit changing any will except emancipation.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#4/r5.anchor: وقالت طائفة: يغير الرجل من وصيته ما شاء إلا العتاقة. وكذلك قال الشعبي وابن سيرين

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#4/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#4/r6.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#4/r6.claim: For Malik, “free after my death” as a bequest is revocable, but calling the slave mudabbar is not; if the first phrase intends tadbir, most of his school also bars revocation.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#4/r6.anchor: فله الرجوع عند مالك في ذلك. وإن قال: فلان مدبر بعد موتي لم يكن له الرجوع فيه.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#4/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#4/r7.speaker: الشافعي وأحمد وإسحق وأبو ثور
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#4/r7.claim: Al-Shafi'i, Ahmad, Ishaq, and Abu Thawr classify all these death-contingent emancipation statements as bequests because they fall within the third.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#4/r7.anchor: وأما الشافعي وأحمد وإسحق وأبو ثور فكل هذا عندهم وصية لأنه في الثلث

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#4/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#4/r8.speaker: الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#4/r8.claim: Al-Shafi'i requires sale or gift out of ownership to revoke a mudabbar; mere words do not suffice, and it frees at death if still owned.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#4/r8.anchor: إلا أن الشافعي قال: لا يكون الرجوع في المدبر إلا بأن يخرجه عن ملكه ببيع أو هبة.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#4/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#4/r9.speaker: الشافعي في القديم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#4/r9.claim: Al-Shafi'i's earlier view allows revoking tadbir like a bequest; al-Muzani chooses this by analogy with revoking an emancipation bequest.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#4/r9.anchor: وقال في القديم: يرجع في المدبر كما يرجع في الوصية. واختاره المزني

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#4/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#4/r10.speaker: أبو ثور
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#4/r10.claim: Abu Thawr says “I revoke my mudabbar” cancels tadbir, so the slave is not freed when the owner dies.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#4/r10.anchor: وقال أبو ثور: إذا قال قد رجعت في مدبري فقد بطل التدبير

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#4/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#4/r11.speaker: ابن القاسم وأشهب
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#4/r11.claim: For an unqualified statement that a slave is free after death, Ibn al-Qasim says bequest while Ashhab says tadbir even without that intention.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#4/r11.anchor: واختلف ابن القاسم وأشهب فيمن قال: عبدي حر بعد موتي ولم يرد الوصية ولا التدبير

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#4/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#4/r12.speaker: الضحاك وطاوس والحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#4/r12.claim: One view holds the verse operative, restricted to noninheriting parents, such as non-Muslims or slaves, and noninheriting relatives; al-Tabari prefers it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#4/r12.anchor: فقيل: هي محكمة، ظاهرها العموم ومعناها الخصوص في الوالدين اللذين لا يرثان

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#4/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#4/r13.speaker: الطبري
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#4/r13.claim: Al-Tabari chooses the view that the verse remains operative for noninheriting parents and relatives.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#4/r13.anchor: القرابة غير الورثة قاله الضحاك وطاوس والحسن، واختاره الطبري.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#4/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#4/r14.speaker: الزهري
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#4/r14.claim: Al-Zuhri says bequest is obligatory whether the estate is small or large.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#4/r14.anchor: وعن الزهري أن الوصية واجبة فيما قل أو كثر.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#4/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#4/r15.speaker: ابن المنذر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#4/r15.claim: Ibn al-Mundhir reports consensus that bequests to noninheriting parents and relatives are permissible.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#4/r15.anchor: وقال ابن المنذر: أجمع كل من يحفظ عنه من أهل العلم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#4/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#4/r16.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن وقتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#4/r16.claim: They say the verse was general and applied temporarily, then inheritance shares abrogated it for heirs.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#4/r16.anchor: وقال ابن عباس والحسن أيضا وقتادة: الآية عامة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#5/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#5/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#5/r1.claim: Abu Umama reports the Prophet saying God assigned each rightful claimant a share, so there is no bequest to an heir; al-Tirmidhi grades it hasan sahih.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#5/r1.anchor: إن الله قد أعطى لكل ذي حق حقه فلا وصية لوارث

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#5/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#5/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#5/r2.claim: Al-Qurtubi prefers that authentic Sunna, not inheritance shares alone, abrogated bequests to heirs.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#5/r2.anchor: فنسخ الآية إنما كان بالسنة الثابتة لا بالإرث، على الصحيح من أقوال العلماء.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#5/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#5/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#5/r3.claim: Without the no-bequest-to-an-heir hadith, the texts could be reconciled by bequest and, absent one, inheritance or the remainder; hadith and consensus prevent it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#5/r3.anchor: ولولا هذا الحديث لأمكن الجمع بين الآيتين بأن يأخذوا المال عن المورث بالوصية

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#5/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#5/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#5/r4.claim: Although al-Shafi'i and Abu al-Faraj disallow abrogating Qur'an by Sunna, al-Qurtubi permits it because both are God's rulings.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#5/r4.anchor: والشافعي وأبو الفرج وإن كانا منعا من نسخ الكتاب بالسنة فالصحيح جوازه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#5/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#5/r5.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#5/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas and al-Hasan say inheritance shares in Surat al-Nisa abrogated bequests to parents but preserved them for noninheriting relatives; al-Shafi'i and most Malikis agree.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#5/r5.anchor: وقال ابن عباس والحسن: نسخت الوصية للوالدين بالفرض في سورة «النساء»

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#5/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#5/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#5/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that property originally went to children and bequests to parents, then shares specified sons' double portion, parents' shares, and spouses' fractions.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#5/r6.anchor: وفي البخاري عن ابن عباس قال: كان المال للولد وكانت الوصية للوالدين

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#5/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#5/r7.speaker: ابن عمر وابن عباس وابن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#5/r7.claim: They say the whole verse was abrogated, leaving bequest as recommended; Malik and reports from al-Sha'bi and al-Nakha'i are similar.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#5/r7.anchor: وقال ابن عمر وابن عباس وابن زيد: الآية كلها منسوخة، وبقيت الوصية ندبا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#5/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#5/r8.speaker: الربيع بن خثيم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#5/r8.claim: Al-Rabi says there is no bequest; when asked for his codex, he cited Qur'anic priority of kin, as Ibn Umar also did.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#5/r8.anchor: وقال الربيع بن خثيم: لا وصية. قال عروة بن ثابت:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#5/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#5/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#5/r9.claim: Al-aqrabīn is the plural of aqrab, “nearer relatives.”
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#5/r9.anchor: قوله تعالى: { والأقربين } الأقربون جمع أقرب.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#5/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#5/r10.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#5/r10.claim: Some say relatives have priority because God names them; al-Dahhak says bequeathing to outsiders ends one's life in disobedience.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#5/r10.anchor: قال قوم: الوصية للأقربين أولى من الأجانب لنص الله تعالى عليهم حتى قال الضحاك

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#5/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#5/r11.speaker: ابن عمر وعائشة وسالم بن عبد الله
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#5/r11.claim: Ibn Umar reportedly left four thousand to each of his children's mothers; Aisha left household furnishings to a client, and Salim did similarly.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#5/r11.anchor: وروي عن ابن عمر أنه أوصى لأمهات أولاده لكل واحدة بأربعة آلاف. وروي أن عائشة وصت

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#5/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#5/r12.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#5/r12.claim: Al-Hasan says a bequest to nonrelatives is redirected to kin, who share even when an outsider was named; without kin, an outsider's bequest does not stand.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#5/r12.anchor: وقال الحسن: إن أوصى لغير الأقربين ردت الوصية للأقربين فإن كانت لأجنبي فمعهم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#5/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#5/r13.speaker: الشعبي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#5/r13.claim: When Abu al-Aliyah left his estate to Banu Hashim despite being freed by a woman of Riyah, al-Sha'bi said the bequest was invalid.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#5/r13.anchor: وقال الناس حين مات أبو العالية: عجبا له! أعتقته امرأة من رياح وأوصى بماله لبني هاشم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#5/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#5/r14.speaker: طاوس وجابر بن زيد والحسن وإسحق
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#5/r14.claim: Tawus and Jaber ibn Zayd say a bequest to outsiders is void and redirected to kin; al-Hasan and Ishaq similarly agree.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#5/r14.anchor: وقال طاوس: إذا أوصى لغير قرابته ردت الوصية إلى قرابته ونقض فعله

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#5/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#5/r15.speaker: مالك والشافعي وأبو حنيفة والأوزاعي وأحمد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#5/r15.claim: These jurists say neglecting needy kin is bad, but bequests to outsiders remain valid for any recipient, rich or poor, close or distant, Muslim or non-Muslim.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#5/r15.anchor: والأوزاعي وأحمد ابن حنبل: من أوصى لغير قرابته وترك قرابته محتاجين

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#6/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#6/r1.speaker: ابن عمر وابن عباس وعائشة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#6/r1.claim: The preceding view is also the meaning of reports from Ibn Umar and Aisha and is attributed to Ibn Umar and Ibn Abbas.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#6/r1.anchor: وهو معنى ما روي عن ابن عمر وعائشة، وهو قول ابن عمر وابن عباس.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#6/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#6/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#6/r2.claim: Al-Qurtubi says the first view, prioritizing relatives, is better.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#6/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#6/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#6/r3.claim: Al-Qurtubi suggests Abu al-Aliyah favored Banu Hashim because he studied with Ibn Abbas; spiritual fatherhood outweighed his freedwoman's worldly emancipation.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#6/r3.anchor: فلعله نظر إلى أن بني هاشم أولى من معتقته لصحبته ابن عباس وتعليمه إياه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#6/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#6/r4.speaker: جمهور العلماء
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#6/r4.claim: The majority restrain a sick person's property; literalists say he is like a healthy person, a view al-Qurtubi rejects.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#6/r4.anchor: ذهب الجمهور من العلماء إلى أن المريض يحجر عليه في ماله وشذ أهل الظاهر

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#6/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#6/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#6/r5.claim: Sa'd reports that near death at the Farewell Pilgrimage he asked to give away two thirds and then half; the Prophet limited him to a third and urged leaving heirs secure.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#6/r5.anchor: قال سعد: عادني رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في حجة الوداع من وجع أشفيت منه على الموت

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#6/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#6/r6.speaker: أهل الظاهر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#6/r6.claim: Literalists also forbid bequests over one third even with heir consent; al-Qurtubi rejects this and allows waiver.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#6/r6.anchor: ومنع أهل الظاهر أيضا الوصية بأكثر من الثلث وإن أجازها الورثة.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#6/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#6/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#6/r7.claim: Most jurists allow an over-third bequest when heirs approve: the cap protects heirs, so their waiver validates it like their gift.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#6/r7.anchor: وأجاز ذلك الكافة إذا أجازها الورثة، وهو الصحيح لأن المريض إنما منع من الوصية

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#6/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#6/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#6/r8.claim: Al-Daraqutni transmits from Ibn Abbas a Prophetic report allowing a bequest to an heir if other heirs approve.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#6/r8.anchor: وروى الدارقطني عن ابن عباس قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#6/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#6/r9.speaker: عمرو بن خارجة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#6/r9.claim: A report from Amr ibn Kharija likewise says a bequest to an heir is valid only if other heirs approve.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#6/r9.anchor: وروي عن عمرو بن خارجة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#6/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#6/r10.speaker: عطاء وطاوس والحسن وابن سيرين وابن أبي ليلى والزهري وربيعة والأوزاعي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#6/r10.claim: One view makes heirs' approval binding even if they later withdraw it; these early jurists hold it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#6/r10.anchor: قالت طائفة: ذلك جائز عليهم وليس لهم الرجوع فيه. هذا قول عطاء بن أبي رباح وطاوس

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#6/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#6/r11.speaker: ابن مسعود وشريح والحكم والثوري وأبو حنيفة والشافعي وأحمد وأبو ثور
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#6/r11.claim: Another view permits heirs to withdraw consent; Ibn al-Mundhir chooses it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#6/r11.anchor: وقالت طائفة: لهم الرجوع في ذلك إن أحبوا. هذا قول ابن مسعود وشريح والحكم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#6/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#6/r12.speaker: مالك وإسحق
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#6/r12.claim: Malik distinguishes permission given while the testator was healthy, which can be revoked, from permission during illness, which binds; Ishaq agrees.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#6/r12.anchor: وفرق مالك فقال: إذا أذنوا في صحته فلهم أن يرجعوا، وإن أذنوا له في مرضه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#6/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#6/r13.speaker: أصحاب القول الأول
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#6/r13.claim: Those making consent irrevocable argue that the rule protects heirs, so approval removes the obstacle; heirs likewise may approve an over-third bequest to an outsider.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#6/r13.anchor: احتج أهل المقالة الأولى بأن المنع إنما وقع من أجل الورثة فإذا أجازوه جاز.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#6/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#6/r14.speaker: أصحاب القول الثاني
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#6/r14.claim: Those allowing withdrawal argue heirs did not own the property when they consented; a prospective heir might die first or someone else inherit.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#6/r14.anchor: واحتج أهل القول الثاني بأنهم أجازوا شيئا لم يملكوه في ذلك الوقت

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#7/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#7/r1.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#7/r1.claim: Malik argues that healthy owners control all their property, but an ill person's heirs waive an established right; if executed, the waiver cannot be recalled.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#7/r1.anchor: إن الرجل إذا كان صحيحا فهو أحق بماله كله يصنع فيه ما شاء

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#7/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#7/r2.speaker: الأبهري
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#7/r2.claim: Al-Abhari says heirs may revoke approval if the sick testator never executed the bequest because it has not taken effect.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#7/r2.anchor: فإن لم ينفذ المريض ذلك كان للوارث الرجوع فيه لأنه لم يفت بالتنفيذ

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#7/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#7/r3.speaker: إسحق
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#7/r3.claim: Ibn al-Mundhir says Ishaq considers Malik's position closer to the Sunna than alternatives.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#7/r3.anchor: وذكر ابن المنذر عن إسحق بن راهويه أن قول مالك في هذه المسألة أشبه بالسنة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#7/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#7/r4.speaker: مالك والثوري والكوفيون والشافعي وأبو ثور
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#7/r4.claim: Ibn al-Mundhir reports agreement that heirs' approval after the testator's death is binding.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#7/r4.anchor: واتفق قول مالك والثوري والكوفيين والشافعي وأبي ثور أنهم إذا أجازوا ذلك بعد وفاته لزمهم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#7/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#7/r5.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#7/r5.claim: If heirs refuse a bequest to an heir conditional on their approval, Malik returns it to them.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#7/r5.anchor: فقال مالك: إن لم تجز الورثة ذلك رجع إليهم.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#7/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#7/r6.speaker: الشافعي وأبو حنيفة ومعمر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#7/r6.claim: Al-Shafi'i, Abu Hanifa, and Ma'mar say a refused conditional bequest goes to charitable use.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#7/r6.anchor: وفي قول الشافعي وأبي حنيفة ومعمر صاحب عبد الرزاق يمضي في سبيل الله.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#7/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#7/r7.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#7/r7.claim: Malik accepts bequests by people with limited understanding, spendthrifts, intermittently lucid people, and children who understand the bequest and speak sensibly.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#7/r7.anchor: الأمر المجمع عليه عندنا أن الضعيف في عقله والسفيه والمصاب الذي يفيق أحيانا تجوز وصاياهم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#7/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#7/r8.speaker: أبو حنيفة وأصحابه
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#7/r8.claim: Abu Hanifa rejects a child's bequest; al-Muzani says this follows al-Shafi'i by analogy, though al-Shafi'i's students differ since he stated no ruling.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#7/r8.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة وأصحابه: لا تجوز وصية الصبي. وقال المزني: وهو قياس قول الشافعي

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#7/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#7/r9.speaker: أصحاب الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#7/r9.claim: Al-Shafi'i's students divide between Malik's permissive view and Abu Hanifa's prohibition.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#7/r9.anchor: واختلف أصحابه على قولين: أحدهما كقول مالك، والثاني كقول أبي حنيفة.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#7/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#7/r10.speaker: أصحاب القول المانع
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#7/r10.claim: Those prohibiting a child's bequest note that a child cannot divorce, emancipate, face retaliation, or be punished for slander.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#7/r10.anchor: وحجتهم أنه لا يجوز طلاقه ولا عتاقه ولا يقتص منه في جناية ولا يحد في قذف

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#7/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#7/r11.speaker: أبو عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#7/r11.claim: Abu Umar argues that a discerning child resembles an adult under restraint and the waste concern ends at death, so the bequest should stand, supported by a report from Umar.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#7/r11.anchor: ومعلوم أن من يعقل من الصبيان ما يوصي به فحاله حال المحجور عليه في ماله

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#7/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#7/r12.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#7/r12.claim: Malik says the child's bequest reflects the established consensus of Medina.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#7/r12.anchor: وقال مالك: إنه الأمر المجمع عليه عندهم بالمدينة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#7/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#7/r13.speaker: محمد بن شريح
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#7/r13.claim: Muhammad ibn Shurayh says that if a young or old testator states what is right, God put truth on that person's tongue and it cannot be rejected.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#7/r13.anchor: وقال محمد بن شريح: من أوصى من صغير أو كبير فأصاب الحق فالله قضاه على لسانه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#7/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#7/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#7/r14.claim: Al-maʿrūf means fairness without shortchanging or excess; it was initially left to the testator's judgment before the Prophet set the limit.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#7/r14.anchor: يعني بالعدل، لا وكس فيه ولا شطط وكان هذا موكولا إلى اجتهاد الميت

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#8/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#8/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#8/r1.claim: The Prophet set the measure as one third, saying one third is much.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#8/r1.anchor:
وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم:
" إن الله تصدق عليكم بثلث أموالكم عند وفاتكم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#8/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#8/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#8/r2.claim: A report says God grants a third of property at death as added good deeds and purification; al-Daraqutni transmits it from Abu Umama through Muadh ibn Jabal.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#8/r2.anchor: إن الله تصدق عليكم بثلث أموالكم عند وفاتكم زيادة لكم في حسناتكم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#8/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#8/r3.speaker: الحسن والبخاري
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#8/r3.claim: Al-Hasan and al-Bukhari hold bequest cannot exceed one third; al-Bukhari cites the command to judge by revelation and the Prophet's ruling.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#8/r3.anchor: وقال الحسن: لا تجوز وصية إلا في الثلث وإليه ذهب البخاري واحتج بقوله تعالى

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#8/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#8/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#8/r4.claim: Knowingly exceeding the Prophet's one-third limit violates his prohibition and is sinful.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#8/r4.anchor: فمن تجاوز ما حده رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وزاد على الثلث فقد أتى ما نهى النبي

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#8/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#8/r5.speaker: الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#8/r5.claim: Al-Shafi'i reads “one third is much” as meaning it is not a small amount.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#8/r5.anchor: وقال الشافعي: وقوله «الثلث كثير» يريد أنه غير قليل.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#8/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#8/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#8/r6.claim: Ḥaqqan means due care and assurance, not obligatory duty; limiting it to the Godfearing signals recommendation rather than universal obligation.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#8/r6.anchor: يعني ثابتا ثبوت نظر وتحصين، لا ثبوت فرض ووجوب بدليل قوله: { على المتقين }

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#8/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#8/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#8/r7.claim: A bequest is obligatory if silence risks losing another person's right, so one must promptly record and disclose it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#8/r7.anchor: إلا فيما يتوقع تلفه إن مات، فيلزمه فرضا المبادرة بكتبه والوصية به

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#8/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#8/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#8/r8.claim: Ḥaqqan is an emphatic verbal noun in the accusative; an uncanonical ḥaqq would mean “that is true.”
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#8/r8.anchor: وانتصب «حقا» على المصدر المؤكد، ويجوز في غير القرآن «حق» بمعنى ذلك حق.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#8/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#8/r9.speaker: ابن عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#8/r9.claim: The prompt to write a will comes from Ibn Umar's hadith, not from this verse itself.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#8/r9.anchor: قال العلماء: المبادرة بكتب الوصية ليست مأخوذة من هذه الآية وإنما هي من حديث ابن عمر.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#8/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#8/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#8/r10.claim: Writing and witnessing strengthen proof; reliable witnesses' verbal attestation is actionable even without a written document.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#8/r10.anchor: وفائدتها: المبالغة في زيادة الاستيثاق وكونها مكتوبة مشهودا بها

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#8/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#8/r11.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#8/r11.claim: Malik says an unwitnessed handwritten will is not implemented, except for an admission of debt owed to a person the testator is not suspected of favoring.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#8/r11.anchor: فلو كتبها بيده ولم يشهد فلم يختلف قول مالك أنه لا يعمل بها

QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#8/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#8/r12.speaker: أنس بن مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#8/r12.claim: Anas reports a customary will preamble: testimony to God and Muhammad, resurrection, and advice to family to fear God, reconcile, and obey God and His messenger.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:180#8/r12.anchor: روى الدارقطني عن أنس ابن مالك قال: كانوا يكتبون في صدور وصاياهم

RAZI-FULL:v5p41/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p41/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p41/r1.claim: Both the legal usage of ‘written’ and the phrase ‘upon you’ signal obligation; the same construction appears in fasting and pilgrimage verses.
RAZI-FULL:v5p41/r1.anchor: أن قوله تعالى : { كتاب } يفيد الوجوب في عرف الشرع قال تعالى : { كتب عليكم الصيام } وقال : { كتب عليكم إذا حضر أحدكم الموت إن ترك خيرا الوصية }

RAZI-FULL:v5p50#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p50#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p50#2/r1.claim: The opening phrase establishes that making the bequest is obligatory, as explained earlier.
RAZI-FULL:v5p50#2/r1.anchor: اعلم أن قوله تعالى : { كتب عليكم } يقتضي الوجوب على ما بيناه

RAZI-FULL:v5p50#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p50#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p50#2/r2.claim: The phrase does not mean the instant of death, since a person is then unable to make a will.
RAZI-FULL:v5p50#2/r2.anchor: أما قوله : { إذا حضر أحدكم الموت } فليس المراد منه معاينة الموت ، لأن في ذلك الوقت يكون عاجزا عن الإيصاء

RAZI-FULL:v5p50#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p50#2/r3.speaker: الأكثرون
RAZI-FULL:v5p50#2/r3.claim: Most interpreters understand the arrival of death as its signs, especially a dangerous illness; Arabic can say death has arrived for someone at risk, just as one nearing a town is said to have reached it.
RAZI-FULL:v5p50#2/r3.anchor: الأول : وهو اختيار الأكثرين أن المراد حضور أمارة الموت ، وهو المرض المخوف وذلك ظاهر في اللغة

RAZI-FULL:v5p50#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p50#2/r4.speaker: الأصم
RAZI-FULL:v5p50#2/r4.claim: Al-Aṣamm understands the command as requiring a healthy person to direct what should be done when death comes; the Qāḍī prefers the majority view because wills need not mention death and it is the apparent sense.
RAZI-FULL:v5p50#2/r4.anchor: والثاني : قول الأصم أن المراد فرض عليكم الوصية في حالة الصحة بأن تقولوا : إذا حضرنا الموت فافعلوا كذا

RAZI-FULL:v5p50#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p50#2/r5.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v5p50#2/r5.claim: The Qāḍī prefers the danger-sign reading: a will is valid without naming death, and the apparent reading should be retained when possible.
RAZI-FULL:v5p50#2/r5.anchor: قال القاضي : والقول الأول أولى لوجهين أحدهما : أن الموصي وإن لم يذكر في وصيته الموت جاز

RAZI-FULL:v5p50#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p50#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p50#2/r6.claim: There is no disagreement that ‘good’ here means wealth; the Qur’an uses the word this way in several passages.
RAZI-FULL:v5p50#2/r6.anchor: فلا خلاف أنه المال ههنا والخير يراد به المال في كثير من القرآن

RAZI-FULL:v5p50#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p50#2/r7.speaker: الزهري
RAZI-FULL:v5p50#2/r7.claim: Al-Zuhrī holds that a bequest is obligatory on any estate, large or small, because even a little property is beneficial and counts as ‘good’ in scripture and reason.
RAZI-FULL:v5p50#2/r7.anchor: أحدهما : أنه لا فرق بين القليل والكثير ، وهو قول الزهري ، فالوصية واجبة في الكل

RAZI-FULL:v5p50#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p50#2/r8.speaker: الزهري
RAZI-FULL:v5p50#2/r8.claim: Al-Zuhrī’s side also argues that inheritance shares apply whether the estate is small or large, so the same should hold for bequests.
RAZI-FULL:v5p50#2/r8.anchor: أن الله تعالى اعتبر أحكام المواريث فيما يبقى من المال قل أم كثر

RAZI-FULL:v5p51/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p51/r1.speaker: القائلون باختصاص الخير بالمال الكثير
RAZI-FULL:v5p51/r1.claim: Another view restricts ‘good’ to substantial wealth: ordinary speech does not call a single dirham a fortune, just as expressions about wealth or comfort imply abundance; this is figurative denial for deficiency.
RAZI-FULL:v5p51/r1.anchor: والقول الثاني : وهو أن لفظ الخير في هذه الآية مختص بالمال الكثير

RAZI-FULL:v5p51/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p51/r2.speaker: القائلون باختصاص الخير بالمال الكثير
RAZI-FULL:v5p51/r2.claim: They argue that if any amount counted as ‘good,’ the condition would add little, since almost everyone leaves something; only the exceptionally destitute leave nothing.
RAZI-FULL:v5p51/r2.anchor: الحجة الثالثة : لو كانت الوصية واجبة في كل ما ترك ، سواء كان قليلا ، أو كثيرا ، لما كان التقييد بقوله : { إن ترك خيرا } كلاما مفيدا

RAZI-FULL:v5p51/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p51/r3.speaker: علي رضي الله عنه
RAZI-FULL:v5p51/r3.claim: Ali reportedly told a dying client with 700 dirhams not to make a will, since this was not substantial wealth.
RAZI-FULL:v5p51/r3.anchor: فروي عن علي رضي الله عنه أنه دخل على مولى لهم في الموت ، وله سبعمائة درهم ، فقال أولا أوصي ، قال لها : لا

RAZI-FULL:v5p51/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p51/r4.speaker: عائشة رضي الله عنها
RAZI-FULL:v5p51/r4.claim: ʿĀʾisha advised a man with 3,000 and four dependents to leave the money to his family, calling the estate small.
RAZI-FULL:v5p51/r4.anchor: وعن عائشة رضي الله عنها أن رجلا قال : إني أريد أن أوصي ، قالت : كم مالك ؟ قال ثلاثة آلاف ، قالت : كم عيالك ؟ قال أربعة

RAZI-FULL:v5p51/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p51/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v5p51/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reportedly set the threshold at 800 dirhams: below 700, no will; at 800, make one.
RAZI-FULL:v5p51/r5.anchor: وعن ابن عباس إذا ترك سبعمائة درهم فلا يوصي فإن بلغ ثمانمائة درهم أوصي

RAZI-FULL:v5p51/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p51/r6.speaker: قتادة
RAZI-FULL:v5p51/r6.claim: Qatāda reportedly set the estate threshold for making a will at 1,000 dirhams.

RAZI-FULL:v5p51/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p51/r7.speaker: النخعي
RAZI-FULL:v5p51/r7.claim: Al-Nakhaʿī reportedly set the threshold at 1,500 dirhams.
RAZI-FULL:v5p51/r7.anchor: وعن النخعي من ألف وخمسمائة درهم

RAZI-FULL:v5p52#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p52#2/r1.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد عن أبيه
RAZI-FULL:v5p52#2/r1.claim: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Zayd, transmitting from his father, takes ‘the near relatives’ to mean the testator’s children, alongside the parents.
RAZI-FULL:v5p52#2/r1.anchor: وهو قول عبد الرحمن بن زيد عن أبيه

RAZI-FULL:v5p52#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p52#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
RAZI-FULL:v5p52#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid understand ‘the near relatives’ as relatives other than the parents.
RAZI-FULL:v5p52#2/r2.anchor: قول ابن عباس ومجاهد أن المراد من الأقربين من عدا الوالدين

RAZI-FULL:v5p52#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p52#2/r3.speaker: القائلون بوجوب الوصية للقرابة ثم نسخها
RAZI-FULL:v5p52#2/r3.claim: A third view includes every relative, inheriting or not, and is associated with those who first required bequests to kin and later regarded that duty as abrogated.
RAZI-FULL:v5p52#2/r3.anchor: والقول الثالث : أنهم جميع القرابات من يرث منهم ومن لا يرث وهذا معنى قول من أوجب الوصية للقرابة ، ثم رآها منسوخة

RAZI-FULL:v5p52#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p52#2/r4.speaker: القائلون بالقول الرابع
RAZI-FULL:v5p52#2/r4.claim: A fourth view identifies the intended relatives as non-heirs and excludes relatives who inherit.
RAZI-FULL:v5p52#2/r4.anchor: والقول الرابع : هم من لا يرثون من الرجل من أقاربه ، فأما الوارثون فهم خارجون عن اللفظ

RAZI-FULL:v5p52#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p52#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p52#2/r5.claim: ‘In a fair manner’ may specify the amount bequeathed or distinguish which relatives should receive a bequest; both senses fit the wording.
RAZI-FULL:v5p52#2/r5.anchor: أما قوله : { بالمعروف } فيحتمل أن يكون المراد منه قدر ما يوصى به ، ويحتمل أن يكون المراد منه تمييز من يوصى له من الأقربين

RAZI-FULL:v5p52#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p52#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p52#2/r6.claim: The testator must follow a customary, gracious course: prioritize fairly, avoid equating parents with cousins, the rich with poor, or remote kin with present siblings; custom supplies the standard.
RAZI-FULL:v5p52#2/r6.anchor: كلفه الوصية على طريقة جميلة خالية عن شوائب الإيحاش وذلك من باب ما يعلم بالعادة

RAZI-FULL:v5p52#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p52#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p52#2/r7.claim: ‘Truly’ reinforces the duty as an accusative cognate adverbial: the obligation is truly incumbent.
RAZI-FULL:v5p52#2/r7.anchor: فقوله : { حقا } مصدر مؤكد ، أي حق ذلك حقا

RAZI-FULL:v5p52#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p52#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p52#2/r8.claim: The duty is not restricted to the pious: the phrase can mean anyone who chooses piety, and consensus makes obligations apply to pious and impious alike.
RAZI-FULL:v5p52#2/r8.anchor: الواجبات والتكاليف عامة في حق المتقين

RAZI-FULL:v5p53/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p53/r1.speaker: القائلون بوجوب الوصية
RAZI-FULL:v5p53/r1.claim: Those who call the bequest obligatory rely on both ‘prescribed’ and ‘upon you’ as obligatory wording, reinforced by ‘truly incumbent upon the God-fearing.’
RAZI-FULL:v5p53/r1.anchor: واحتج الأولون بقوله : { كتاب } وبقوله : { عليكم } وكلا اللفظين ينبىء عن الوجوب

RAZI-FULL:v5p53/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p53/r2.speaker: القائلون بالندب
RAZI-FULL:v5p53/r2.claim: Other interpreters hold that the bequest is recommended rather than obligatory.
RAZI-FULL:v5p53/r2.anchor: واعلم أن الناس اختلفوا في هذه الوصية ، منهم من قال : كانت واجبة ومنهم من قال : كانت ندبا

RAZI-FULL:v5p53/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p53/r3.speaker: القائلون بنسخ الآية
RAZI-FULL:v5p53/r3.claim: Some of those who consider the bequest obligatory also say this verse was later abrogated.
RAZI-FULL:v5p53/r3.anchor: وهؤلاء اختلفوا منهم من قال هذه الآية صارت منسوخة

RAZI-FULL:v5p53/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p53/r4.speaker: أبو مسلم الأصفهاني
RAZI-FULL:v5p53/r4.claim: Abū Muslim al-Iṣfahānī holds that the bequest verse was not abrogated.
RAZI-FULL:v5p53/r4.anchor: وهذا اختيار أبي مسلم الأصفهاني ، وتقرير قوله من وجوه أحدها

RAZI-FULL:v5p53/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p53/r5.speaker: أبو مسلم الأصفهاني
RAZI-FULL:v5p53/r5.claim: Abū Muslim argues that the verse does not conflict with inheritance: it can refer to God’s allocation of parents’ and relatives’ inheritance or require preserving their prescribed shares.
RAZI-FULL:v5p53/r5.anchor: هذه الآية ما هي مخالفة لآية المواريث ومعناها كتب عليكم ما أوصى به الله تعالى من توريث الوالدين والأقربين

RAZI-FULL:v5p53/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p53/r6.speaker: أبو مسلم الأصفهاني
RAZI-FULL:v5p53/r6.claim: He argues that inheritance and a bequest do not conflict: inheritance is God’s gift, while a will is a gift from the dying person, so a relative could receive both.
RAZI-FULL:v5p53/r6.anchor: لا منافاة بين ثبوت الميراث للأقرباء مع ثبوت الوصية بالميراث عطية من الله تعالى والوصية عطية ممن حضره الموت

RAZI-FULL:v5p53/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p53/r7.speaker: أبو مسلم الأصفهاني
RAZI-FULL:v5p53/r7.claim: Even if the rules conflict, he says the inheritance verse only specifies out inheriting relatives; bequests remain permitted for non-heirs, including kin disqualified by impediments or displaced by closer heirs.
RAZI-FULL:v5p53/r7.anchor: وثالثها : لو قدرنا حصول المنافاة لكان يمكن جعل آية الميراث مخصصة لهذه الآية وذلك لأن هذه الآية توجب الوصية للأقربين

RAZI-FULL:v5p53#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p53#2/r1.speaker: القائلون بنسخ الآية
RAZI-FULL:v5p53#2/r1.claim: The argument that inheritance allocations themselves abrogated the will duty fails: inheritance and an additional bequest can coexist, and any exception would be specification, not abrogation.
RAZI-FULL:v5p53#2/r1.anchor: أنها صارت منسوخة بإعطاء الله تعالى أهل المواريث كل ذي حق حقه فقط وهذا بعيد لأنه لا يمتنع مع قدر من الحق بالميراث وجوب قدر آخر بالوصية

RAZI-FULL:v5p53#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p53#2/r2.speaker: النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام
RAZI-FULL:v5p53#2/r2.claim: A Prophetic report says there is no bequest for an heir; al-Razi calls this the strongest abrogation argument but notes it is a solitary report.
RAZI-FULL:v5p53#2/r2.anchor: وثانيها : أنها صارت منسوخة بقوله عليه السلام : ( ألا لا وصية لوارث ) وهذا أقرب إلا أن الإشكال فيه أن هذا خبر واحد

RAZI-FULL:v5p53#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p53#2/r3.speaker: القائلون بنسخ الآية
RAZI-FULL:v5p53#2/r3.claim: Some answer that the no-bequest report gained mass-transmission status through the imams’ acceptance; al-Razi replies that acceptance may only be conjectural, while certainty would imply collective error about a solitary report.
RAZI-FULL:v5p53#2/r3.anchor: وأجيب عن هذا السؤال بأن هذا الخبر وإن كان خبر واحد إلا أن الأئمة تلقته بالقبول فالتحق بالمتواتر

RAZI-FULL:v5p53#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p53#2/r4.speaker: القائلون بنسخ الآية
RAZI-FULL:v5p53#2/r4.claim: Abrogation by consensus is proposed, but consensus cannot abrogate Qur’an and cannot be claimed because some scholars denied that abrogation occurred.
RAZI-FULL:v5p53#2/r4.anchor: ثالثها أنها صارت منسوخة بالإجماع والإجماع لا يجوز أن ينسخ به القرآن

RAZI-FULL:v5p53#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p53#2/r5.speaker: القائلون بنسخ الآية
RAZI-FULL:v5p53#2/r5.claim: An analogy with debts argues that relatives receive no special share when no will exists, based on the inheritance verse; al-Razi rejects analogy as a means of abrogating Qur’an.
RAZI-FULL:v5p53#2/r5.anchor: منسوخة بدليل قياسي وهو أن نقول

RAZI-FULL:v5p54/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p54/r1.speaker: أكثر المفسرين والمعتبرين من الفقهاء
RAZI-FULL:v5p54/r1.claim: Most exegetes and authoritative jurists hold that the bequest duty was abrogated for both inheriting and non-inheriting relatives.
RAZI-FULL:v5p54/r1.anchor: قول أكثر المفسرين والمعتبرين من الفقهاء

RAZI-FULL:v5p54/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p54/r2.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن البصري ومسروق وطاوس والضحاك ومسلم بن يسار والعلاء بن زياد
RAZI-FULL:v5p54/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī, Masrūq, Ṭāwūs, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, Muslim b. Yasār, and al-ʿAlāʾ b. Ziyād hold that only the duty to heirs was abrogated; bequests to non-heir relatives remain obligatory.
RAZI-FULL:v5p54/r2.anchor: وهو مذهب ابن عباس / والحسن البصري ومسروق وطاوس والضحاك

RAZI-FULL:v5p54/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p54/r3.speaker: الضحاك
RAZI-FULL:v5p54/r3.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says that dying without making a bequest to one’s relatives ends one’s deeds in disobedience.
RAZI-FULL:v5p54/r3.anchor: حتى قال الضحاك : من مات من غير أن يوصي لأقربائه فقد ختم عمله بمعصية

RAZI-FULL:v5p54/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p54/r4.speaker: طاوس
RAZI-FULL:v5p54/r4.claim: Ṭāwūs says that if someone bequeaths to outsiders and leaves relatives out, the bequest is taken from the outsiders and returned to the relatives.
RAZI-FULL:v5p54/r4.anchor: وقال طاوس : إن أوصى للأجانب وترك الأقارب نزع منهم ورد إلى الأقارب

RAZI-FULL:v5p54/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p54/r5.speaker: القائلون ببقاء الآية في غير الوارث
RAZI-FULL:v5p54/r5.claim: They argue that the verse obliges bequests to relatives; since the heir exception is established by inheritance rules, the Qur’an, or consensus—which they deny exists amid disagreement—the duty remains for non-heirs.
RAZI-FULL:v5p54/r5.anchor: هذه الآية دالة على وجوب الوصية للقريب ترك العمل به في حق الوارث القريب

RAZI-FULL:v5p54/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p54/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v5p54/r6.claim: A Prophetic report says a Muslim with property should not let two nights pass without a written will; since bequests to non-relatives are not obligatory, these scholars infer the obligation concerns relatives and the Sunna confirms the verse.
RAZI-FULL:v5p54/r6.anchor: الحجة الثانية : قوله عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( ما حق امرىء مسلم له مال أن يبيت ليلتين إلا ووصيته مكتوبة عنده )

RAZI-FULL:v5p54/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p54/r7.speaker: الجمهور
RAZI-FULL:v5p54/r7.claim: The majority’s strongest proof for abrogation is the inheritance verse’s phrase ‘after a bequest or debt,’ discussed earlier.
RAZI-FULL:v5p54/r7.anchor: فأجود ما لهم التمسك بقوله تعالى : { من بعد وصية يوصى بها أو دين }

RAZI-FULL:v5p54/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p54/r8.speaker: ابن مسعود
RAZI-FULL:v5p54/r8.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says the bequest should go first to the poorest relatives.
RAZI-FULL:v5p54/r8.anchor: نقل عن ابن مسعود أنه جعل هذه الوصية للأفقر فالأفقر من الأقرباء

RAZI-FULL:v5p54/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p54/r9.speaker: الحسن البصري
RAZI-FULL:v5p54/r9.claim: Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī says the relevant relatives are wealthy and should be treated equally.
RAZI-FULL:v5p54/r9.anchor: وقال الحسن البصري : هم الأغنياء سواء

RAZI-FULL:v5p54/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p54/r10.speaker: الحسن وخالد بن زيد وعبد الملك بن يعلى
RAZI-FULL:v5p54/r10.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Khālid b. Zayd, and ʿAbd al-Malik b. Yaʿlā assign two-thirds of the bequest’s one-third to non-inheriting kin and one-third to the outsider named in the will.
RAZI-FULL:v5p54/r10.anchor: روي عن الحسن وخالد بن زيد وعبد الملك بن يعلى أنهم قالوا فيمن يوصي لغير قرابته وله قرابة لا ترثه

RAZI-FULL:v5p54/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p54/r11.speaker: طاوس
RAZI-FULL:v5p54/r11.claim: Ṭāwūs says that when relatives are needy, an outsider’s bequest is taken away and redirected to the relatives.
RAZI-FULL:v5p54/r11.anchor: وعن طاوس أن الأقارب إن كانوا محتاجين انتزعت الوصية من الأجانب وردت إلى الأقارب

STUDYQURAN:2:180/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:180/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:180/r1.claim: The term bequest is also used in 4:12 and 5:106.
STUDYQURAN:2:180/r1.anchor: is also used in 4:12 and 5:106. Here some good

STUDYQURAN:2:180/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:180/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:180/r2.claim: Here khayr means property, as in 2:272 and 100:8.
STUDYQURAN:2:180/r2.anchor: means one’s property, as in, Whatever good you spend

STUDYQURAN:2:180/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:180/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:180/r3.claim: One interpretation makes the bequest conditional on leaving property, so it is not universally obligatory; debts and other financial obligations are paid first, and the clause can mean should one desire a bequest.
STUDYQURAN:2:180/r3.anchor: being an obligation upon the reverent only if one leaves some good, which does not make such a bequest a universal obligation

STUDYQURAN:2:180/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:180/r4.speaker: Some jurists
STUDYQURAN:2:180/r4.claim: Some jurists set a specific minimum amount of property for a bequest.
STUDYQURAN:2:180/r4.anchor: some jurists assign a specific amount

STUDYQURAN:2:180/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:180/r5.speaker: Other jurists
STUDYQURAN:2:180/r5.claim: Other jurists allow a bequest of any amount, large or small.
STUDYQURAN:2:180/r5.anchor: others consider any sum, large or small, to be a possible bequest

STUDYQURAN:2:180/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:180/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:180/r6.claim: Islamic law generally limits bequests to no more than one third of the estate.
STUDYQURAN:2:180/r6.anchor: they account for no more than a third of one’s property

STUDYQURAN:2:180/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:180/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:180/r7.claim: A bequest generally cannot designate someone who automatically inherits under the Quranic shares.
STUDYQURAN:2:180/r7.anchor: not be designated for a person who automatically inherits according to the Quranic injunctions concerning shares of inheritance

STUDYQURAN:2:180/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:180/r8.speaker: Some
STUDYQURAN:2:180/r8.claim: Some consider the bequest verse completely abrogated.
STUDYQURAN:2:180/r8.anchor: Some consider this verse to be abrogated completely

STUDYQURAN:2:180/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:180/r9.speaker: Others
STUDYQURAN:2:180/r9.claim: Others hold that it is abrogated only for heirs entitled to Quranic shares and remains applicable to others.
STUDYQURAN:2:180/r9.anchor: others say it is partially abrogated in the case of those legally entitled to an inheritance share

STUDYQURAN:2:180/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:180/r10.speaker: Shiites
STUDYQURAN:2:180/r10.claim: Shiites hold that the verse is not abrogated and does not conflict with another Quranic verse, given their different inheritance framework.

STUDYQURAN:2:180/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:180/r11.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:180/r11.claim: The hadith barring bequests for heirs, if universal, prevents bequests to automatic heirs and appears to conflict with Quranic inheritance-share verses.
STUDYQURAN:2:180/r11.anchor: The question of abrogation arises because of the ḥadīth, “Let there be no bequests for heirs.”

STUDYQURAN:2:180/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:180/r12.speaker: al-Qurṭubī
STUDYQURAN:2:180/r12.claim: Al-Qurṭubī accepts the hadith as binding, showing that the Sunnah can abrogate the Quran.
STUDYQURAN:2:180/r12.anchor: such as al-Qurṭubī, the acceptance of this ḥadīth as binding shows that the Sunnah can abrogate the Quran

STUDYQURAN:2:180/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:180/r13.speaker: Others
STUDYQURAN:2:180/r13.claim: Others say this verse remains unabrogated because a hadith is less certain than the Quran and cannot replace its ruling.
STUDYQURAN:2:180/r13.anchor: for others this shows that the present verse is not abrogated for the very same reason, namely, that a ḥadīth

STUDYQURAN:2:180/r14.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:180/r14.speaker: al-Qurṭubī
STUDYQURAN:2:180/r14.claim: Al-Qurṭubī says the only text preventing harmonization of bequest and inheritance commands is the hadith barring bequests for heirs.
STUDYQURAN:2:180/r14.anchor: Al-Qurṭubī acknowledges that the only text preventing a harmonization of the Quranic injunctions regarding bequests and inheritance is this ḥadīth

STUDYQURAN:2:180/r15.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:180/r15.speaker: Some
STUDYQURAN:2:180/r15.claim: Some reconcile the commands by taking the parents and relatives to be people who would not inherit, such as disbelieving parents.
STUDYQURAN:2:180/r15.anchor: Some have tried to harmonize them by saying that the parents and relatives here are those who would not inherit in any case

STUDYQURAN:2:180/r16.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:180/r16.speaker: Early commentators
STUDYQURAN:2:180/r16.claim: Bequests should favor relatives before nonrelatives; early commentators condemned leaving needy relatives to give property to outsiders.
STUDYQURAN:2:180/r16.anchor: early commentators severely condemned those who would leave relatives in need while giving property to nonrelatives

STUDYQURAN:2:180/r17.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:180/r17.speaker: Prophet
STUDYQURAN:2:180/r17.claim: The Prophet advised limiting a bequest to one third, saying that amount is considerable and heirs should be left free from want rather than destitute.
STUDYQURAN:2:180/r17.anchor: the Prophet said to a man who offered to make a bequest

STUDYQURAN:2:180/r18.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:180/r18.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:180/r18.claim: Before Quranic inheritance rules, Arab custom gave inheritance through the male line to male relations, an arrangement called agnatic inheritance.
STUDYQURAN:2:180/r18.anchor: the custom of Arabia was that male relations would inherit through the male line, called agnatic inheritance

STUDYQURAN:2:180/r19.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:180/r19.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:180/r19.claim: Quranic quota shares subordinated customary agnatic heirs; under Sunni law they may inherit only from the residue after quota shares.
STUDYQURAN:2:180/r19.anchor: The Quranic shares, which included the nearest male relatives, demoted the customary agnatic heirs to a secondary status

STUDYQURAN:2:180/r20.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:180/r20.speaker: Shiites
STUDYQURAN:2:180/r20.claim: Shiism rejects agnatic inheritance and allocates the residual estate by blood proximity equally through male and female lines.
STUDYQURAN:2:180/r20.anchor: In Shiism, agnatic inheritance is rejected, and a system of proximity in blood kinship is used for the residual property

TAB-FULL:v3p123#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p123#3/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v3p123#3/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī explains the verse as an obligation imposed on God-fearing believers, who must obey it.
TAB-FULL:v3p123#3/r1.anchor: يعني بذلك: فرض عليكم هذا وأوجبه، وجعله حقا واجبا على من اتقى الله فأطاعه أن يعمل به

TAB-FULL:v3p123#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p123#3/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v3p123#3/r2.claim: The duty applies to a person with property who can bequeath to parents and relatives who do not inherit.
TAB-FULL:v3p123#3/r2.anchor: أو فرض على الرجل ذي المال أن يوصي لوالديه وأقربيه الذين لا يرثونه؟ قيل: نعم

TAB-FULL:v3p123#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p123#3/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v3p123#3/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī names the parents and relatives as the people whom the bequest is meant to benefit.
TAB-FULL:v3p123#3/r3.anchor: أو فرض على الرجل ذي المال أن يوصي لوالديه وأقربيه الذين لا يرثونه؟ قيل: نعم

TAB-FULL:v3p123#3/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p123#3/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v3p123#3/r4.claim: Failing to bequeath when able neglects a divine duty; al-Ṭabarī compares the wording to the obligation of fasting.
TAB-FULL:v3p123#3/r4.anchor: كما قال: {كتب عليكم الصيام} [البقرة: 183] ولا خلاف بين الجميع أن تارك الصيام وهو عليه قادر مضيع بتركه فرضا لله عليه

TAB-FULL:v3p123#3/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p123#3/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v3p123#3/r5.claim: Some scholars hold the bequest rule abrogated by inheritance verses, while others hold it remains; al-Ṭabarī prefers its continued force because the rules can apply together and abrogation needs decisive proof.
TAB-FULL:v3p123#3/r5.anchor: لم يكن لنا القضاء عليه بأنه منسوخ إلا بحجة يجب التسليم لها

TAB-FULL:v3p123#3/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p123#3/r6.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v3p123#3/r6.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says whoever dies without bequeathing to his relatives ends his deeds with a sin.
TAB-FULL:v3p123#3/r6.anchor: عن الضحاك، أنه كان يقول «من مات ولم يوص لذوي قرابته فقد ختم عمله بمعصية»

TAB-FULL:v3p123#3/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p123#3/r7.speaker: مسروق
TAB-FULL:v3p123#3/r7.claim: Masrūq rebukes inappropriate bequests, urging a bequest to non-inheriting kin and leaving the rest to God's apportionment.
TAB-FULL:v3p123#3/r7.anchor: عن مسلم، عن مسروق: أنه حضر رجلا فوصى بأشياء لا تنبغي، فقال له مسروق

TAB-FULL:v3p128/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p128/r1.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v3p128/r1.claim: Al-Ḥasan says that if someone bequeaths one-third to non-relatives, the relatives receive one-third of that third.
TAB-FULL:v3p128/r1.anchor: عن الحسن، أنه كان يقول «إذا أوصى الرجل لغير ذي قرابته بثلثه فلهم ثلث الثلث

TAB-FULL:v3p128/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p128/r2.speaker: طاووس
TAB-FULL:v3p128/r2.claim: Ṭāwūs says a bequest to named people is taken back and returned to needy relatives if the testator left those relatives needy.
TAB-FULL:v3p128/r2.anchor: عن ابن طاوس، عن أبيه، قال «من أوصى لقوم وسماهم وترك ذوي قرابته محتاجين انتزعت منهم وردت إلى ذوي قرابته»

TAB-FULL:v3p128/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p128/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v3p128/r3.claim: Qatāda says inheritance fixed shares for the parents, replacing their bequests, while bequests remained for non-inheriting relatives and were forbidden to heirs.
TAB-FULL:v3p128/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، في قوله " {كتب عليكم إذا حضر أحدكم الموت إن ترك خيرا الوصية للوالدين والأقربين} [البقرة: 180] فجعلت الوصية

TAB-FULL:v3p128/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p128/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v3p128/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the rule was abrogated for inheriting relatives but remained for non-inheriting kin.
TAB-FULL:v3p128/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {إن ترك خيرا الوصية للوالدين والأقربين} [البقرة: 180] قال «نسخ من يرث ولم ينسخ الأقربين الذين لا يرثون»

TAB-FULL:v3p128/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p128/r5.speaker: طاووس
TAB-FULL:v3p128/r5.claim: Ṭāwūs says inheritance superseded bequests for heirs while the rule remained for those who do not inherit; his report adds that a bequest to a relative was not valid.
TAB-FULL:v3p128/r5.anchor: عن ابن طاوس، عن أبيه، قال «كانت الوصية قبل الميراث للوالدين، والأقربين، فلما نزل الميراث

TAB-FULL:v3p128/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p128/r6.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v3p128/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the parents' bequest was abrogated, but bequests to relatives excluded from inheritance remained, even if they were wealthy.
TAB-FULL:v3p128/r6.anchor: عن الحسن، في قوله: {إن ترك خيرا الوصية للوالدين والأقربين} [البقرة: 180] قال «نسخ الوالدين، وأثبت الأقربين الذين يحرمون فلا يرثون»

TAB-FULL:v3p130/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p130/r1.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v3p130/r1.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the verse was abrogated as to parents but the bequest to kin remained, whether they were rich or poor.
TAB-FULL:v3p130/r1.anchor: عن الحسن، في هذه الآية " {الوصية للوالدين والأقربين} [البقرة: 180] قال: للوالدين منسوخة، والوصية للقرابة وإن كانوا أغنياء

TAB-FULL:v3p130/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p130/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v3p130/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says 4:11 clarified the parents' inheritance shares and left a one-third bequest for relatives.
TAB-FULL:v3p130/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله " {إن ترك خيرا الوصية للوالدين والأقربين} [البقرة: 180] فكان لا يرث مع الوالدين غيرهم إلا وصية

TAB-FULL:v3p130/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p130/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v3p130/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the bequest to parents was abrogated while bequests to non-inheriting relatives remained established.
TAB-FULL:v3p130/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله " {إن ترك خيرا الوصية للوالدين والأقربين} [البقرة: 180] فنسخ الوصية للوالدين وأثبت الوصية للأقربين الذين لا يرثون

TAB-FULL:v3p130/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p130/r4.speaker: الربيع
TAB-FULL:v3p130/r4.claim: Al-Rabīʿ says the inheritance verse replaced the parents' bequests, leaving bequests for relatives who do not inherit.
TAB-FULL:v3p130/r4.anchor: عن الربيع، قوله: {كتب عليكم إذا حضر أحدكم الموت إن ترك خيرا الوصية للوالدين والأقربين} [البقرة: 180] بالمعروف

TAB-FULL:v3p130/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p130/r5.speaker: مسلم بن يسار والعلاء بن زياد
TAB-FULL:v3p130/r5.claim: Muslim b. Yasār and al-ʿAlāʾ b. Ziyād interpret the surviving bequest as one for relatives.
TAB-FULL:v3p130/r5.anchor: سألت مسلم بن يسار، والعلاء بن زياد، عن قول الله، تبارك وتعالى

TAB-FULL:v3p130/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p130/r6.speaker: إياس بن معاوية
TAB-FULL:v3p130/r6.claim: Iyas b. Muʿāwiya likewise says the bequest is for relatives.
TAB-FULL:v3p130/r6.anchor: عن إياس بن معاوية، قال «في القرابة»

TAB-FULL:v3p130/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p130/r7.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v3p130/r7.claim: Another group holds that inheritance rules abrogated the entire bequest obligation, whether for close or distant kin.
TAB-FULL:v3p130/r7.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل نسخ الله ذلك كله، وفرض الفرائض والمواريث فلا وصية تجب لأحد على أحد قريب ولا بعيد

TAB-FULL:v3p132/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p132/r1.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v3p132/r1.claim: Ibn Zayd says inheritance allotments abrogated the whole bequest rule.
TAB-FULL:v3p132/r1.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله " {إن ترك خيرا الوصية للوالدين والأقربين} [البقرة: 180] الآية، قال: فنسخ الله ذلك كله وفرض الفرائض

TAB-FULL:v3p132/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p132/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v3p132/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, while explaining al-Baqara, says this verse was abrogated.
TAB-FULL:v3p132/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، " أنه قام فخطب الناس هاهنا، فقرأ عليهم سورة البقرة ليبين لهم منها، فأتى على هذه الآية: {إن ترك خيرا الوصية للوالدين والأقربين} [البقرة: 180] قال: نسخت هذه

TAB-FULL:v3p132/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p132/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v3p132/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says inheritance allotments for parents and relatives abrogated the bequest.
TAB-FULL:v3p132/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله " {إن ترك خيرا الوصية للوالدين والأقربين} [البقرة: 180] نسخت الفرائض التي للوالدين، والأقربين الوصية

TAB-FULL:v3p132/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p132/r4.speaker: ابن عمر
TAB-FULL:v3p132/r4.claim: Ibn ʿUmar says the inheritance verse abrogated the bequest verse; the transmitter later could not recall the report precisely.
TAB-FULL:v3p132/r4.anchor: قال: سمعت ابن عمر، يقول في قوله " {إن ترك خيرا الوصية للوالدين والأقربين} [البقرة: 180] قال: نسختها آية الميراث

TAB-FULL:v3p132/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p132/r5.speaker: عكرمة والحسن البصري
TAB-FULL:v3p132/r5.claim: ʿIkrima and al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī say the rule remained until the inheritance verse abrogated it.
TAB-FULL:v3p132/r5.anchor: عن عكرمة، والحسن البصري، قالا " {إن ترك خيرا الوصية للوالدين والأقربين} [البقرة: 180] فكانت الوصية كذلك حتى نسختها آية الميراث

TAB-FULL:v3p132/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p132/r6.speaker: شريح
TAB-FULL:v3p132/r6.claim: Shurayḥ says people used to bequeath all their property until the inheritance verse came down.
TAB-FULL:v3p132/r6.anchor: عن شريح، في هذه الآية: {إن ترك خيرا الوصية للوالدين والأقربين} [البقرة: 180] قال «كان الرجل يوصي بماله كله حتى نزلت آية الميراث»

TAB-FULL:v3p132/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p132/r7.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v3p132/r7.claim: Qatāda says the inheritance verses in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ abrogated the bequest verse in al-Baqara.
TAB-FULL:v3p132/r7.anchor: زعم قتادة «أنه نسخت آيتا المواريث في سورة النساء الآية في سورة البقرة في شأن الوصية»

TAB-FULL:v3p132/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p132/r8.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v3p132/r8.claim: Mujāhid says children inherited, while parents and relatives received bequests under the earlier rule, which was abrogated.
TAB-FULL:v3p132/r8.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قول الله: {إن ترك خيرا الوصية للوالدين والأقربين} [البقرة: 180] قال «كان الميراث للولد، والوصية للوالدين، والأقربين، وهي منسوخة»

TAB-FULL:v3p134/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p134/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v3p134/r1.claim: Mujāhid says the earlier bequest rule was abrogated by the inheritance ruling in 4:11.
TAB-FULL:v3p134/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد، قال " كان الميراث للولد، والوصية للوالدين والأقربين وهي منسوخة نسختها آية في سورة النساء: {يوصيكم الله في أولادكم} [النساء: 11]

TAB-FULL:v3p134/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p134/r2.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v3p134/r2.claim: Al-Suddī says people initially had no fixed inheritance shares and divided property by bequest to parents and family, until 4:11 replaced that practice.
TAB-FULL:v3p134/r2.anchor: عن السدي: {كتب عليكم إذا حضر أحدكم الموت إن ترك خيرا الوصية للوالدين والأقربين} [البقرة: 180] " أما الوالدان والأقربون

TAB-FULL:v3p134/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p134/r3.speaker: ابن عمر
TAB-FULL:v3p134/r3.claim: Ibn ʿUmar himself did not make a will, saying God knew how he had used his property in life and he did not want others sharing his real estate with his children.
TAB-FULL:v3p134/r3.anchor: عن نافع، أن ابن عمر، لم يوص وقال «أما مالي فالله أعلم ما كنت أصنع فيه في الحياة، وأما رباعي

TAB-FULL:v3p134/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p134/r4.speaker: ربيع بن خثيم
TAB-FULL:v3p134/r4.claim: When ʿUrwa b. Thābit asked for his Qurʾān codex, Rabīʿ b. Khuthaym cited 33:6, that blood relatives have prior claim to one another.
TAB-FULL:v3p134/r4.anchor: قال عروة يعني ابن ثابت، لربيع بن خثيم أوص لي بمصحفك قال " فنظر إلى أبيه فقال: {وأولو الأرحام بعضهم أولى ببعض في كتاب الله} [الأحزاب: 6]

TAB-FULL:v3p134/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p134/r5.speaker: إبراهيم
TAB-FULL:v3p134/r5.claim: Ibrāhīm says Zayd and Ṭalḥa need not have insisted on wills: the Prophet died without one, Abū Bakr made one, and either practice is sound.
TAB-FULL:v3p134/r5.anchor: عن إبراهيم، قال «ذكرنا له أن زيدا، وطلحة كانا يشددان في الوصية، فقال» ما كان عليهما أن يفعلا، مات النبي

TAB-FULL:v3p134/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p134/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v3p134/r6.claim: Al-Ṭabarī concludes that khayr here means wealth, citing Ibn ʿAbbās's gloss مالا.
TAB-FULL:v3p134/r6.anchor: وأما الخير الذي إذا تركه تارك وجب عليه الوصية فيه لوالديه وأقربيه الذين لا يرثون فهو المال

TAB-FULL:v3p136/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p136/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v3p136/r1.claim: Mujāhid says khayr means wealth, and adduces the same sense in 100:8, 38:32, and 24:33.
TAB-FULL:v3p136/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد: {إن ترك خيرا} [البقرة: 180] كان يقول " الخير: في القرآن كله المال {لحب الخير لشديد} [العاديات: 8]

TAB-FULL:v3p136/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p136/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v3p136/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، " {إن ترك خيرا الوصية} [البقرة: 180] أي مالا

TAB-FULL:v3p136/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p136/r3.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v3p136/r3.anchor: عن السدي، " {إن ترك خيرا الوصية} [البقرة: 180] أما خيرا: فالمال

TAB-FULL:v3p136/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p136/r4.speaker: الربيع
TAB-FULL:v3p136/r4.anchor: عن الربيع، " {إن ترك خيرا} [البقرة: 180] قال: إن ترك مالا

TAB-FULL:v3p136/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p136/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v3p136/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses khayr as wealth.
TAB-FULL:v3p136/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله: {إن ترك خيرا} [البقرة: 180] قال " الخير: المال

TAB-FULL:v3p136/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p136/r6.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v3p136/r6.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says khayr means wealth, citing 11:84 where Shuʿayb says he sees his people in prosperity.
TAB-FULL:v3p136/r6.anchor: عن الضحاك، في قوله " {إن ترك خيرا الوصية} [البقرة: 180] قال: المال، ألا ترى أنه يقول: قال شعيب لقومه: {إني أراكم بخير} [هود: 84]

TAB-FULL:v3p136/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p136/r7.speaker: عطاء بن أبي رباح
TAB-FULL:v3p136/r7.claim: ʿAṭāʾ b. Abī Rabāḥ says khayr in this verse means wealth.
TAB-FULL:v3p136/r7.anchor: عن عطاء بن أبي رباح، قال: {كتب عليكم إذا حضر أحدكم الموت إن ترك خيرا} [البقرة: 180] قال عطاء " الخير فيما يرى: المال

TAB-FULL:v3p136/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p136/r8.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v3p136/r8.claim: Qatāda sets the amount of wealth that triggers the bequest rule at one thousand dirhams or more.
TAB-FULL:v3p136/r8.anchor: عن قتادة، في هذه الآية: {إن ترك خيرا الوصية} [البقرة: 180] قال " الخير: ألف فما فوقه

TAB-FULL:v3p137/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p137/r1.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
TAB-FULL:v3p137/r1.claim: In reports about sick relatives with roughly six hundred to nine hundred dirhams, ʿAlī advises against a bequest because they had not left much property.
TAB-FULL:v3p137/r1.anchor: عن عروة: أن علي بن أبي طالب، " دخل على ابن عم له يعوده، فقال: إني أريد أن أوصي، فقال علي " لا توص فإنك لم تترك خيرا

TAB-FULL:v3p137/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p137/r2.speaker: عائشة
TAB-FULL:v3p137/r2.claim: ʿĀʾisha sees no surplus for a man with many children who wanted to bequeath when he had four hundred dinars.
TAB-FULL:v3p137/r2.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عيينة أو عتبة، الشك مني «أن رجلا أراد أن يوصي وله ولد كثير، وترك أربعمائة دينار، فقالت عائشة، ما أرى فيه فضلا»

TAB-FULL:v3p137/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p137/r3.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
TAB-FULL:v3p137/r3.claim: Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī places the threshold at five hundred to one thousand dirhams.
TAB-FULL:v3p137/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، عن أبان عن إبراهيم النخعي، في قوله " {إن ترك خيرا} [البقرة: 180] قال: ألف درهم إلى خمسمائة

TAB-FULL:v3p137/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p137/r4.speaker: الزهري
TAB-FULL:v3p137/r4.claim: Al-Zuhrī says the bequest is obligatory regardless of whether the property is little or much.
TAB-FULL:v3p137/r4.anchor: عن الزهري، قال «جعل الله الوصية حقا مما قل منه أو كثر»

TAB-FULL:v3p137/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p137/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v3p137/r5.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers al-Zuhrī's unrestricted view: small and large property both count as khayr, God set no threshold, and every dying person with property must make a proper bequest to non-inheriting parents and kin.
TAB-FULL:v3p137/r5.anchor: ولم يحد الله ذلك بحد ولا خص منه شيئا فيجوز أن يحال ظاهر إلى باطن

TABATABAI:2:180-182/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:180-182/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:180-182/r1.claim: The words ‘written’ and ‘a right’ signal obligation, but limiting the right to the pious weakens a strict duty, which would more naturally be imposed on believers.
TABATABAI:2:180-182/r1.anchor: لسان الآية لسان الوجوب فإن الكتابة تستعمل في القرآن في مورد القطع واللزوم ويؤيده ما في آخر الآية من قوله حقا

TABATABAI:2:180-182/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:180-182/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:180-182/r2.claim: Some say the inheritance verse abrogated this command; if so, only its obligatory force was abrogated, while recommendation and desirability remain, perhaps signaled by ‘upon the pious.’
TABATABAI:2:180-182/r2.anchor: فقد قيل إن الآية منسوخة بآية الإرث، ولو كان كذلك فالمنسوخ هو الفرض دون الندب وأصل المحبوبية

TABATABAI:2:180-182/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:180-182/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:180-182/r3.claim: ‘Good’ means substantial wealth, not a negligible amount.
TABATABAI:2:180-182/r3.anchor: والمراد بالخير المال، وكأنه المال المعتد به، دون اليسير الذي لا يعبأ به

TABATABAI:2:180-182/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:180-182/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:180-182/r4.claim: ‘In a fair manner’ means the customary form of beneficence and kindness.
TABATABAI:2:180-182/r4.anchor: والمراد بالمعروف هو المعروف المتداول من الصنيعة والإحسان

TABATABAI:2:180-182/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:180-182/r8.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
TABATABAI:2:180-182/r8.claim: Asked whether a bequest may be made to an heir, al-Sadiq answered yes and recited this verse; reported by Muhammad ibn Muslim in al-Kafi, al-Tahdhib, and al-Ayyashi’s tafsir.
TABATABAI:2:180-182/r8.anchor: عن محمد بن مسلم عن الصادق عليه السلام سألته عن الوصية تجوز للوارث؟ قال نعم ثم تلا هذه الآية

TABATABAI:2:180-182/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:180-182/r9.speaker: علي عليه السلام
TABATABAI:2:180-182/r9.claim: Ali says that one who dies without bequeathing to non-inheriting relatives has ended his work in disobedience.
TABATABAI:2:180-182/r9.anchor: عن الصادق عن أبيه عن علي عليه السلام قال من لم يوص عند موته لذوي قرابته ممن لا يرث فقد ختم عمله بمعصية

TABATABAI:2:180-182/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:180-182/r10.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
TABATABAI:2:180-182/r10.claim: Al-Sadiq describes a right placed by God in people’s wealth for ‘the possessor of this matter,’ bounded from one-sixth to one-third; al-Saduq also transmits this in al-Faqih.
TABATABAI:2:180-182/r10.anchor: عن الصادق عليه السلام في الآية قال حق جعله الله في أموال الناس لصاحب هذا الأمر

TABATABAI:2:180-182#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:180-182#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:180-182#2/r1.claim: The author links the bequest to 33:6: early inheritance through brotherhood was replaced by kinship, while a good deed to allies remained; the Prophet and his purified descendants count as allies, making this bequest the exception.
