TABATABAI:2:180-182#2/r1.anchor: وقد عدت النبي وليا والطاهرين من ذريته أولياء لهم

TABATABAI:2:180-182#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:180-182#2/r2.speaker: أحدهما عليهما السلام
TABATABAI:2:180-182#2/r2.claim: One of the two Imams says the bequest verse was abrogated by the inheritance shares; al-Tabataba’i reconciles this with other reports by retaining recommendation while dropping only obligation.
TABATABAI:2:180-182#2/r2.anchor: عن أحدهما عليهما السلام في قوله تعالى

TABATABAI:2:184-185#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:184-185#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:184-185#2/r4.claim: Unlike retaliation and bequests, which accord with natural impulses and need no preface, fasting deprives people of food, drink, and sex, so it needs preparatory explanation.
TABATABAI:2:184-185#2/r4.anchor: فإنه يلازم حرمان النفوس من أعظم مشتهياتها ومعظم ما تميل إليها وهو الأكل والشرب والجماع

TUSTARI:2:180/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:2:180/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:2:180/r1.claim: The 'good' left for testamentary bequests means lawful wealth.
TUSTARI:2:180/r1.anchor: ما هذا الخير عندك؟ قال: المال الحلال

AKHFASH:v1p168/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p168/r2.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p168/r2.claim: الوصية is a new clause: if someone leaves property, then the bequest for parents and relatives is due in a proper way.
AKHFASH:v1p168/r2.anchor: ف {الوصية} على الاستئناف، كأنه - والله أعلم -

TABRISI:2:180/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:180/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:180/r1.claim: Maʿrūf is just conduct that cannot rightly be condemned and contains no unfairness or injustice.
TABRISI:2:180/r1.anchor: المعروف هو العدل الذي لا يجوز أن ينكر ولا حيف فيه ولا جور

TABRISI:2:180/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:180/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:180/r2.claim: Ḥuḍūr means that something is present in a way that can be perceived.
TABRISI:2:180/r2.anchor: والحضور وجود الشيء بحيث يمكن أن يدرك

TABRISI:2:180/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:180/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:180/r3.claim: Ḥaqq can mean an act that cannot be denied, or anything known to be sound as a statement, act, or belief; it is the verbal noun of ḥaqqa.
TABRISI:2:180/r3.anchor: والحق هو الفعل الذي لا يجوز إنكاره وقيل هو ما علم صحته سواء كان قولا أو فعلا أو اعتقادا

TABRISI:2:180/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:180/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:180/r4.claim: Kutiba ʿalaykum means ‘and it was prescribed’; the conjunction is omitted because the prior account is complete and this account connects through its subject matter.
TABRISI:2:180/r4.anchor: قوله كتب عليكم المعنى وكتب عليكم إلا أن الكلام إذا طال استغنى عن العطف بالواو

TABRISI:2:180/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:180/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:180/r5.claim: Al-waṣiyya is nominative either as the passive subject of kutiba or as a subject whose predicate is li-l-wālidayn; in the latter parse the statement is quoted as what was prescribed.
TABRISI:2:180/r5.anchor: والوصية ارتفعت لأحد وجهين إما بأنه اسم ما لم يسم فاعله وهو كتب وإما بأنه مبتدأ وقوله للوالدين خبره

TABRISI:2:180/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:180/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:180/r6.claim: The time phrase may attach to kutiba, placing the duty at the onset of illness, or follow al-Zajjāj’s parse: make a will while healthy for implementation when death comes.
TABRISI:2:180/r6.anchor: وأما العامل في إذا ففيه وجهان

TABRISI:2:180/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:180/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:180/r7.claim: Ḥaqqan can be an emphatic verbal noun, a circumstantial adjective meaning ‘rightful’, or a verbal noun from kataba meaning ‘a written obligation’.
TABRISI:2:180/r7.anchor: وحقا نصب على المصدر وتقديره أحق ذلك حقا وقد استعمل على وجه الصفة بمعنى ذي الحق

TABRISI:2:180/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:180/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:180/r8.claim: The verse establishes the law of bequests; ‘when death comes’ means its causes, such as illness or old age, not the moment when death is directly witnessed and the dying person is too occupied to dictate a will.
TABRISI:2:180/r8.anchor: أي أسباب الموت من مرض ونحوه من الهرم

TABRISI:2:180/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:180/r9.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:2:180/r9.claim: Another view makes the bequest obligatory while a person is healthy, with instructions for what should happen when death arrives.
TABRISI:2:180/r9.anchor: وقيل فرض عليكم الوصية في حال الصحة أن تقولوا إذا حضرنا الموت فافعلوا كذا

TABRISI:2:180/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:180/r10.speaker: الزهري
TABRISI:2:180/r10.claim: Al-Zuhrī says the bequest is due for any amount of property, little or much.
TABRISI:2:180/r10.anchor: فقال الزهري في القليل والكثير مما يقع عليه اسم المال

TABRISI:2:180/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:180/r11.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
TABRISI:2:180/r11.claim: Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī sets the relevant property threshold at one thousand to five hundred dirhams.
TABRISI:2:180/r11.anchor: وقال إبراهيم النخعي من ألف درهم إلى خمسمائة

TABRISI:2:180/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:180/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:2:180/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās sets the threshold at eight hundred dirhams.
TABRISI:2:180/r12.anchor: وقال ابن عباس إلى ثمانمائة درهم

TABRISI:2:180/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:180/r13.speaker: علي
TABRISI:2:180/r13.claim: ʿAlī visited a sick client with six or seven hundred dirhams, advised him not to make a will because he did not have much wealth, and the author says this is the adopted position among his school.
TABRISI:2:180/r13.anchor: وروي عن علي ع أنه دخل على مولى له

TABRISI:2:180/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:180/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:180/r14.claim: Fair dealing may refer to a proportionate bequest, since a wealthy person’s bequest of one dirham is not fair, or to choosing recipients justly; both readings apply.
TABRISI:2:180/r14.anchor: ويحتمل أن يرجع ذلك إلى قدر ما يوصي لأن من يملك المال الكثير إذا أوصى بدرهم فلم يوص بالمعروف

TABRISI:2:180/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:180/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:180/r15.claim: Fair distribution also requires not preferring the rich over the poor or a more distant relative over a closer one.
TABRISI:2:180/r15.anchor: أن يوصي للغني ويترك الفقير ويوصي للقريب

TABRISI:2:180/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:180/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:180/r16.claim: The phrase ‘a duty upon the God-fearing’ emphasizes that the bequest is obligatory for those who choose piety.
TABRISI:2:180/r16.anchor: أي حقا واجبا على من آثر التقوى وهذا تأكيد في الوجوب

TABRISI:2:180/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:180/r17.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:180/r17.claim: Three positions are reported: the verse is abrogated, it is abrogated only for heirs but remains for non-heirs, or it is not abrogated; the author endorses the last view.
TABRISI:2:180/r17.anchor: واختلف في هذه الآية فقيل إنها منسوخة وقيل إنها منسوخة في المواريث ثابتة في غير الوارث وقيل إنها غير منسوخة أصلا

TABRISI:2:180/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:180/r18.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:180/r18.claim: The author prefers that the verse remains in force: inheritance and bequest rulings do not conflict, and abrogation requires that the two rulings cannot both be followed.
TABRISI:2:180/r18.anchor: وهو الصحيح عند المحققين من أصحابنا لأن من قال إنها منسوخة بآية المواريث فقوله باطل بأن النسخ بين الخبرين إنما يكون إذا تنافى العمل بموجبهما

TABRISI:2:180#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:180#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:180#2/r1.claim: Tabrisi rejects abrogating the certain Qur'anic rule with a report that, even if sound, establishes only probability.
TABRISI:2:180#2/r1.anchor: فقد أبعد لأن الخبر لو سلم من كل قدح لكان يقتضي الظن ولا يجوز أن ينسخ كتاب الله تعالى

TABRISI:2:180#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:180#2/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:180#2/r2.claim: If the no-bequest-for-an-heir report is accepted despite criticism of its transmitter, it can specify the verse: an heir may receive a bequest up to one third, not beyond it.
TABRISI:2:180#2/r2.anchor: لخصصنا عموم الآية وحملناها على أنه لا وصية لوارث بما يزيد على الثلث

TABRISI:2:180#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:180#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:180#2/r3.claim: Consensus that a bequest is not obligatory does not prove abrogation, since a recommended and encouraged act need not be obligatory.
TABRISI:2:180#2/r3.anchor: الإجماع إنما هو على أنها لا تفيد الفرض وذلك لا يمنع من كونها مندوبا إليها مرغبا فيها

TABRISI:2:180#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:180#2/r4.speaker: أبو جعفر
TABRISI:2:180#2/r4.claim: Asked whether a bequest to an heir is permissible, Abu Jaʿfar answered yes and recited this verse.
TABRISI:2:180#2/r4.anchor: عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام أنه سئل هل تجوز الوصية للوارث فقال: نعم وتلا هذه الآية

TABRISI:2:180#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:180#2/r5.speaker: علي
TABRISI:2:180#2/r5.claim: ʿAlī says that dying without a bequest for close relatives who do not inherit ends one's deeds in disobedience.
TABRISI:2:180#2/r5.anchor: السكوني عن أبي عبد الله عن أبيه عن علي ع قال: من لم يوص عند موته لذوي قرابته

TABRISI:2:180#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:180#2/r6.speaker: النبي
TABRISI:2:180#2/r6.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet says that one who dies without a will dies a death of the pre-Islamic age.
TABRISI:2:180#2/r6.anchor:
النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال:
" من مات بغير وصية مات ميتة جاهلية "

TABRISI:2:180#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:180#2/r7.speaker: النبي
TABRISI:2:180#2/r7.claim: The Prophet is reported to call a person's failure to make a sound will before death a deficiency in character and intellect.
TABRISI:2:180#2/r7.anchor:
النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال:
" من مات بغير وصية مات ميتة جاهلية "
وعنه عليه السلام أنه قال:

TABRISI:2:180#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:180#2/r8.speaker: أبو عبد الله
TABRISI:2:180#2/r8.claim: Abu ʿAbd Allāh says a Muslim should not go to sleep without keeping his will beneath his head.
TABRISI:2:180#2/r8.anchor:
أبي عبد الله عليه السلام أنه قال:
" ما ينبغي لامرىء مسلم أن يبيت إلا ووصيته تحت رأسه "

THALABI:v2p56#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p56#2/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p56#2/r1.claim: Kutiba means prescribed and made obligatory.

THALABI:v2p56#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p56#2/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p56#2/r2.anchor: كتب فرض ووجب. عليكم إذا حضر جاء.

THALABI:v2p56#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p56#2/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p56#2/r3.claim: The arrival of death means its causes, effects, and preliminaries such as illness, not the moment of direct observation.
THALABI:v2p56#2/r3.anchor: يعني اسباب الموت وآثاره ومقدماته من العلل والأمراض ولم يرد المعاينة

THALABI:v2p56#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p56#2/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p56#2/r4.anchor: إن ترك خيرا مالا، نظيره قوله وما تنفقوا من خير

THALABI:v2p56#2/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p56#2/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p56#2/r5.claim: The nominative الوصية has two analyses: it is the passive subject of كتب, or it is the predicate associated with the preposition lām in للوالدين.
THALABI:v2p56#2/r5.anchor: الوصية في رفعها وجهان: أحدهما: اسم ما لم يسم فاعله

THALABI:v2p56#2/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p56#2/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p56#2/r6.claim: Fairness means not exceeding one third and not leaving the poor without a bequest while giving to the rich; Ibn Masud says to prioritize the neediest relatives.
THALABI:v2p56#2/r6.anchor: بالمعروف يعني لا يزيد على الثلث ولا يوصي للغني ويدع الفقير

THALABI:v2p56#2/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p56#2/r7.speaker: ابن مسعود
THALABI:v2p56#2/r7.claim: Ibn Masud says bequests should go first to the neediest relatives.
THALABI:v2p56#2/r7.anchor: كما قال ابن مسعود: الوصية للأخل فالأخل أي الأحوج فالأحوج

THALABI:v2p56#2/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p56#2/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p56#2/r8.claim: Ḥaqqan is parsed as a cognate accusative, as an object declaring the bequest a right, or as an accusative severed from الوصية.
THALABI:v2p56#2/r8.anchor: حقا واجبا، وهو نصب على المصدر أي حق ذلك حقا

THALABI:v2p56#2/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p56#2/r10.speaker: ابن عباس، طاوس، قتادة، الحسن، مسلم بن يسار، العلاء بن زياد، الربيع، ابن زيد
THALABI:v2p56#2/r10.claim: This view holds that bequests to parents and relatives with wealth were initially obligatory; inheritance verses abrogated this for heirs, leaving the obligation for noninheriting kin and parents barred by unbelief or slavery. The Prophet’s no-bequest-to-an-heir ruling explains the change.
THALABI:v2p56#2/r10.anchor: فقال قوم: كانت الوصية للوالدين والأقربين، فرضا واجبا على من مات، وله مال حتى نزلت آية المواريث في سورة النساء

THALABI:v2p56#2/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p56#2/r11.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v2p56#2/r11.claim: After the inheritance verse, the Prophet said God had given each entitled person their due, so there is no bequest to an heir; inheritance and bequest do not combine.
THALABI:v2p56#2/r11.anchor: فخطب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لما نزلت هذه الآية فقال: «الآن الله تعالى قد أعطى كل ذي حق حقه فلا وصية لوارث

THALABI:v2p56#2/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p56#2/r12.speaker: الضحاك
THALABI:v2p56#2/r12.claim: Al-Dahhak says one who dies without bequeathing to relatives ends his work with disobedience.
THALABI:v2p56#2/r12.anchor: قال الضحاك: من مات ولم يوص لذي قرابته فقد ختم عمله بمعصية

THALABI:v2p56#2/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p56#2/r13.speaker: طاوس
THALABI:v2p56#2/r13.claim: Tawus says a bequest to named people that leaves needy relatives unsupported is taken from those named and returned to the relatives.
THALABI:v2p56#2/r13.anchor: وقال طاوس: من أوصى لقوم وسماهم، وترك ذوي قرابته محتاجين

THALABI:v2p57/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p57/r1.speaker: علي، ابن عمر، عائشة، عكرمة، مجاهد، السدي
THALABI:v2p57/r1.claim: This group says inheritance abrogated the whole bequest duty: no one, near or distant, is owed a bequest, though making one is good and omitting it creates no liability.
THALABI:v2p57/r1.anchor: وهذا قول علي وابن عمر وعائشة وعكرمة ومجاهد والسدي

THALABI:v2p57/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p57/r2.speaker: شريح
THALABI:v2p57/r2.claim: Shurayh says a man used to be able to bequeath all his property until the inheritance verse was revealed.
THALABI:v2p57/r2.anchor: قال شريح في هذه الآية. كان الرجل يوصي بماله كله حتى نزلت آية المواريث

THALABI:v2p57/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p57/r3.speaker: علي
THALABI:v2p57/r3.claim: When a sick man asked whether to make a will, Ali urged him to leave his small estate to his dependents, saying that was better for them.
THALABI:v2p57/r3.anchor: فقال علي عليه السلام: إن الله تعالى يقول إن ترك خيرا وإنما يدع شيئا يسير

THALABI:v2p57/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p57/r4.speaker: ابن عمر
THALABI:v2p57/r4.claim: Ibn Umar says he did not make a will; God knew what he would have done with his wealth privately, and he would not let anyone share his property with his children.
THALABI:v2p57/r4.anchor: وروى أيوب عن نافع عن ابن عمر: إنه لم يوص

THALABI:v2p57/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p57/r5.speaker: عائشة
THALABI:v2p57/r5.claim: Aisha advised a man with 3,000 and four dependents to leave the small estate to his family rather than make a will.
THALABI:v2p57/r5.anchor: وروى ابن أبي مليكة: إن رجلا قال لعائشة: إني أريد أن أوصي، قالت: كم مالك؟ قال: ثلاثة آلاف

THALABI:v2p57/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p57/r6.speaker: الربيع بن خثيم
THALABI:v2p57/r6.claim: When Urwa ibn Thabit asked al-Rabiʿ ibn Khuthaym to bequeath him his Quran copy, al-Rabiʿ invoked the priority of blood relatives.
THALABI:v2p57/r6.anchor: قال: فنظر إلى أبيه فقال: أولوا الأرحام بعضهم أولى ببعض

THALABI:v2p57/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p57/r7.speaker: إبراهيم
THALABI:v2p57/r7.claim: Ibrahim says Zubayr and Talha were strict about bequests; the Prophet made no will while Abu Bakr did, and either choice is good.
THALABI:v2p57/r7.anchor: إبراهيم قال: ذكر لنا إن زبيرا وطلحة كانا يشددان في الوصية. فقال: ما كان عليهما أن لا يفعلا

THALABI:v2p59/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p59/r7.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
THALABI:v2p59/r7.claim: At the Farewell Pilgrimage, Saʿd asked the Prophet whether he could bequeath two thirds, then half, and then one third of his wealth; the Prophet permitted one third but called it much, saying wealthy children are better than dependents who beg.
THALABI:v2p59/r7.anchor: وروى عامر بن سعد بن أبي وقاص عن أبيه: قال كنت مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في حجة الوداع

THALABI:v2p59/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p59/r8.speaker: مسروق
THALABI:v2p59/r8.claim: Masruq refused to witness an excessive bequest, saying God apportioned well; one should bequeath to noninheriting relatives and leave the rest under God’s allotment.
THALABI:v2p59/r8.anchor: وقال مسلم بن صبيح: أوصى جار لمسروق فدعا مسروقا ليشهده فوجده قد بذر وأكثر. فقال: لا أشهد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p529/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p529/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p529/r1.claim: In the command about retaliation, kutiba means prescribed and made obligatory, as it does in the bequest verse.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p529/r1.anchor: كتب هاهنا، بمعنى: فرض وأوجب، كقوله: {كتب عليكم إذا حضر أحدكم الموت}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p529/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p529/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p529/r2.claim: The verb comes from writing something down to secure it from being forgotten, so it came to mean firmly imposing an obligation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p529/r2.anchor: وأصله: أن من أراد إحكام شيء والاستيثاق منه كتبه؛ لئلا ينساه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p529/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p529/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p529/r3.claim: Another derivation connects kutiba with God’s decree in the Preserved Tablet, meaning He decreed and settled the matter, as in the cited verses.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p529/r3.anchor: وقيل: أصله: ما كتبه الله في اللوح المحفوظ، ومن هذا قوله: {كتب الله لأغلبن أنا ورسلي}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p529/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p529/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p529/r4.claim: The verb can also mean made or appointed, as in the cited verses about faith, witnesses, and what God will grant.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p529/r4.anchor: ويكون (كتب) بمعنى (¬1): جعل، كقوله: {أولئك كتب في قلوبهم الإيمان}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p544#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p544#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p544#2/r1.claim: The phrase means that someone is certain death is near, sees its signs, and has no doubt it is approaching.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p544#2/r1.anchor: يعني: إذا تيقن حضور الموت، ورأى أعلامه، ولم يشكك في قربه منه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p544#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p544#2/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p544#2/r2.claim: Death’s arrival refers to its causes and preliminaries, such as illness; bequest was obligatory earlier but becomes urgent when those signs arise and may not be delayed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p544#2/r2.anchor: يريد: أسباب الموت ومقدماته، من العلل والأمراض. وكان الإيصاء فرضا قبل نزول أسباب الموت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p544#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p544#2/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p544#2/r3.claim: The phrasing does not mean the duty began only at death’s onset: al-waṣiyya can mean the act of bequeathing, or the long separation between verb and noun can compensate for the feminine ending.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p544#2/r3.anchor: لأنه أراد بالوصية الإيصاء، أو للفصل بين الفعل والوصية؛ لأن الكلام لما طال

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p544#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p544#2/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p544#2/r4.claim: Al-waṣiyya is nominative either as a passive construction or as the subject, with li-l-wālidayn as its predicate; either whole clause is governed by kutiba.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p544#2/r4.anchor: ورفع {الوصية} من وجهين: أحدهما: على ما لم يسم فاعله، والثاني: على الابتداء، ويكون {للوالدين} الخبر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p545/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p545/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p545/r1.claim: Khayr is a general term for property and other good things, but often denotes money in the Qurʾan, as in 2:272, 100:8, and 28:24.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p545/r1.anchor: الخير: اسم جامع للمال وغيره، والخير يراد به المال في كثير من القرآن،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p545/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p545/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p545/r2.claim: The bequest should be in a fair amount that discerning people recognize as free of injustice; it must not exceed one third.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p545/r2.anchor: أي: بالشيء الذي يعلم ذوو التمييز أنه لا حيف فيه، فهو العدل الذي لا ينكر، يعني: لا يزيد على الثلث

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p545/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p545/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p545/r3.claim: Ḥaqqan affirms that this is genuinely incumbent on you.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p545/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p545/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p545/r4.claim: The people described as God-fearing are believers who avoid associationism.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p545/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p545/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p545/r5.claim: Scholars agree that the verse’s ruling was abrogated, though they later differ over whether the abrogation covered all bequests or only those to heirs.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p545/r5.anchor: وقد اجتمعت العلماء على نسخ هذه الآية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p545/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p545/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p545/r6.claim: The occasion was that pre-Islamic Arabs ostentatiously bequeathed wealth to distant people while leaving dependents destitute; the verse redirected bequests to family and kin until inheritance verses replaced that rule.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p545/r6.anchor: وكان السبب في نزول هذه الآية: أن أهل الجاهلية كانوا يوصون بمالهم للبعداء رياء وسمعة، ويتركون العيال عالة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p545/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p545/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p545/r7.claim: The inheritance rules abrogated the mandatory bequest to parents and other relatives who inherit, in light of the Prophetic rule that no heir receives a bequest.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p545/r7.anchor: فأجمعوا على نسخ الوصية للوالدين والأقربين الذين يرثون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p545/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p545/r8.speaker: مسلم بن يسار والعلاء بن زياد ومسروق والحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p545/r8.claim: These authorities hold that the bequest duty remains for kin who do not inherit, including parents excluded by unbelief or enslavement; al-Ḍaḥḥāk says dying without such a bequest ends one’s work in sin.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p545/r8.anchor: وهو (¬2) مذهب مسلم بن يسار، والعلاء بن زياد (¬3) (¬4)، ومسروق (¬5) والحسن (¬6)، حتى قال # الضحاك: من مات ولم يوص لذي قرابته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p545/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p545/r9.speaker: طاوس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p545/r9.claim: Ṭāwūs says that when someone bequeaths to outsiders while leaving kin, the gift should be taken from the outsiders and returned to the relatives.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p545/r9.anchor: وقال طاوس: إن أوصى للأجانب (¬2) وترك ذوي قرابته نزع منهم، ورد إلى ذوي قرابته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p545/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p545/r10.speaker: الأكثرون من العلماء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p545/r10.claim: The majority, whose position the author says is practiced today, hold that the whole ruling is abrogated: no bequest is required for any relative or stranger, though one may be made for anyone except an heir.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p545/r10.anchor: والأكثرون من العلماء -وهو الذي يعمل به اليوم- على أن حكم الآية كله (¬5) منسوخ، ولا تجب على أحد وصية لأحد قريب ولا بعيد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p548/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p548/r1.speaker: أبو عبيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p548/r1.claim: Abū ʿUbayd reports consensus among scholars of the Ḥijāz, Tihāma, Iraq, and Syria, including Sufyān, Mālik, al-Awzāʿī, and al-Layth: bequests are permitted for all except heirs but are not obligatory.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p548/r1.anchor: قال أبو عبيد: وعلى هذا القول أجمعت العلماء من أهل الحجاز وتهامة والعراق والشام، منهم سفيان ومالك الأوزاعي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p548/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p548/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p548/r2.anchor: والخير في هذه الآية حمل على المال الكثير

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p548/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p548/r3.speaker: علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p548/r3.claim: When an ill man wanted to bequeath, ʿAlī cited the verse and advised him to leave his small amount to his dependents because that was better.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p548/r3.anchor: فقد روي عن علي رضي الله عنه أنه دخل على مريض يعوده، فقال: إني أريد أن أوصي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p548/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p548/r4.speaker: عائشة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p548/r4.claim: ʿĀʾisha told a man with three thousand and four dependents that this was only a small amount and he should leave it to his family.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p548/r4.anchor: وروي أيضا أن رجلا قال لعائشة رضي الله عنها: إني أريد أن أوصي، قالت: كم مالك؟ قال: ثلاثة آلاف

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p72#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p72#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p72#2/r1.claim: Khayr here means property or wealth.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p72#2/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p72#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p72#2/r2.claim: The bequest is to be made for parents and relatives in a fair amount, without extravagance or harm.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p72#2/r2.anchor: أي يوصي لهم ويقتصد في ذلك، لا يسرف ولا يضر.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p72#2/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p72#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p72#2/r3.claim: This bequest rule was abrogated by the inheritance rules.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p72#2/r3.anchor: لا يسرف ولا يضر. وهذه منسوخة بالمواريث.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:179-180/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:179-180/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:179-180/r4.claim: The verse responded to pre-Islamic Arabs who left their relatives poor while bequeathing wealth to distant people for show and reputation.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:179-180/r4.anchor: كان أهل الجاهلية يوصون بمالهم للبعداء رياء وسمعة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:179-180/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:179-180/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:179-180/r5.claim: The bequest was initially prescribed and made obligatory.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:179-180/r5.anchor: فرض عليكم وأوجب { إذا حضر أحدكم الموت }

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:179-180/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:179-180/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:179-180/r6.claim: Death arriving means its causes and preliminaries have appeared.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:179-180/r6.anchor: إذا حضر أحدكم الموت } أي: أسبابه ومقدماته

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:179-180/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:179-180/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:179-180/r8.claim: A bequest to parents and relatives should be reasonable and must not exceed one third of the estate.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:179-180/r8.anchor: يعني: لا يزيد على الثلث { حقا } أي: حق ذلك حقا

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:179-180/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:179-180/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:179-180/r9.claim: The duty is placed on the God-fearing, whom the author characterizes here as those who avoid associating partners with God.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:179-180/r9.anchor: على المتقين } الذين يتقون الشرك، وهذه الآية

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:179-180/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:179-180/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:179-180/r10.claim: The inheritance verse abrogated this rule; a bequest is not obligatory and may not be made for an heir.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:179-180/r10.anchor: ولا تجب الوصية على أحد، [ولا تجوز الوصية للوارث]

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p256/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p256/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p256/r1.claim: كتاب originally denotes what God wrote on the Preserved Tablet concerning what will come to pass.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p256/r1.anchor: ما كتبه الله في اللوح مما هو كائن.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p256/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p256/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p256/r2.claim: كتب can mean decreed or settled, as when God decreed victory, allotted fate, or those destined for death.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p256/r2.anchor: ثم تتفرع منه معان ترجع إلى هذا الأصل. كقوله:

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p256/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p256/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p256/r3.claim: In this verse and other commands, كتب means prescribed as an obligation.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p256/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p256/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p256/r4.claim: كتب may mean made or placed, as when God placed faith in people's hearts.

ELMALILI:2:180-182/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:180-182/r1.claim: The phrase means death has approached and shown its signs, during the illness of death.
ELMALILI:2:180-182/r1.anchor: herhangi birinize ölüm hâzır olduğu, yani yaklaşıp emârelerini gösterdiği demde, maraz-ı mevt hengâmında

ELMALILI:2:180-182/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:180-182/r2.claim: Here khayr means property left after death, especially a substantial estate.
ELMALILI:2:180-182/r2.anchor: eğer bir hayır terk ederse; ba‘de’l-mevt mal bırakacak, hatta çok bir mal bırakacak olursa

ELMALILI:2:180-182/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:180-182/r3.claim: A bequest for parents and near relatives must follow what is recognized as fair, avoiding excess, deficiency, injustice, and harm that causes alienation or disappointment.
ELMALILI:2:180-182/r3.anchor: mâruf vechile, yani ifrât u tefritten, tevahhuş ve inkisârı mûcib cevrden ‘ârî, adalet dairesinde vasiyet yapmak

ELMALILI:2:180-182/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:180-182/r4.claim: Carrying out this fair bequest is an obligatory right upon the God-fearing.

ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r1.claim: Wasiyyah began as a verbal noun meaning entrusting or recommending, then came to name the thing bequeathed.
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r1.anchor: “Vasiyyet”, lügaten masdar, yani îsâ’ ve tavsiye mânasına bir isimdir. Sonra مُوصَى بِهِ mânasına isim olmuştur

ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r2.claim: Îsâʾ and tavsiye mean asking someone to do something during one’s absence, in life or after death; Turkish calls this ısmarlamak.
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r2.anchor: “Îsâ’” ve “tavsiye” lügaten bir kimsenin hayâtı veya memâtı ile gaybûbeti hâlinde diğerlerinden bir şey yapmasını talep eylemektir

ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r3.claim: In legal usage, îsâ with lām means transferring ownership after death; with ilā it means delegating posthumous management of property and children’s affairs.
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r3.anchor: Şer‘an îsâ’ لِفُلَاَنٍ gibi لاَم ile veya إِلَى فُلَاَنٍ gibi إِلَى ile isti‘mâline göre iki mânaya gelir

ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r4.claim: Because the verse uses lām, its wasiyyah means giving another person ownership of property after death.
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r4.anchor: Bu âyette ise لاَم ile isti‘mâl edilmiş olduğundan birinci mânayadır

ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r5.claim: Khayr is agreed here to mean property: lexically it is anything beneficial, and Qurʾanic usage can use it specifically for wealth.

ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r6.claim: Scholars disagree whether the qualifying wealth includes any amount or only substantial property.
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r6.anchor: Ancak burada hayır denilen mal, aza çoğa şâmil ‘ale’l-ıtlâk mal mıdır, yoksa mâl-ı kesîr midir? Bunda ihtilâf edilmiştir

ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r7.speaker: Zührî
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r7.claim: Zührī is cited among those who take the condition to cover wealth without a minimum threshold.
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r7.anchor: Zührî’den rivayet olunduğu üzere mutlak diyenler çoktur

ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r8.speaker: Hazret-i Ali
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r8.claim: Ali reportedly told a dying freedman with six or seven hundred dirhams that he need not bequeath, since he had no substantial wealth.
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r8.anchor: Hazret-i Ali “hayır, Allah teâlâ إِن تَرَكَ خَيْرًا buyurmuştur, senin ise çok malın yoktur” demiştir

ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r9.speaker: Hazret-i Ali
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r9.claim: A report from Ali says four thousand dirhams or less counts as ordinary maintenance funds.
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r9.anchor: Hazret-i Ali’den mervîdir ki “dört bin dirhem ve mâdûnu nafakadır” demiş

ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r10.speaker: İbn Abbas
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas reportedly held that a person with eight hundred dirhams need not make a bequest.
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r10.anchor: İbn Abbas hazretleri “sekiz yüz dirhemde vasiyet yoktur” demiş

ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r11.speaker: Hazret-i Âişe
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r11.claim: Asked about a woman with four children and three thousand dirhams, Aisha judged the sum insufficient to count as surplus wealth for a bequest.
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r11.anchor: Hazret-i Âişe radıyallahu ‘anhâ dahi vasiyet etmek isteyen ve çocuğu var, malı da az diye ehli tarafından men‘olunan bir kadın hakkında

ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r12.claim: Elmalılı takes these reports as evidence that khayr here means substantial wealth.
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r12.anchor: ki bunlar hayrın mâl-ı kesîr mânasına olduğuna delâlet etmektedirler

ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r13.claim: If any possession counted, the condition would add little, since nearly everyone leaves at least food or clothing.
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r13.anchor: Fi’l-vâki böyle olmasa idi إِن تَرَكَ خَيْرًا şartı pek müfîd olmazdı. Zîrâ bir ekmek veya setr-i avret edecek bir bez parçası olsun

ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r14.speaker: bazıları
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r14.claim: Some scholars considered the bequest recommended rather than obligatory because determining wealth and proper allocation requires judgment; Elmalılı rejects that view.
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r14.anchor: hayır, mâruf gibi takdîre, re’y ü ictihâda mütevakkıf olan bazı şartlardan dolayı bu vasiyetin vâcib değil mendub olduğuna kāil olanlar dahi bulunmuş ise de doğru değildir

ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r15.claim: The words kutiba, alaykum, and haqqan each indicate obligation, so the recommended-only view is wrong.
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r15.anchor: حَقًّا,عَلَيْكُمْ,كُتِبَ, عَلَيْكُمْ kelimelerinden her biri vücûba dâldir

ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r16.claim: The verse legislated as a religious duty that owners make a suitable financial bequest for parents and relatives.
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r16.anchor: mal sâhiplerinin ebeveyn ve akrabînine vech-i ma‘rûf ile sûret-i lâyıkada bir vasiyyet-i mâliye yapması bir farîza-i dîniye olarak teşrî‘kılınmış idi

ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r17.claim: The duty protects parenthood and kinship, especially the closest ties, from rupture; Elmalılı reads this wisdom from the lām construction.
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r17.anchor: vilâdet ve karâbet, daha doğrusu akrebiyet hakkı ve câmi‘a-i karâbetin kuvvet ve derecesine göre halelden vikāyesi olduğu da lâm’ın mânasından anlaşılmaktadır

ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r18.claim: The amount judged proper was initially left to the dying person’s judgment and bequest.
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r18.anchor: hakkın mâruf vechile ta‘yîn-i mikdârı vefat edecek kimsenin re’yine

ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r19.claim: Later inheritance verses in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ fixed these shares, relieving people of deciding them at death and reducing the risk of resentment among relatives.
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r19.anchor: Sûre-i Nisâ’da gelecek olan mîras âyetleri ile Cenâb-ı Allah bu hakkın mikdarlarını bizzat tâyin etmiş

ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r20.claim: Inheritance law strengthened the kinship and parenthood right, while abrogating bequests to relatives who inherit.
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r20.anchor: burada vücûbu müekkeden gösterilen hakk-ı karâbet ve vilâdet daha ziyade takviye edilmiş ve fakat vâris olacak akraba hakkında vasiyet neshedilmiştir

ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r21.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r21.speaker: Aleyhissalâtü vesselâm Efendimiz
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r21.claim: At the Farewell Pilgrimage sermon, the Prophet said God had given each rights-holder their due and there is no bequest for an heir.

ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r22.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r22.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r22.claim: Elmalılı says this widely transmitted and received hadith has the status of mass transmission and was accepted and acted upon by consensus.
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r22.anchor: bu hadîs-i şerîf ümmette meşhur ve müstefîz olduğundan dolayı mütevâtir hükmündedir. Ve ümmet bunu ittifak ile telakkī bi’l-kabul ederek ma‘mûlün-bih tutmuştur

ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r23.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r23.speaker: Aleyhissalâtü vesselâm Efendimiz
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r23.claim: The Prophet also said a bequest for an heir is invalid unless the other heirs approve; a group of Companions transmitted this hadith, according to Ahkām al-Qurʾān.
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r23.anchor: Vârise vasiyet câiz olmaz meğer ki sâir verese

ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r24.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r24.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r24.claim: Therefore, the bequest to heirs was abrogated either by the inheritance verses’ implication or by the explicit wording of these hadiths.
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r24.anchor: vârise vasiyet mîras âyetlerinin işâreti veya bu hadislerin ibaresi ile mensuh olmuştur

ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r25.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r25.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r25.claim: The majority of commentators and authoritative jurists say the duty is wholly abrogated.
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r25.anchor: Ekser-i müfessirîn ve fukahâ-yı mu‘teberîne göre bâkī değildir, nesih umûmîdir

ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r26.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r26.speaker: Hasan-ı Basrî, Mesrûk, Tâvûs, Dahhâk, Müslim b. Yesâr, Alâ b. Ziyâd
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r26.claim: These early authorities hold that the duty was abrogated for heir relatives but remains for non-heir relatives, a partial rather than total abrogation.
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r26.anchor: Hasan-ı Basrî, Mesrûk, Tâvûs, Dahhâk, Müslim b. Yesâr, Alâ b. Ziyâd hazerâtı buna kāildirler

ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r27.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r27.speaker: İbn Abbas
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r27.claim: Two reports from Ibn Abbas place him respectively with the majority and minority positions.
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r27.anchor: İbn Abbas hazretlerinden de biri ekseriyetle, biri ekalliyetle beraber olduğuna dair iki rivayet vardır

ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r28.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r28.speaker: Dahhâk
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r28.claim: Dahhak says a person who dies without bequeathing to relatives ends his deeds in sin.
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r28.anchor: Dahhâk demiştir ki “akrabasına vasiyet etmeden vefat eden kimse amelini masiyet ile hatm eylemiş

ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r29.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r29.speaker: Tâvus
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r29.claim: Tawus says that if someone bequeaths to outsiders while leaving relatives out, the bequest is taken from the outsiders and returned to the relatives.
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r29.anchor: Tâvûs dahi “bir kimse akrabasını bırakıp da ecânibe vasiyet ederse

ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r30.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r30.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r30.claim: The minority’s first proof is that the verse generally obligates a bequest to relatives; inheritance verses, the heir hadith, or consensus remove heirs, but no abrogating proof removes non-heir relatives.
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r30.anchor: Bunların iki delîli vardır; evvelâ, bu âyet ‘ale’l-‘umûm akrabaya vasiyetin vücûbuna dâldir. Vâris olan akraba hakkında

ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r31.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r31.speaker: Peygamber
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r31.claim: A Prophetic report says a Muslim with property should not pass two nights without having a written bequest.
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r31.anchor: Malı bulunan müslimin vasiyeti yazılmış olarak yanında bulunmadıkça

ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r32.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r32.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r32.claim: The minority infers the obligatory bequest must concern relatives, since bequests to outsiders are unanimously not obligatory; they say the Sunnah reinforces the Qurʾanic duty.
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r32.anchor: Ecânibe vasiyet vâcib olmadığı mücma‘un ‘aleyh bulunduğundan bu vasiyyet-i vâcibenin ekāribe muhtas olması lâzım gelir

ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r33.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r33.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r33.claim: The majority begins by noting that the inheritance passage also names parents and relatives as recipients of fixed shares.
ELMALILI:2:180-182#2/r33.anchor: Cumhûrun istidlâline gelince, bu da müte‘addiddir. Evvelâ, burada لِلْوَٰلِدَيْنِ وَٱلْأَقْرَبِينَ buyurulduğu gibi mîras âyetlerinin başında da

ELMALILI:2:180-182#3/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182#3/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:180-182#3/r1.claim: The majority argues 4:7 uses the same parent-and-relative categories and assigns men and women fixed shares from any-sized estate; this fixed inheritance right replaces the bequest duty, so abrogation is total.
ELMALILI:2:180-182#3/r1.anchor: Vâlideyn ve akrabîn unvânı her ikisinde müsâvîdir ve bunların az veya çok terikeden farz birer nasibleri bulunduğu ibtidâ icmâlen gösterilmiş, sâniyen tafsîlen tâyin edilmiştir

ELMALILI:2:180-182#3/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182#3/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:180-182#3/r2.claim: The majority’s second proof is that inheritance law defines kinship rights and excludes distant relatives, leaving no mandatory bequest duty for nonheirs to survive abrogation.
ELMALILI:2:180-182#3/r2.anchor: vasiyeti îcab eden hakk-ı karâbeti mîras âyetleri tâyin etmiştir. Bununla mîrasta dâhil olmayan uzak akrabanın sâhib-i hak olmadığı da tebeyyün eylemiştir

ELMALILI:2:180-182#3/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182#3/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:180-182#3/r3.claim: The majority reads al-aqrabīn as a relational superlative for the nearest relatives, so distant relatives were not originally included in the bequest duty.
ELMALILI:2:180-182#3/r3.anchor: وَٱلْأَقْرَبِينَ ism-i tafdîli izâfî bir mâna ifade ederek en yakın akrabayı gösterir

ELMALILI:2:180-182#3/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182#3/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:180-182#3/r4.claim: The majority’s third proof says the indefinite wasiyyah in 4:11 cannot be identified with this verse’s specific obligatory bequest.
ELMALILI:2:180-182#3/r4.anchor: bu vasiyet nekre olduğundan dolayı bundan murad burada vâcib olan ٱلْوَصِيَّةُ’tir denemez

ELMALILI:2:180-182#3/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182#3/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:180-182#3/r5.claim: If no bequest is made, the entire estate is the heirs’ lawful right; by implication, other relatives have no entitlement that could make a bequest obligatory.
ELMALILI:2:180-182#3/r5.anchor: şer‘an vasiyet bulunmayabilir ve bir vasiyet bulunmadığı takdirde bütün terike vârislerin hakk-ı meşrû‘u olacaktır

ELMALILI:2:180-182#3/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182#3/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:180-182#3/r6.claim: Although Rāzī reports this as analogy, Elmalılı calls it an implication of the text that entails abrogation and says it is the strongest argument.
ELMALILI:2:180-182#3/r6.anchor: bu bir kıyas değil, işâret-i nastır. Ve işâret-i nas dahi neshi ifade eder

ELMALILI:2:180-182#3/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182#3/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:180-182#3/r7.claim: The majority’s fourth proof is that the bequest hadith predates the inheritance rules and its obligation was abrogated; a bequest to non-heir kin is at least recommended.
ELMALILI:2:180-182#3/r7.anchor: zikr olunan hadîs-i şerif dahi bu âyet gibi ahkâm-ı mîrastan evvel vârid olmuştur, vücûbu mensuhtur. Ma‘amâfîh bu ihtilâftan şu neticeye vâsıl oluruz

ELMALILI:2:180-182#3/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182#3/r8.speaker: Ebû Müslim-i İsfahânî
ELMALILI:2:180-182#3/r8.claim: Abu Muslim uniquely dissents from the exegetical consensus, holding that the verse’s bequest obligation was not abrogated.
ELMALILI:2:180-182#3/r8.anchor: Müfessirîn içinde yalnız Ebû Müslim-i İsfahânî icmâ‘a muhalefet ederek bu âyetteki vücûb-ı vasiyet hükmünün mensuh olmadığına kāil olmuş

ELMALILI:2:180-182#3/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182#3/r9.speaker: Ebû Müslim-i İsfahânî
ELMALILI:2:180-182#3/r9.claim: Abu Muslim’s first interpretation is that the bequest here means God’s inheritance assignment for parents and relatives in 4:11.
ELMALILI:2:180-182#3/r9.anchor: Müfessirîn içinde yalnız Ebû Müslim-i İsfahânî icmâ‘a muhalefet ederek bu âyetteki vücûb-ı vasiyet hükmünün mensuh olmadığına kāil olmuş

ELMALILI:2:180-182#3/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182#3/r10.speaker: Ebû Müslim-i İsfahânî
ELMALILI:2:180-182#3/r10.claim: Alternatively, Abu Muslim says the dying person must ensure parents and relatives receive their full inheritance shares without concealment or reduction.
ELMALILI:2:180-182#3/r10.anchor: Müfessirîn içinde yalnız Ebû Müslim-i İsfahânî icmâ‘a muhalefet ederek bu âyetteki vücûb-ı vasiyet hükmünün mensuh olmadığına kāil olmuş

ELMALILI:2:180-182#3/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182#3/r11.speaker: Ebû Müslim-i İsfahânî
ELMALILI:2:180-182#3/r11.claim: He argues that inheritance and a testator’s bequest can coexist as separate gifts, one from God and one from the dying person, so heirs may receive both.

ELMALILI:2:180-182#3/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182#3/r12.speaker: Ebû Müslim-i İsfahânî
ELMALILI:2:180-182#3/r12.claim: If the rules conflict, Abu Muslim says inheritance law specifies the earlier duty by excluding heirs while leaving non-heir relatives within its scope.
ELMALILI:2:180-182#3/r12.anchor: Müfessirîn içinde yalnız Ebû Müslim-i İsfahânî icmâ‘a muhalefet ederek bu âyetteki vücûb-ı vasiyet hükmünün mensuh olmadığına kāil olmuş

ELMALILI:2:180-182#3/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182#3/r13.speaker: Ebû Müslim-i İsfahânî
ELMALILI:2:180-182#3/r13.claim: He includes relatives barred from inheritance by religious difference, slavery, murder, displacement by a nearer heir, or status as distant kin without fixed shares.
ELMALILI:2:180-182#3/r13.anchor: ihtilâf-ı din, rık, katl gibi esbâb-ı mâni‘a dolayısıyla vâris olmayanlar da bulunabilir. Akrabanın dahi ashâb-ı ferâizden oldukları hâlde

ELMALILI:2:180-182#3/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182#3/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:180-182#3/r14.claim: The discussion reinforces kinship duties with Qurʾanic commands to maintain family ties and give relatives their due.
ELMALILI:2:180-182#3/r14.anchor: kavl-i kerîmleriyle bunu tekid de etmiştir

ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r1.claim: Elmalılı says Abu Muslim’s position in substance defends the minority’s partial abrogation, but calling it specification is wrong because inheritance verses came later, so the ruling was partly abrogated.
ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r1.anchor: bu zat en nihâyet kısmen neshe kāil olan ekalliyet mezhebini müdafaa etmiş ve fakat buna “nesih” demeyip “tahsis” tâbir eylemiştir. Hâlbuki tahsis târihen mukārin

ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r2.claim: Inheritance’s fixed shares prohibit increase or decrease, so its obligation conflicts with an unrestricted duty to bequeath to an heir; permission with other heirs’ consent does not remove that conflict.
ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r2.anchor: “nasîb-i mefrûz”, “farîza” buyurulmuş olması ziyade ve noksanı kat‘iyyetle mâni‘olduğundan yalnız vücûb-ı mîras, vücûb-ı vasiyete münâfîdir

ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r3.claim: Abu Muslim’s first interpretation gives this verse no meaning beyond inheritance verses; Elmalılı says that neglects rather than preserves the disputed ruling and effectively admits its total abrogation.
ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r3.anchor: bu âyetin mîras âyetlerinden başka hüküm

ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r4.claim: Elmalılı attributes Abu Muslim’s denial of Qurʾanic abrogation to reading 2:106 as limited by context to earlier scriptures and notes some contemporary Egyptian writers follow him.
ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r4.anchor: siyâk karînesiyle kütüb ü şerâyi‘-i sâlifeye kasr u tahsis ile Kur’an’da hükmü mensuh âyet bulunmadığını

ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r5.claim: The unrestricted wording of 2:106 is explicit in its scope; context cannot restrict the apparent wording, and denial of Qurʾanic abrogation produces a contradiction.
ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r5.anchor: مَا نَنسَخْ مِنْ ءَايَةٍ nazmı ıtlâkında zâhir, mâ-sîka lehinde nastır ve siyâk-ı nas zâhir-i nassı tahsis ve takyid etmez

ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r6.speaker: Cessâs Ebû Bekir Râzî
ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r6.claim: Cessās reports that some later non-jurists claimed Muhammad’s law contains no abrogation, and that examples instead abrogate earlier prophets’ laws, such as prayer direction.
ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r6.anchor: Müfessirînden ve e‘âzım-ı fukahâ-yı Hanefiyyeden Cessâs Ebû Bekir Râzî hazretleri

ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r7.speaker: Cessâs Ebû Bekir Râzî
ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r7.claim: Cessās says Muslims across generations understood and transmitted many abrogated rulings without doubt, just as they accepted general and specific or clear and ambiguous passages.
ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r7.anchor: Müfessirînden ve e‘âzım-ı fukahâ-yı Hanefiyyeden Cessâs Ebû Bekir Râzî hazretleri

ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r8.speaker: Cessâs Ebû Bekir Râzî
ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r8.claim: Cessās calls the denial outside the received consensus and strained interpretation, while describing its proponent as sound in belief and not acting from bad intent.
ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r8.anchor: Müfessirînden ve e‘âzım-ı fukahâ-yı Hanefiyyeden Cessâs Ebû Bekir Râzî hazretleri

ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r9.speaker: Cessâs Ebû Bekir Râzî
ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r9.claim: Cessās speculates that the dissenter lacked knowledge of jurisprudence, legal method, chronology, and transmitted scholarship, and relied too quickly on personal opinion.
ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r9.anchor: Müfessirînden ve e‘âzım-ı fukahâ-yı Hanefiyyeden Cessâs Ebû Bekir Râzî hazretleri

ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r10.speaker: Peygamber
ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r10.claim: Cessās invokes the Prophetic warning that one who speaks about the Qurʾan from personal opinion errs even if correct.

ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r11.claim: Elmalılı says Abu Muslim Isfahani is the only scholar known to deny abrogation in this way.
ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r11.anchor: evvel ve âhir ulemâ-yı İslâm içinde bu suretle neshi inkâr eden Ebû Müslim İsfahânî’den başka bir kimse yoktur

ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r12.claim: On Abu Muslim’s account, the verse cannot be applied while taking inheritance law into account.
ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r12.anchor: Bunun re’yine göre de mîrâsı hesâba katmadan yalnız

ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r13.claim: Early Islam may have had no inheritance at all, or inheritance only for children; in either case a bequest was required for parents and other relatives, with children outside al-aqrabīn in the second scenario.
ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r13.anchor: bidâyet-i İslâm’da bu âyet mûcebince ya mîras hiç yoktu da evlâd da dâhil olduğu hâlde vâlideyn ve akrabaya ber vech-i ma‘rûf bir vasiyet farz kılınmış idi

ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r14.claim: Elmalılı says the earlier reports from Ali and Aisha support this account of the original rule.
ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r14.anchor: Bâlâda Hazret-i Ali ve Hazret-i Âişe’den mervî olan kelâmlar dahi bunu teyid eylemektedir

ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r15.claim: It is uncertain rather than certain that children and distant non-heir relatives fall within the general meaning of al-aqrabīn.
ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r15.anchor: evlâd ile gayr-i vâris uzak akrabanın “akrabîn” mefhûm-ı ‘âmmında duhûlleri kat‘î değil, meşkuk veya maznundur

ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r16.claim: Once inheritance was extended beyond children, the definite bequest obligation was abrogated, while kinship rights were further secured.
ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r16.anchor: Mîras âyetleri mûcebince irsin evlâddan mâ‘adâya da teşmîli ile bu âyette kat‘î olan vücûb-i vasiyyet neshedilmiş ve ma‘amâfîh hakk-ı karâbet daha ziyade tevsik olunmuştur

ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r17.claim: Only the explicit rule making a financial bequest obligatory is wholly abrogated; other implications and indications may still operate under legal method.
ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r17.anchor: külliyen mensuh olduğu beyan edilen hüküm de yalnız bi-vechin vasiyyet-i mâliyenin vücûbuna ait bulunan ve bi’l-ibâre sâbit olan hükümdür. İşârât ve delâlât-ı sâiresi ile kavâ‘id-i usûliye dairesinde amel edilebilir

ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r18.claim: Although khayr is explicit in the wording as property, its implications and indications extend to broader meanings.
ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r18.anchor: خَيْرًا kelimesi bi’l-ibâre مَال ile müfesser olmakla beraber işâret veya delâletiyle daha vâsi‘dir

ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r19.claim: In some cases and for some people, bequests to discharge obligations owed to God or people, including debts and deposits, remain obligatory; this verse also grounds other bequest rulings.
ELMALILI:2:180-182#4/r19.anchor: Dinde hukūk-ı ‘ibâd ve hukūk-ı ilâhiyeye müte‘allik duyûn u emânât ve sâir hukūkun kazâsına müte‘allik bazı vasiyetlerin vâcib olduğu ahvâl ve eşhâs da vardır

ELMALILI:2:180-182#5/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182#5/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:180-182#5/r1.claim: Execution of a lawful bequest made in a recognized manner is obligatory for those concerned besides the testator, whether making it was obligatory, recommended, or merely permissible.
ELMALILI:2:180-182#5/r1.anchor: Esâsı gerek vâcib ve gerek mendub veya mubah olsun ber vech-i ma‘rûf yapılmış olan bir vasiyyet-i meşrû‘anın tenfîzi

ELMALILI:2:180-182#5/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182#5/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:180-182#5/r7.claim: The earlier obligation to make a bequest was abrogated, but these verses do not abrogate the continuing duty to execute a lawful bequest.
ELMALILI:2:180-182#5/r7.anchor: evvelki âyetteki vücûb-ı vasiyet mensuh olmakla beraber bu âyette nesih yoktur, vücûb-ı tenfîz bâkīdir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r1.claim: Before Islam, sons inherited all property when present; otherwise it went to the nearest male relatives, from closest outward.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r1.anchor: Ölenin erkek çocukları varsa bütün mirası onlar alırlardı. Erkek çocuğu olmayanın malı yakından uzağa doğru diğer erkek akrabasına kalırdı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r2.claim: Pre-Islamic Arabs sometimes also bequeathed property to children, relatives, or friends.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r2.anchor: Bazan vasiyet yoluyla çocuklara, akrabaya ve arkadaşlara da mal bırakıldığı olurdu

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r3.claim: The verse initially required bequests to all relatives, male and female, especially parents, preparing believers for the later inheritance rules.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r3.anchor: Bu âyet başta ana ve baba olmak üzere, kadın erkek ayırımı yapmadan bütün akrabaya vasiyet etmenin gerekli bulunduğunu ifade ederek müminleri

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r4.claim: The inheritance passage in Nisa included female relatives among heirs and, with related verses and hadiths, set fixed, unalterable inheritance shares.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r4.anchor: Nisâ sûresindeki miras âyeti (4/11 vd.), zaten mirastan pay almakta olan bu erkekleri doğrudan zikretmeksizin kadın akrabayı da mirasa dahil etti

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r5.speaker: Hz. Peygamber
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r5.claim: At the Farewell Pilgrimage, the Prophet said each rightful claimant had received their due and there was no bequest for an heir, barring bequests to relatives with fixed inheritance rights.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r5.anchor: Allah her hak sahibine hakkını vermiştir, artık vâris olana vasiyetle mal bırakmak yoktur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r6.speaker: Hz. Peygamber
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r6.claim: When Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas proposed bequeathing all his property, the Prophet told him to limit it to one-third and said leaving relatives wealthy is better than leaving them destitute and begging.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r6.anchor: Yakınlarını zengin olarak bırakman, onları halka el avuç açan yoksullar olarak bırakmandan daha iyidir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r7.claim: The Saʿd report shows that a person with heirs should not bequeath all their property.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r7.anchor: vârisleri olan bir kimsenin bütün malını vasiyet etmesinin uygun olmadığı ortaya çıkmıştır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r8.speaker: müctehidler çoğunluğu
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r8.claim: Most jurists, including the four imams, say bequest was first obligatory but inheritance verses partly changed the rule, leaving bequests recommended rather than obligatory.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r8.anchor: Dört mezhep imamının da dahil bulunduğu müctehidler çoğunluğu bu hükmü benimsemişlerdir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r9.speaker: Dahhâk, Tâvûs, Taberî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r9.claim: Dahhak, Tawus, and Tabari hold that the bequest verse was not abrogated; it applies to relatives excluded from inheritance, such as parents of another religion or enslaved relatives.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r9.anchor: Dahhâk, Tâvûs, Taberî gibi müctehidlere göre vasiyet âyeti ne kısmen ne de tamamen neshedilmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r10.speaker: Dahhâk, Tâvûs, Taberî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r10.claim: Under this view, the amount bequeathed is left to customary practice and fairness.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r10.anchor: Kime ne kadar vasiyet edileceği ise örfe, âdete ve hakkaniyet kurallarına (mârûf ölçüsüne) bırakılmıştır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r11.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r11.claim: An orphaned grandchild whose father died before the grandfather can be excluded because the living paternal uncle is nearer; Islamic law has no rule making the child inherit in the father’s place.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r11.anchor: Çocuğun ölen babasının yerine konarak (ona halef olarak) vâris olması hükmü İslâm hukukunda yoktur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r12.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r12.claim: Some contemporary Muslim countries used the non-heir bequest reasoning to provide inheritance shares to orphaned grandchildren.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r12.anchor: çağımızda bazı İslâm ülkelerinde, bu ictihaddan yararlanmak suretiyle çözülmüş, yetim torunlar mirastan paya kavuşturulmuştur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r13.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r13.speaker: some müctehidler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r13.claim: Some jurists hold that a bequest to a relative who already inherits is invalid.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r13.anchor: Mirastan payı olan akrabaya (vâris) vasiyet yoluyla da mal bırakılmış olursa bazı müctehidlere göre bu tasarruf geçerli değildir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r14.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r14.speaker: Hanefîler, Hanbelîler ve daha başka bazı müctehidler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r14.claim: Hanafis, Hanbalis, and some others validate a bequest to an heir if the other heirs consent.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r14.anchor: Hanefîler, Hanbelîler ve daha başka bazı müctehidlere göre ise diğer vârisler razı oldukları takdirde bu vasiyet de geçerlidir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r15.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r15.speaker: some müctehidler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r15.claim: Some jurists treat a bequest exceeding one-third as invalid, citing the relevant hadith.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r15.anchor: İlgili hadisi delil gösteren bazı müctehidler üçte biri geçen vasiyeti hükümsüz sayarken

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r16.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r16.speaker: müctehidler çoğunluğu
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r16.claim: Most jurists, including Hanafis, consider an over-one-third bequest valid if the heirs consent.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r16.anchor: Hanefîler’in de dahil bulunduğu çoğunluk, vârislerin razı olmaları halinde bunun da geçerli olduğu hükmünü benimsemişlerdir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r17.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r17.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r17.claim: A bequest is a legal disposition whose execution is left until after death.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r17.anchor: Vasiyet fiilen gerçekleştirilmesi ölüm sonrasına bırakılan bir hukukî tasarruftur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r18.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r18.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r18.claim: It is obligatory to bequeath that debts or outstanding rights be settled from the estate after death.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r18.anchor: Bir kimsenin üzerinde bir hak, bir borç varsa ölümünden sonra bunun terekesinden ödenmesini, yerine getirilmesini vasiyet etmesi farzdır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r19.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r19.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r19.claim: Where no such debt or right exists, bequest is recommended rather than obligatory when circumstances allow; hadiths encouraging bequests are read this way.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:180/r19.anchor: Böyle bir borcun veya sahibine teslim edilmesi gereken bir hakkın bulunmaması halinde vasiyet farz değil menduptur

NAHHAS:v1p281/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p281/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p281/r12.claim: An implied coordinating wāw gives the sense “and it was prescribed for you.”
NAHHAS:v1p281/r12.anchor: في الكلام تقدير واو العطف المعنى وكتب عليكم

NAHHAS:v1p281/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p281/r13.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p281/r13.claim: A similar omitted wāw is understood in «لا يصلاها إلا الأشقى الذي كذب وتولى»: “nor will enter it except the most wretched.”
NAHHAS:v1p281/r13.anchor: ومثله في بعض الأقوال ( لا يصلاها إلا الأشقى الذي كذب وتولى ) أي ولا يصلاها

NAHHAS:v1p281/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p281/r14.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p281/r14.claim: «أحدكم» is the object and «الموت» the subject.

NAHHAS:v1p281/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p281/r15.speaker: الأخفش سعيد
NAHHAS:v1p281/r15.claim: Al-Akhfash supplies «فالوصية» as the apodosis, with the fāʾ omitted; he cites poetry where a conditional is answered without it.
NAHHAS:v1p281/r15.anchor: قال الأخفش سعيد التقدير فالوصية ثم حذف الفاء

NAHHAS:v1p281/r16.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p281/r16.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p281/r16.claim: Alternatively, the past conditional may be answered by a clause before or after it; «الوصية» can then be a subject, or the passive subject of «كتب».
NAHHAS:v1p281/r16.anchor: والجواب الآخر أن الماضي يجوز أن يكون جوابه قبله وبعده فيكون التقدير الوصية للوالدين

NAHHAS:v1p281/r17.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p281/r17.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p281/r17.claim: One reported legal view is that this bequest rule was abrogated by the prescribed inheritance shares.
NAHHAS:v1p281/r17.anchor: وقد ذكرنا في الآية أقوالا منها أن تكون منسوخة بالفرض

NAHHAS:v1p281/r18.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p281/r18.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p281/r18.claim: Another view treats the bequest as recommended; Abū Jaʿfar says recommendation requires evidence and reports abrogation by the hadith “no bequest for an heir.”
NAHHAS:v1p281/r18.anchor: ومنها أن تكون على الندب على الوصية قال أبو جعفر والقول أنه لا يجوز أن يكون شيء من هذا على الندب إلا بدليل

NAHHAS:v1p281/r19.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p281/r19.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p281/r19.claim: Abū Jaʿfar rejects treating the rule as recommended without evidence and notes the report that it is abrogated by “no bequest for an heir.”
NAHHAS:v1p281/r19.anchor: وقد قيل أنها منسوخة بالحديث لا وصية لوارث

NAHHAS:v1p281/r20.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p281/r20.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p281/r20.claim: «حقا» is a verbal noun; outside the Qurʾānic form «حق» may mean “that is true.”
NAHHAS:v1p281/r20.anchor: ( حقا ) مصدر ويجوز في غير القرآن حق بمعنى ذلك حق

BURHAN:v2p30/r12.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p30/r12.speaker: قيل
BURHAN:v2p30/r12.claim: Some say the inheritance verses abrogated the earlier command to bequeath to parents and relatives, since one cannot both inherit and receive a bequest.
BURHAN:v2p30/r12.anchor: فقيل الآيتان إذا أوجبتا حكمين مختلفين وكانت إحداهما متقدمة الأخرى فالمتأخرة ناسخة للأولى

BURHAN:v2p30/r13.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p30/r13.speaker: قيل
BURHAN:v2p30/r13.claim: Others say the verses are compatible and the bequest ruling was abrogated for heirs by the Prophetic report, “No bequest to an heir.”
BURHAN:v2p30/r13.anchor: وقيل بل ذلك جائز وليس فيهما ناسخ ولا منسوخ

BURHAN:v2p32/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p32/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p32/r5.claim: The author answers that the bequest verse was abrogated by Qurʾan, not by the report Ibn ʿAtiyya cites.
BURHAN:v2p32/r5.anchor: قلنا أما آية الوصية فقد ذكرنا أن ناسخها القرآن

BURHAN:v2p499/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p499/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p499/r1.claim: For the conditional construction under discussion, the answer is the two clauses together; it does not exist before the condition, even if one clause alone does.
BURHAN:v2p499/r1.anchor: إن الجواب ليس كلا من الجملتين بل مجموع المجموع الجملتين ومعدوم قبل وجود الشرط

BURHAN:v2p372/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p372/r3.speaker: الأخفش
BURHAN:v2p372/r3.claim: Al-Akhfash reads an implicit fa before “the bequest,” making 2:180 an instance of a condition interposed on another condition.

BURHAN:v2p372/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p372/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p372/r4.claim: If “the bequest” is nominative as the subject of “was prescribed,” the construction instead resembles earlier cases with two omitted answers.
BURHAN:v2p372/r4.anchor: فهي كالآيات السابقة في حذف الجوابين

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p285/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p285/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p285/r1.claim: Khayr names anything praised and desired.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p285/r1.anchor: الخير : اسم لكل ممدوح ومرغوب فيه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p285/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p285/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p285/r2.anchor: والخير : الكرم . والاستخارة أن تسأل الله تعالى

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p285/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p285/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p285/r3.claim: Istikhāra is asking God to guide one to the better of two choices.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p285/r3.anchor: والاستخارة أن تسأل الله تعالى ] خير الأمرين

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p285/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p285/r7.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p285/r7.claim: Khayr means property in the inheritance and spending verses.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p285/r7.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الخير في القرآن على اثنين وعشرين وجها : -

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p285/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p285/r8.speaker: قالوا
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p285/r8.claim: An unnamed gloss identifies the khayr left behind as religion.

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p514/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p514/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p514/r1.claim: The root of kitāba is gathering; a writer is like one who gathers letters.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p514/r1.anchor: الأصل في الكتب : الجمع . فكأن الكاتب هو جامع الحروف

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p514/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p514/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p514/r2.claim: The verb for fastening a she-mule’s thighs with a ring illustrates gathering; kitba and katb refer to stitching.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p514/r2.anchor: يقال : كتبت البغلة ، إذا جمعت بين شفريها بحلقة . والكتبة : الخرزة . والكتب : الخرز

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p514/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p514/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p514/r3.claim: A mukātaba is an emancipation contract: a slave pays the agreed amount and is then freed.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p514/r3.anchor: والمكاتب : العبد يكاتب على نفسه بشيء يؤديه ، فإذا أداه عتق

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p514/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p514/r7.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p514/r7.claim: Kataba can mean prescribing an obligation, including fasting, retaliation, wills, and fighting.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p514/r7.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الكتب في القرآن على خمسة أوجه : -

BURHAN:v3p211/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p211/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p211/r5.claim: On one grammatical view, the conditional reply in إن ترك خيرا الوصية has an elided فاء: فالوصية.
BURHAN:v3p211/r5.anchor: ومنه الفاء في جواب الشرط على رأى وخرج عليه قوله تعالى ﴿ إن ترك خيرا الوصية ﴾ 4 أي فالوصية

BURHAN:v2p293/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p293/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p293/r4.claim: The wording about death’s arrival means when death is near, not after death has already occurred.
BURHAN:v2p293/r4.anchor: وقوله تعالى ﴿ كتب عليكم إذا حضر أحدكم الموت ﴾ أي قارب حضور الموت

ITQAN:v3p44/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p44/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p44/r1.claim: A general text may be restricted by a condition, as in the examples of emancipation contracts and bequests.
ITQAN:v3p44/r1.anchor: الثالث الشرط نحو ﴿ والذين يبتغون الكتاب مما ملكت أيمانكم فكاتبوهم إن علمتم فيهم خيرا ﴾ ﴿ كتب عليكم إذا حضر أحدكم الموت إن ترك خيرا الوصية ﴾

ITQAN:v3p59/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p59/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p59/r2.claim: The deathbed bequest verse is said to be abrogated by inheritance verses, by the hadith that there is no bequest for an heir, or by consensus as Ibn al-Arabi reports.
ITQAN:v3p59/r2.anchor: قوله تعالى ﴿ كتب عليكم إذا حضر أحدكم الموت ﴾ الآية منسوخة قيل بأية المواريث وقيل بحديث

ITQAN:v3p94#2/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p94#2/r5.speaker: بعض الأقدمين
ITQAN:v3p94#2/r5.claim: The will passage is an example of precedence and postponement: its intended order is that the will is prescribed when death approaches, if one leaves property.
ITQAN:v3p94#2/r5.anchor: والتقديم والتأخير مثل ﴿ كتب عليكم إذا حضر أحدكم الموت إن ترك خيرا الوصية ﴾ التقدير كتب عليكم الوصية إذا حضر أحدكم الموت

DAMGHANI:v1p166/r8.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p166/r8.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p166/r8.claim: Khayr can mean wealth, as in the bequest verse and several commands to spend one's good or property.
DAMGHANI:v1p166/r8.anchor: الخير بمعنى المال قوله سبحانه في سورة البقرة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p587/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p587/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p587/r1.claim: In the cited inheritance verse, الوصية is the نائب فاعل.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p614/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p614/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p614/r2.claim: حضر الموت occurs in legal and testamentary contexts, where death is present like a witness; these passages concern rulings and wills rather than the experience of dying.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p614/r2.anchor: حضور الموت يُستعمل في القرآن الكريم في الأحكام والوصايا كما في آية سورة البقرة وكأن الموت هو من جملة الشهود

JISHUMI:v1p746/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p746/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p746/r1.claim: كتب عليكم means that making a will was prescribed.
JISHUMI:v1p746/r1.anchor: قال تعالى: (كتب عليكم) يعني فرض عليكم

JISHUMI:v1p746/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p746/r2.speaker: أكثر أهل العلم
JISHUMI:v1p746/r2.claim: Most scholars take death’s arrival to mean its causes, such as illness.
JISHUMI:v1p746/r2.anchor: يعني أسباب الموت من مرض ونحوه، عن أكثر أهل العلم

JISHUMI:v1p746/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p746/r3.speaker: الأصم
JISHUMI:v1p746/r3.claim: Al-Asamm instead says the will is prescribed in health, as an instruction about what should be done when death comes.
JISHUMI:v1p746/r3.anchor: وقيل: فرض عليكم الوصية في حال الصحة أن تقولوا: إذا حضرنا الموت فافعلوا كذا، عن الأصم

JISHUMI:v1p746/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p746/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p746/r4.anchor: أي مالا، واختلفوا، فقيل: يجب في القليل والكثير

JISHUMI:v1p746/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p746/r5.speaker: الزهري
JISHUMI:v1p746/r5.claim: Al-Zuhri says a will is required whether the estate is small or large.
JISHUMI:v1p746/r5.anchor: فقيل: يجب في القليل والكثير، عن الزهري

JISHUMI:v1p746/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p746/r6.speaker: أكثر أهل العلم
JISHUMI:v1p746/r6.claim: Most scholars require a minimum amount of wealth before the testamentary duty applies.
JISHUMI:v1p746/r6.anchor: وقال غيره: لا بد من مقدار، وهو قول أكثر أهل العلم

JISHUMI:v1p746/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p746/r7.speaker: القاضي
JISHUMI:v1p746/r7.claim: Al-Qadi says a minimum is agreed apart from views without a recognized threshold: someone who leaves one dirham is not ordinarily said to have left wealth.
JISHUMI:v1p746/r7.anchor: اتفقوا على إثبات قدر منه إلا من لا يعتد بقدره؛ لأنه لا يقال لمن ترك درهما

JISHUMI:v1p746/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p746/r8.speaker: قتادة والنخعي وابن عباس وعلي وعائشة
JISHUMI:v1p746/r8.claim: Reported thresholds vary: Qatada gives one thousand dirhams, al-Nakhaʿi five hundred to one thousand, Ibn Abbas eight hundred, Ali four thousand, and Aisha says four hundred dinars is little; Ali also said an estate of nine hundred did not warrant a will.
JISHUMI:v1p746/r8.anchor: فقيل: ألف درهم، عن قتادة، وقيل: من ألف إلى خمسمائة، عن النخعي، وقيل: ثمانمائة درهم، عن ابن عباس

JISHUMI:v1p746/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p746/r9.speaker: القاضي
JISHUMI:v1p746/r9.claim: Al-Qadi prefers measuring the threshold by each person’s circumstances, since the wealth that makes one person rich may not suffice for another with greater dependents and expenses.
JISHUMI:v1p746/r9.anchor: وقال القاضي، وهو الأصح؛ لأنه بمقدار من المال يوصف المرء أنه غني، وبذلك القدر لا يوصف غيره

JISHUMI:v1p746/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p746/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p746/r10.claim: The prescribed will is for parents and nearest relatives in order of closeness; معروف may describe the proper amount of the bequest or the proper beneficiaries.
JISHUMI:v1p746/r10.anchor: الوصية هي التي فرض وكتبت للوالدين للأب وللأم، والأقربين قرابة الميت الأقرب فالأقرب

JISHUMI:v1p746/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p746/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p746/r11.claim: Known propriety in amount means that someone with great wealth should not bequeath only a dirham; in beneficiaries it means not favoring a rich relative over a poor one or treating a cousin as equal to a parent. The author applies both.
JISHUMI:v1p746/r11.anchor: ليس من المعروف أن يوصي للغني ويترك الفقير، وأن يسوي بين بني العم والوالدين، فالواجب حمله عليهما

JISHUMI:v1p746/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p746/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p746/r12.claim: The phrase reinforces that the will is an obligatory right owed by those who choose piety.
